The 2024 NFL draft was the 89th annual meeting of National Football League (NFL) franchises to select newly eligible players. The draft was held at Campus Martius Park and Hart Plaza in Detroit on April 25–27, 2024.[1] The draft had a then-record attendance of over 775,000, which was later surpassed in 2026.[2][3]

Six quarterbacks were selected in the first round—Caleb Williams, Jayden Daniels, Drake Maye, Michael Penix Jr., J. J. McCarthy, and Bo Nix—tying the record from 1983. The six were within the first 12 picks, with five in the top 10. Conversely, for the first time since the 1970 AFL–NFL merger, no quarterbacks were selected in the second through fourth rounds.[4] Seven wide receivers were also selected in the first round, tying the record from 2004.[5] A record 23 offensive players were selected in the first round, with 14 consecutive offensive players to start the draft.[4][6][7]

Host cityedit

Detroit was chosen over Green Bay and Washington, D.C. as the host city on March 28, 2022.[8] The city prepared to host the draft by undertaking beautification efforts, including construction work in various parts of the city and organizing a series of pop-ups to fill vacant storefronts downtown in time for the draft's visitors.[9][10]

The city installed the Detroit Sign, inspired by the Hollywood Sign in Los Angeles, to welcome visitors entering the city along Interstate 94.[11][12] City officials claimed to have spent $230,000 of state grant money and municipal funds on murals. Additionally $1.53 million was said to have been spent on improvements to streets and traffic lights, as well as the planting of trees and beautification of roadway medians.[13] The hosting of the draft was regarded to have been a success, with the city experiencing an estimated economic impact of $160 million.[13][14]

As part of an effort to beautify the city, the city's Planning and Development Department, Downtown Detroit Partnership, and the City Office of Arts, Culture and Entrepreneurship partnered with Street Art for Mankind (SAM)'s "Be The Change" campaign to create seven sizable murals. The murals, however, became a subject of controversy. Criticism arose that international artists involved in the paintings may have been compensated below market rate for their work.[15] The artworks became more controversial after the City Council refused to approve payment for the works, arguing that they had been approved without following the approval process imposed by the city charter. City employees' emails were later released under the Freedom of Information Act and revealed that department officials had considered the painting of buildings with historic designation without the required approval of the Historic District Commission.[16]

Trades involving draft picksedit

(PD) indicates trades completed prior to the start of the draft (i.e. Pre-Draft), while (D) denotes trades which took place during the 2024 draft.

Round 1edit
 No. 1: Carolina → Chicago (PD). Carolina traded a first-round selection (1st overall), 2023 first- and second-round selections (9th and 61st overall), a 2025 second-round selection and WR D. J. Moore to Chicago in exchange for a 2023 first-round selection (1st overall).[Trade 1]
 No. 10: NY Jets → Minnesota (D). NY Jets traded first- and sixth-round selections (10th and 203rd overall) to Minnesota in exchange for first-, fourth- and fifth-round selections (11th, 129th and 157th overall).[Trade 2]
 No. 11: Minnesota → NY Jets (D). See Round 1: NY Jets → Minnesota.[Trade 2]
 No. 17: Jacksonville → Minnesota (D). Jacksonville traded a first-round selection (17th overall) to Minnesota in exchange for first- and fifth-round selections (23rd and 167th overall) and 2025 third and fourth-round selections.[Trade 3]
 No. 23: Cleveland → Houston → Minnesota → Jacksonville. Multiple trades:
       Cleveland → Houston (PD). Cleveland traded first- and fourth-round selections, 2022 first- and fourth-round selections (13th and 107th overall), and 2023 first- and third-round selections (12th and 73rd overall) to Houston in exchange for a sixth-round selection (203rd overall) and QB Deshaun Watson.[Trade 4]
        Houston → Minnesota (PD). Houston traded first- and seventh-round selections (23rd and 232nd overall) to Minnesota in exchange for second- and sixth-round selections (42nd and 188th overall) as well as a 2025 second-round selection.[Trade 5]
       Minnesota → Jacksonville (D). See Round 1: Jacksonville → Minnesota.[Trade 3]
 No. 24: Dallas → Detroit (D). Dallas traded a first-round selection (24th overall) and a 2025 seventh-round selection to Detroit in exchange for first- and third-round selections (29th and 73rd overall).[Trade 6]
 No. 27: Houston → Arizona (PD). Houston traded first- and third-round selections (27th and 90th overall), and 2023 first- and second-round selections (12th and 33rd overall) to Arizona in exchange for 2023 first- and fourth-round selections (3rd and 105th overall).[Trade 7]
 No. 28: Buffalo → Kansas City (D). Buffalo traded first-, fourth- and seventh-round selections (28th, 133rd and 248th overall) to Kansas City in exchange for first-, third- and seventh-round selections (32nd, 95th and 221st overall).[Trade 8]
 No. 29: Detroit → Dallas (D). See Round 1: Dallas → Detroit.[Trade 6]
 No. 32: Kansas City → Buffalo → Carolina. Multiple trades:
       Kansas City → Buffalo (D). See Round 1: Buffalo → Kansas City.[Trade 8]

Forfeited and penalized picksedit
 Miami forfeited a third-round selection as well as a 2023 first-round selection for violating the anti-tampering policy in conversations with QB Tom Brady and the agent for then-New Orleans Saints' coach Sean Payton.[17]
 San Francisco had a fourth-round selection (131st overall) moved to the end of the round (135th overall) as punishment for administrative payroll accounting errors.[20]
Resolution JC-2A picksedit

Resolution JC-2A, enacted by the NFL in November 2020, rewards teams for developing minority candidates for head coach and/or general manager positions by awarding draft picks.[22] These draft picks are at the end of the third round, after standard compensatory picks; if multiple teams qualify, they are awarded by draft order in the first round. These picks are in addition to, and have no impact on, the standard 32 compensatory picks.[23] Two picks were awarded for the 2024 draft pursuant to the resolution.

 The LA Rams received a third-round selection (99th overall) and a 2025 third-round selection as compensation for Atlanta hiring defensive coordinator Raheem Morris as head coach.[18]
 San Francisco received a third-round selection (100th overall) and a 2023 third-round selection as compensation for Tennessee hiring director of player personnel Ran Carthon as general manager.[19]

The 2024 NFL draft was the 89th annual meeting of National Football League (NFL) franchises to select newly eligible players. The draft was held at Campus Martius Park and Hart Plaza in Detroit on April 25–27, 2024.[1] The draft had a then-record attendance of over 775,000, which was later surpassed in 2026.[2][3]

Six quarterbacks were selected in the first round—Caleb Williams, Jayden Daniels, Drake Maye, Michael Penix Jr., J. J. McCarthy, and Bo Nix—tying the record from 1983. The six were within the first 12 picks, with five in the top 10. Conversely, for the first time since the 1970 AFL–NFL merger, no quarterbacks were selected in the second through fourth rounds.[4] Seven wide receivers were also selected in the first round, tying the record from 2004.[5] A record 23 offensive players were selected in the first round, with 14 consecutive offensive players to start the draft.[4][6][7]

Host cityedit

Detroit was chosen over Green Bay and Washington, D.C. as the host city on March 28, 2022.[8] The city prepared to host the draft by undertaking beautification efforts, including construction work in various parts of the city and organizing a series of pop-ups to fill vacant storefronts downtown in time for the draft's visitors.[9][10]

The city installed the Detroit Sign, inspired by the Hollywood Sign in Los Angeles, to welcome visitors entering the city along Interstate 94.[11][12] City officials claimed to have spent $230,000 of state grant money and municipal funds on murals. Additionally $1.53 million was said to have been spent on improvements to streets and traffic lights, as well as the planting of trees and beautification of roadway medians.[13] The hosting of the draft was regarded to have been a success, with the city experiencing an estimated economic impact of $160 million.[13][14]

As part of an effort to beautify the city, the city's Planning and Development Department, Downtown Detroit Partnership, and the City Office of Arts, Culture and Entrepreneurship partnered with Street Art for Mankind (SAM)'s "Be The Change" campaign to create seven sizable murals. The murals, however, became a subject of controversy. Criticism arose that international artists involved in the paintings may have been compensated below market rate for their work.[15] The artworks became more controversial after the City Council refused to approve payment for the works, arguing that they had been approved without following the approval process imposed by the city charter. City employees' emails were later released under the Freedom of Information Act and revealed that department officials had considered the painting of buildings with historic designation without the required approval of the Historic District Commission.[16]

Forfeited and penalized picksedit
 Miami forfeited a third-round selection as well as a 2023 first-round selection for violating the anti-tampering policy in conversations with QB Tom Brady and the agent for then-New Orleans Saints' coach Sean Payton.[17]
 San Francisco had a fourth-round selection (131st overall) moved to the end of the round (135th overall) as punishment for administrative payroll accounting errors.[20]
Resolution JC-2A picksedit

Resolution JC-2A, enacted by the NFL in November 2020, rewards teams for developing minority candidates for head coach and/or general manager positions by awarding draft picks.[22] These draft picks are at the end of the third round, after standard compensatory picks; if multiple teams qualify, they are awarded by draft order in the first round. These picks are in addition to, and have no impact on, the standard 32 compensatory picks.[23] Two picks were awarded for the 2024 draft pursuant to the resolution.

 The LA Rams received a third-round selection (99th overall) and a 2025 third-round selection as compensation for Atlanta hiring defensive coordinator Raheem Morris as head coach.[18]
 San Francisco received a third-round selection (100th overall) and a 2023 third-round selection as compensation for Tennessee hiring director of player personnel Ran Carthon as general manager.[19]

The **2021 NFL draft** was the 86th [National Football League draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League_draft "National Football League draft"), the annual meeting of [National Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League") (NFL) franchises to select newly eligible players for the [2021 NFL season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_NFL_season "2021 NFL season"). The draft was held in [Cleveland, Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland "Cleveland") from April 29 to May 1, 2021.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_NFL_draft#cite_note-1)

Five quarterbacks were selected in the first round—[Trevor Lawrence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence "Trevor Lawrence"), [Zach Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson "Zach Wilson"), [Trey Lance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trey_Lance "Trey Lance"), [Justin Fields](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields "Justin Fields"), and [Mac Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mac_Jones "Mac Jones")—the second highest amount (along with the [1999](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_NFL_draft "1999 NFL draft") and [2018](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_NFL_draft "2018 NFL draft") drafts) after the six selected in [1983](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1983_NFL_draft "1983 NFL draft") and 2024. The draft also marked the third time the first three picks were quarterbacks, following the [1971](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1971_NFL_draft "1971 NFL draft") and 1999 drafts. A total of eight quarterbacks were selected in the first three rounds, the most in NFL draft history, although only two quarterbacks were taken in the remaining rounds. By 2024, Lawrence was the only first-round quarterback to remain with his original team.

In addition to the high number of quarterbacks, six [Alabama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alabama_Crimson_Tide_football "Alabama Crimson Tide football") players were taken in the first round, which is tied with the six [Miami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_Hurricanes_football "Miami Hurricanes football") players picked in [2004](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_NFL_draft "2004 NFL draft") for the most from an individual school. Conversely, no [Big 12 Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_12_Conference "Big 12 Conference") players were drafted in the first round for the first time since the conference began play in 1996 and no [Michigan State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michigan_State_Spartans_football "Michigan State Spartans football") players were selected for the first time since 1941.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_NFL_draft#cite_note-2)

Scouts considered the later rounds of the draft to lack desirable prospects due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic") shortening the 2020 college football season. The [NCAA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NCAA "NCAA") granted an extra year of eligibility and an opt-out option for athletes because of the shortened season, resulting in many prospects returning to school instead of declaring for the draft.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_NFL_draft#cite_note-3)

The host city was chosen during the NFL Spring League Meeting on May 22, 2019.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_NFL_draft#cite_note-4) Cleveland and [Kansas City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City,_Missouri "Kansas City, Missouri") were announced as the hosts for 2021 and [2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_NFL_draft "2023 NFL draft"), respectively, from the remaining finalists from the 2019 draft after [Las Vegas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas "Las Vegas") was chosen to host the 2022 event.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_NFL_draft#cite_note-5)

The **2021 NFL draft** was the 86th [National Football League draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League_draft "National Football League draft"), the annual meeting of [National Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League") (NFL) franchises to select newly eligible players for the [2021 NFL season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_NFL_season "2021 NFL season"). The draft was held in [Cleveland, Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland "Cleveland") from April 29 to May 1, 2021.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_NFL_draft#cite_note-1)

Five quarterbacks were selected in the first round—[Trevor Lawrence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence "Trevor Lawrence"), [Zach Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson "Zach Wilson"), [Trey Lance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trey_Lance "Trey Lance"), [Justin Fields](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields "Justin Fields"), and [Mac Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mac_Jones "Mac Jones")—the second highest amount (along with the [1999](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_NFL_draft "1999 NFL draft") and [2018](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_NFL_draft "2018 NFL draft") drafts) after the six selected in [1983](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1983_NFL_draft "1983 NFL draft") and 2024. The draft also marked the third time the first three picks were quarterbacks, following the [1971](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1971_NFL_draft "1971 NFL draft") and 1999 drafts. A total of eight quarterbacks were selected in the first three rounds, the most in NFL draft history, although only two quarterbacks were taken in the remaining rounds. By 2024, Lawrence was the only first-round quarterback to remain with his original team.

In addition to the high number of quarterbacks, six [Alabama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alabama_Crimson_Tide_football "Alabama Crimson Tide football") players were taken in the first round, which is tied with the six [Miami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_Hurricanes_football "Miami Hurricanes football") players picked in [2004](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_NFL_draft "2004 NFL draft") for the most from an individual school. Conversely, no [Big 12 Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_12_Conference "Big 12 Conference") players were drafted in the first round for the first time since the conference began play in 1996 and no [Michigan State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michigan_State_Spartans_football "Michigan State Spartans football") players were selected for the first time since 1941.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_NFL_draft#cite_note-2)

Scouts considered the later rounds of the draft to lack desirable prospects due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic") shortening the 2020 college football season. The [NCAA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NCAA "NCAA") granted an extra year of eligibility and an opt-out option for athletes because of the shortened season, resulting in many prospects returning to school instead of declaring for the draft.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_NFL_draft#cite_note-3)

The host city was chosen during the NFL Spring League Meeting on May 22, 2019.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_NFL_draft#cite_note-4) Cleveland and [Kansas City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City,_Missouri "Kansas City, Missouri") were announced as the hosts for 2021 and [2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_NFL_draft "2023 NFL draft"), respectively, from the remaining finalists from the 2019 draft after [Las Vegas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas "Las Vegas") was chosen to host the 2022 event.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_NFL_draft#cite_note-5)

**William Trevor Lawrence** (born October 6, 1999) is an American professional [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_football "American football")[quarterback](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quarterback "Quarterback") for the [Jacksonville Jaguars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacksonville_Jaguars "Jacksonville Jaguars") of the [National Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League") (NFL). Considered among the highest-touted [college football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_football "College football") prospects, he won the [2019 National Championship Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_College_Football_Playoff_National_Championship "2019 College Football Playoff National Championship") as a freshman with the [Clemson Tigers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clemson_Tigers_football "Clemson Tigers football") and set the school's record for quarterback wins. Lawrence was selected [first overall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_first_overall_NFL_draft_picks "List of first overall NFL draft picks") by the Jaguars in the 2021 NFL draft. In his second season, Lawrence led the Jaguars to their first division title since 2017 and earned [Pro Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pro_Bowl "Pro Bowl") honors. He led the team to another division title in 2025.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Trevor_Lawrence&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/71/Trevor_Lawrence_%28American_football%29_Sept_2017.jpg/250px-Trevor_Lawrence_%28American_football%29_Sept_2017.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Trevor_Lawrence_(American_football)_Sept_2017.jpg)

Lawrence at [Cartersville High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cartersville_High_School "Cartersville High School") in 2017

William Trevor Lawrence was born in [Knoxville, Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knoxville,_Tennessee "Knoxville, Tennessee") on October 6, 1999 and moved to [Cartersville, Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cartersville,_Georgia "Cartersville, Georgia") when he was six.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-jcp-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-3) He later attended [Cartersville High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cartersville_High_School "Cartersville High School"), where he played football and basketball. As a junior in 2016, Lawrence was _[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Atlanta\_Journal-Constitution "The Atlanta Journal-Constitution")_ player of the year after completing 250 of 406 passes for 3,904 yards and 51 [touchdowns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Touchdowns "Touchdowns").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-4) As a sophomore, he passed for 3,655 yards and 43 touchdowns and as a freshman, Lawrence had 3,042 yards and 26 touchdowns.

From his sophomore year to his senior year, Lawrence led the Purple Hurricanes to 41 straight victories, winning two state championships and four region titles while also receiving numerous national high school player of the year honors. In 2017, Lawrence broke the [Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_(U.S._state) "Georgia (U.S. state)") state record for passing yards and passing [touchdowns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Touchdown "Touchdown"), which were previously held by [Deshaun Watson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deshaun_Watson "Deshaun Watson") of Gainesville, who also played for [Clemson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clemson_Tigers_football_team "Clemson Tigers football team").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-6)

Lawrence was a five-star recruit who was regarded as one of the best high school quarterback prospects of all time.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-10) On December 16, 2016, he committed to [Clemson University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clemson_University "Clemson University") to play college football.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-12)

## College career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Trevor_Lawrence&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: College career")]

### Freshman year

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Trevor_Lawrence&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Freshman year")]

See also: [2018 Clemson Tigers football team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Clemson_Tigers_football_team "2018 Clemson Tigers football team")

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5a/2019_CFP_-_Clemson_offense.JPG/250px-2019_CFP_-_Clemson_offense.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2019_CFP_-_Clemson_offense.JPG)

Lawrence (#16) during the [2019 College Football Playoff National Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_College_Football_Playoff_National_Championship "2019 College Football Playoff National Championship")

Lawrence started his freshman season behind [Kelly Bryant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kelly_Bryant_(American_football) "Kelly Bryant (American football)") on Clemson's depth chart, but was given equal playing time in the season's first games. Head coach [Dabo Swinney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dabo_Swinney "Dabo Swinney") named Lawrence the new starter after four games, after which Bryant announced his intention to transfer schools.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-13) Lawrence led [Clemson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Clemson_Tigers_football_team "2018 Clemson Tigers football team") to an undefeated regular season, a 42–10 victory over [Pittsburgh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Pittsburgh_Panthers_football_team "2018 Pittsburgh Panthers football team") in the [ACC Championship Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_ACC_Championship_Game "2018 ACC Championship Game"), and a bid to play in the [College Football Playoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_Football_Playoff "College Football Playoff"). The Tigers were ranked No. 2 in the College Football Playoff rankings, and defeated No. 3 [Notre Dame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Notre_Dame_Fighting_Irish_football_team "2018 Notre Dame Fighting Irish football team"), 30–3, in the [2018 Cotton Bowl Classic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Cotton_Bowl_Classic "2018 Cotton Bowl Classic").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-14) They advanced to the [2019 College Football Playoff National Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_College_Football_Playoff_National_Championship "2019 College Football Playoff National Championship") game, where they defeated [Alabama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Alabama_Crimson_Tide_football_team "2018 Alabama Crimson Tide football team"), 44–16, handing the Crimson Tide their worst loss of the [Nick Saban](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Saban "Nick Saban") era.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-15) Lawrence was named Offensive MVP of the game and became the first [true freshman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/True_freshman "True freshman") quarterback to start for a national champion since [Jamelle Holieway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamelle_Holieway "Jamelle Holieway") in [1985](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985_NCAA_Division_I-A_football_season "1985 NCAA Division I-A football season") for [Oklahoma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985_Oklahoma_Sooners_football_team "1985 Oklahoma Sooners football team").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-16)

Lawrence threw for 3,280 passing yards and 30 touchdowns on the season, and was awarded the National Freshman of the Year and [Archie Griffin Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Touchdown_Club_of_Columbus#Archie_Griffin_Award "Touchdown Club of Columbus") by the [Touchdown Club of Columbus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Touchdown_Club_of_Columbus "Touchdown Club of Columbus").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-17) He was also awarded ACC Rookie of the Year honors.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-18)

all but lost Lawrence the Heisman Trophy race, but he led FBS in [passer rating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passer_rating "Passer rating") over the final half of the regular season and ended seventh in Heisman Trophy voting.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-21) Lawrence helped lead Clemson to an rankings.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-23) In the [2019 Fiesta Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Fiesta_Bowl_(December) "2019 Fiesta Bowl (December)") against [Ohio State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Ohio_State_Buckeyes_football_team "2019 Ohio State Buckeyes football team"), he had 259 passing yards and two touchdowns to go along with 16 rushes for 107 yards and a touchdown in the 29–23 victory that brought them to the national championship game for the second consecutive year.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-24) Lawrence lost the first game of his career in the [CFP Championship Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_College_Football_Playoff_National_Championship "2020 College Football Playoff National Championship") against [LSU](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_LSU_Tigers_football_team "2019 LSU Tigers football team"), as Clemson snapped its 29-game winning streak and lost 42–25. Lawrence posted the worst passer rating of his career as he only completed 18 of 37 passes for 234 yards in the game.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-26)

Lawrence returned for his junior season with the Tigers. In his first six games of the season, Lawrence threw for 1,833 passing yards with 17 touchdowns and two interceptions. On October 30, 2020, Lawrence tested positive for [COVID-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19 "COVID-19"), which resulted in a 10-day quarantine, per [ACC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Coast_Conference "Atlantic Coast Conference") protocols. As a result, he missed two games before returning.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-Cobb-27) Clemson lost one of those two games, to [Notre Dame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Notre_Dame_Fighting_Irish_football_team "2020 Notre Dame Fighting Irish football team").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-28) After Lawrence returned to the team, he helped guide the Tigers back to the ACC Championship Game by finishing in second in the division-less format adopted for the 2020 season. They defeated Notre Dame in the rematch in the conference title game with Lawrence starting at quarterback and were selected to a spot in the College Football Playoff.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-29) In the CFP semifinal, the [Sugar Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Sugar_Bowl "2021 Sugar Bowl"), Lawrence and the Tigers lost to [Ohio State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Ohio_State_Buckeyes_football_team "2020 Ohio State Buckeyes football team").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-30)

Lawrence finished his final season with the Tigers 231-of-334 for 3,153 passing yards with 24 touchdowns and five interceptions.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-31) He was named ACC Player of the Year, and finished in second in voting for the Heisman Trophy behind Alabama wide receiver [DeVonta Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeVonta_Smith "DeVonta Smith").[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-32) After the season, Lawrence would be the men's recipient of the [ACC Athlete of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACC_Athlete_of_the_Year "ACC Athlete of the Year") award across all conference sports, sharing honors with women's recipient Charlotte North of [Boston College lacrosse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_College_Eagles_women's_lacrosse "Boston College Eagles women's lacrosse").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-33)

One of the NFL's highest-regarded amateur prospects, Lawrence was nearly unanimously projected to be taken [first overall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_first_overall_National_Football_League_draft_picks "List of first overall National Football League draft picks") in the 2021 NFL draft.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-CatchLawrence-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-DraftOdds-38) He drew comparisons to [Pro Football Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pro_Football_Hall_of_Fame "Pro Football Hall of Fame") quarterbacks [John Elway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Elway "John Elway") and [Peyton Manning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peyton_Manning "Peyton Manning") and 2012 first overall pick [Andrew Luck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Luck "Andrew Luck"),[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-Pollack-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-Rank-40) with the slogan "[Tank for Trevor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanking_(sports)#Encouragement_by_fans "Tanking (sports)")" gaining popularity among fans of struggling teams.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-Tank-41)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-LawrenceResponse-42)_[ESPN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ESPN "ESPN")_'s[Mel Kiper Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mel_Kiper_Jr. "Mel Kiper Jr.") ranked Lawrence as the fourth highest-graded quarterback he had ever evaluated, behind Elway, Luck, and Manning.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-Kiper-43)

### 2021

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Trevor_Lawrence&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: 2021")]

See also: [2021 Jacksonville Jaguars season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Jacksonville_Jaguars_season "2021 Jacksonville Jaguars season")

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/01/Trevor_Lawrence_TEN_video.png/250px-Trevor_Lawrence_TEN_video.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Trevor_Lawrence_TEN_video.png)

Lawrence in 2021

After undergoing surgery to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder, Lawrence was officially selected first overall by the [Jacksonville Jaguars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacksonville_Jaguars "Jacksonville Jaguars"), which had finished with a league-worst 1–15 record the previous season.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-44)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-45)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-46) On July 5, 2021, he signed his four-year rookie contract, worth $36.8 million with a $24.1 million signing bonus.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-47)

Ahead of the final week of preseason, Lawrence was named the Jaguars' starting quarterback for 2021.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-48)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-49) Making his NFL debut in the season-opener against the [Houston Texans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_Texans "Houston Texans"), Lawrence finished with 332 passing yards, three touchdowns, and three interceptions in the 37–21 road loss. The loss was Lawrence's first in a regular season game.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-50) In the next game against the [Denver Broncos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver_Broncos "Denver Broncos"), he threw a touchdown pass on the opening drive, but completed only eight of 25 passes afterwards and was intercepted twice as the Jaguars lost 23–13.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-OpeningTD-51) Two weeks later against the [Cincinnati Bengals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cincinnati_Bengals "Cincinnati Bengals") on _[Thursday Night Football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thursday\_Night\_Football "Thursday Night Football")_, Lawrence had a stronger performance, completing 17 of 24 passes for 204 yards and scored his first rushing touchdown, also making it his first NFL game without an interception. Despite his efforts, the Jaguars lost on the road 24–21.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-BurrowSpoils-52)

Lawrence won his first NFL game in Week 6 against the [Miami Dolphins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_Dolphins "Miami Dolphins"), throwing for 319 yards and a touchdown during the 23–20 victory. Having played the game at [Tottenham Hotspur Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tottenham_Hotspur_Stadium "Tottenham Hotspur Stadium"), Lawrence became the first NFL rookie to win in London. The victory was also the Jaguars' first since Week 1 of the 2020 season, ending a 20-game losing streak.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-EndStreak-53)

Following a Week 8 31–7 road loss to the [Seattle Seahawks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seattle_Seahawks "Seattle Seahawks"), Lawrence took part in the season's biggest upset when he helped the 15.5-point underdog Jaguars defeat the [Buffalo Bills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buffalo_Bills "Buffalo Bills") 9–6.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-SeventhLargest-54) However, the victory began a stretch that saw Lawrence throw only two touchdown passes in nine games, including seven games without any touchdowns, while having eight interceptions.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-FightingOpponents-55) The Jaguars also went on an eight-game losing streak, dropping them to the league's worst record for a second consecutive year. Nevertheless, Lawrence concluded the season with his strongest performance in the regular season finale, completing 23 of 32 passes for 223 yards and two touchdowns to secure a 26–11 victory over the [Indianapolis Colts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indianapolis_Colts "Indianapolis Colts").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-ShockingWin-56)

Lawrence finished his rookie year with 3,641 passing yards, 12 touchdowns, and a league-leading 17 interceptions to go along with 73 carries for 334 yards and two touchdowns. Lawrence's passing yards ranked second for rookies, only behind [Mac Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mac_Jones "Mac Jones").[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-NFL2021-57)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-58)

### 2022

Lawrence in 2022

After losing to the [Washington Commanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Commanders "Washington Commanders") in the season opener, Lawrence won his next two games against the Colts and [Los Angeles Chargers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Chargers "Los Angeles Chargers"), throwing for a combined 497 yards and five touchdowns.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-TakeLeap-59)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-TheStar-60) The latter also marked Lawrence's first road victory and earned him AFC Offensive Player of the Week honors.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-WorthIt-61)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-62) However, the Jaguars went on a five-game losing streak, during which Lawrence completed 57.8% of his passes for 1,068 yards, five touchdowns, and five interceptions.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-ToughToTake-63) He also had two games without any touchdown passes.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-Texans13Jaguars6-64)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-Giants23Jaguars17-65) The losing streak ended with a Week 9 victory over the [Las Vegas Raiders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas_Raiders "Las Vegas Raiders"), which saw Lawrence help Jacksonville overcome a 20–10 halftime deficit to win 27–20.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-TheComeback-66)

The Week 9 victory kicked off the Jaguars winning seven of their last nine games, with Lawrence throwing for 2,273 yards, 15 touchdowns, and two interceptions. During this period, he led a game-winning drive against the [Baltimore Ravens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltimore_Ravens "Baltimore Ravens") in the final two minutes of their Week 12 matchup and helped overcome a 17-point third quarter deficit in Week 15 to beat the [Dallas Cowboys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas_Cowboys "Dallas Cowboys") in overtime.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-67)[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-68)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-69) Lawrence was also named AFC Offensive Player of the Week in Week 14 after completing 30 of 42 passes for 368 yards and three touchdowns while also rushing for a touchdown during a 36–22 road victory over the [Tennessee Titans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee_Titans "Tennessee Titans").[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-70) In the season finale against the Titans to determine the [AFC South](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFC_South "AFC South"), he completed 20 of 32 passes for 212 yards and a touchdown to win 20–16 and clinch the Jaguars' first division title since 2017.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-71)

Lawrence finished his second professional season with 4,113 passing yards, 25 touchdowns, and eight interceptions to go along with 62 carries for 291 yards and five touchdowns, all noted improvements from his rookie campaign.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-72) Lawrence was named as an alternate to the [Pro Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Pro_Bowl "2023 Pro Bowl") and was the first Jaguars quarterback to receive Pro Bowl honors since [David Garrard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Garrard "David Garrard") in 2009.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-73) He was ranked 96th by his fellow players on the [NFL Top 100 Players of 2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_Top_100_Players_of_2023 "NFL Top 100 Players of 2023").[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-74) During the [Wild Card Round](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_NFL_playoffs#AFC:_Jacksonville_Jaguars_31,_Los_Angeles_Chargers_30 "2022–23 NFL playoffs") against the Chargers, Lawrence threw four interceptions in the first half, three of which were in the first quarter, which contributed to the Chargers taking a 27–0 lead.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-75)[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-76) However, Lawrence rebounded by throwing a touchdown pass before halftime and completing 18 of 23 passes for 211 yards and three touchdowns in the second half to secure a narrow 31–30 victory.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-77) The Jaguars' 27-point comeback was the third-largest in NFL history.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-78) In the [Divisional Round](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_NFL_playoffs#AFC:_Kansas_City_Chiefs_27,_Jacksonville_Jaguars_20 "2022–23 NFL playoffs") against the eventual [Super Bowl LVII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LVII "Super Bowl LVII") champion [Kansas City Chiefs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City_Chiefs "Kansas City Chiefs"), Lawrence completed 24 of 39 passes for 217 yards, a touchdown, and an interception during the 27–20 road loss, marking his first defeat on a Saturday.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-79)

During the season-opening 31–21 road victory over the Colts, Lawrence completed 24 of 32 passes for 241 yards, two touchdowns, and an interception.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-80)[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-81) In the next game against the Chiefs, he had 216 passing yards during the 17–9 loss.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-82) The following week against the Texans, Lawrence threw for 279 yards with a touchdown and an interception in the 37–17 loss.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-83)

During a Week 4 23–7 victory over the [Atlanta Falcons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta_Falcons "Atlanta Falcons") at [Wembley Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wembley_Stadium "Wembley Stadium"), Lawrence completed 23 of 30 passes for 207 yards and a touchdown.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-84) In the next game against the Bills at [Tottenham Hotspur Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tottenham_Hotspur_Stadium "Tottenham Hotspur Stadium"), he threw for 315 yards and a touchdown during the 25–20 victory, despite losing two fumbles.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-85) Returning to Jacksonville the following week, Lawrence had 181 passing yards, including two touchdowns and an interception in a 37–20 victory over the Colts.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-indvsjagweek62023-86)[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-87) However, Lawrence left the game late with a sprained left knee.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-indvsjagweek62023-86)[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-novsjagweek72023-88)

During Week 7 against the [New Orleans Saints](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans_Saints "New Orleans Saints") on _Thursday Night Football_, despite still being hampered by his sprained knee, Lawrence completed 20-of-29 passes for 204 yards and a touchdown in the 31–24 road victory.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-novsjagweek72023-88) In the next game against the [Pittsburgh Steelers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_Steelers "Pittsburgh Steelers"), Lawrence completed 24 of 32 passes for 292 yards, a touchdown, and an interception during the 20–10 road victory.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-89)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-90)

Following a Week 9 [bye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bye_(sports) "Bye (sports)"), Lawrence threw for 185 yards and two interceptions and lost a fumble during a 34–3 loss to the [San Francisco 49ers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_49ers "San Francisco 49ers").[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-91)[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-92) He bounced back from his poor performance against the Titans in the next game, completing 24 of 32 attempts for 262 yards and two touchdowns, plus rushing for another two touchdowns to secure a 34–14 victory.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-93)[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-94)[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-lawrence2023week11afcoff-95) Lawrence was named AFC Offensive Player of the Week after his performance in Week 11.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-lawrence2023week11afcoff-95) Two weeks later against the Bengals on _[Monday Night Football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monday\_Night\_Football "Monday Night Football")_, Lawrence completed 22-of-29 passes for 259 yards and two touchdowns while also rushing for a touchdown before leaving the eventual 34–31 overtime loss in the fourth quarter with an ankle sprain.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-96) Despite his injury, Lawrence played in Week 14 to the [Cleveland Browns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland_Browns "Cleveland Browns"), where he threw for 257 yards, three touchdowns, and three interceptions during the 31–27 road loss.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-97)

During Week 15 against the [Baltimore Ravens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltimore_Ravens "Baltimore Ravens") on _[Sunday Night Football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC\_Sunday\_Night\_Football "NBC Sunday Night Football")_, Lawrence had 264 passing yards and a touchdown in the 23–7 loss.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-98) In the next game against the [Tampa Bay Buccaneers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tampa_Bay_Buccaneers "Tampa Bay Buccaneers"), he struggled, throwing for 211 yards, a touchdown, and two interceptions before leaving the eventual 30–12 road loss during the third quarter with a shoulder injury.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-99)[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-100) As a result, Lawrence did not play the following week against [Carolina Panthers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carolina_Panthers "Carolina Panthers"), marking the first missed game in his NFL career.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-101) Lawrence returned in the regular-season finale against the Titans, where he threw for 280 yards, two touchdowns, and two interceptions while the Jaguars also turned the ball over on downs thrice during the 28–20 road loss, finishing the season having lost Lawrence's last five starts and missing the playoffs.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-102)

Lawrence finished the 2023 season with 4,016 passing yards, 21 touchdowns, and 14 interceptions to go along with 70 carries for 339 yards and four touchdowns in 16 games and starts despite dealing with four separate injuries.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-103)[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-104) He was ranked 94th by his fellow players on the [NFL Top 100 Players of 2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_Top_100_Players_of_2024 "NFL Top 100 Players of 2024").[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-105)

On April 29, 2024, the Jaguars picked up the fifth-year option on Lawrence's contract.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-106) On June 14, he signed a five-year, $275 million contract extension with $142 million guaranteed, which tied him with [Joe Burrow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow "Joe Burrow") as the highest paid player in NFL history at the time of the signing.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-107)

After the Jaguars dropped to 0–4 and Lawrence suffered his ninth consecutive loss as a starter, he threw for a career-high 371 yards and two touchdowns in Week 5 against the Colts, leading the team to a 37–34 victory on his 25th birthday.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-108) Two weeks later against the [New England Patriots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_England_Patriots "New England Patriots") in London, Lawrence completed 15 of 20 passes for 193 yards and a touchdown during the 32–16 victory.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-109) Returning to Jacksonville the following week against the [Green Bay Packers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Bay_Packers "Green Bay Packers"), Lawrence had 308 passing yards, two touchdowns, and an interception to go along with 10 rushing yards and a touchdown in the 30–27 loss.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-110)

During a Week 9 28–23 road loss to the [Philadelphia Eagles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_Eagles "Philadelphia Eagles"), Lawrence threw for 169 yards and two interceptions while also rushing for two touchdowns.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-111) However, he sustained a left shoulder injury that was later identified as a significant AC joint sprain and he was declared inactive for the next two games.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-112) Following a Week 12 bye, Lawerence returned to the lineup against the Texans. He left the eventual 23–20 loss in the second quarter with a concussion after a violent hit from [Azeez Al-Shaair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Azeez_Al-Shaair "Azeez Al-Shaair") during a slide, sparking a sideline brawl.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-113) On December 4, Lawrence was placed on injured reserve.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-114)

Lawrence finished the 2024 season with 2,045 passing yards, 11 touchdowns, and seven interceptions to go along with 26 carries for 119 yards and three touchdowns in 10 games and starts.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-115) The Jaguars finished with a 4–13 record with Lawrence leading them to a record of 2–8 under center, missing the playoffs.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-116)

See also: [2025 Jacksonville Jaguars season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Jacksonville_Jaguars_season "2025 Jacksonville Jaguars season")

Lawrence began the 2025 season throwing for 178 yards, a touchdown, and an interception in the season-opening 26–10 victory over the Panthers.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-117) In the next game against the Bengals, he had 271 passing yards, three touchdowns, and two interceptions during the 31–27 road loss.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-118) Two weeks later against the 49ers, Lawrence completed 21 of 31 passes for 174 yards and a touchdown in the 26–21 road victory.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-119)

During Week 5, against the Chiefs on his 26th birthday, Lawrence completed 18 of 25 passes for 221 yards, a touchdown, and an interception while also rushing 10 times for 54 yards and two touchdowns in the 31–28 comeback victory on _Monday Night Football_. The second touchdown run happened after Lawrence was tripped by his own right guard, stumbled getting back up, then breaking a tackle before diving into the endzone for the go ahead score.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-120) In the next game against the Seahawks, Lawrence threw for 258 yards and two touchdowns during the 20–12 loss.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-121) The following week against the [Los Angeles Rams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Rams "Los Angeles Rams") in London, he had 296 passing yards and a touchdown in the 35–7 loss.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-122)

Following a Week 8 bye, the Jaguars went on the road to face the Raiders. Despite facing an illness, Lawrence completed 23 of 34 passes for 220 yards and an interception while also rushing for 24 yards and two touchdowns in the narrow 30–29 overtime victory.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-123) In the next game against the Texans, he threw for 158 yards, a touchdown, and an interception during the 36–29 road loss.[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-124) The following week against the Chargers, he had 153 passing yards, a touchdown, and an interception to go along with a rushing touchdown in the 35–6 victory.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-125)

During Week 12, Lawrence had 256 passing yards, three touchdowns, and three interceptions in a 27–24 overtime road victory over the Cardinals.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-126) In the next game against the Titans, he threw for 229 yards and two touchdowns during the 25–3 road victory.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-127) The following week against the Colts, Lawrence had 244 passing yards and two touchdowns in the 36–19 victory.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-128)

During Week 15, Lawrence had 330 passing yards and five touchdowns to go along with five carries for 51 yards and a touchdown in a 48–20 victory over the [New York Jets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Jets "New York Jets").[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-129) He became the first player in NFL history to record five or more passing touchdowns, one or more rushing touchdowns, and 50 or more rushing yards in a single game, and was named AFC Offensive Player of the Week for his performance.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-130) He was named AFC Offensive Player of the Month for December.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-131)

During the final week of the season, Lawrence had 255 passing yards and three passing touchdowns, to finish the regular season with 29 touchdowns passing and nine rushing. In this game, he broke the franchise record for total touchdowns in a single season with 38, previously held by [Blake Bortles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blake_Bortles "Blake Bortles").[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-132) He was also voted to be the FedEx Air and Ground player of the week for the third time in the 2025 season.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-133) He also surpassed 4,000 passing yards for this season, and clinched a division win for the first time since 2022 and the 3 seed in the playoffs.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-134) In the Wild Card Round against the Bills, he had 207 yards, three touchdowns, and two interceptions in the 27–24 loss.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-135)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Trevor_Lawrence&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Lawrence is [Baptist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baptist "Baptist").[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-FloridaTimes2021-138)[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-Independent2023-139) He is noted for his long blond hair.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-140)[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-141)[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-142) Lawrence's older brother, Chase, is a visual artist for whom Trevor has posed.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-143) On April 10, 2021, Lawrence married Marissa Mowry, whom he had been dating since high school.[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-144)[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-145) In June 2024, they announced they were expecting their first child.[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-146) Their daughter, Shae Lynn, was born on January 4, 2025.[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-147)

In 2021, Lawrence, among other high-profile athletes and celebrities, was a paid spokesperson for [FTX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FTX "FTX"), a cryptocurrency exchange. In November 2022, [FTX filed for bankruptcy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bankruptcy_of_FTX "Bankruptcy of FTX"), wiping out billions of dollars in customer funds. Lawrence, alongside other spokespeople, was sued for promoting unregistered securities through a [class-action lawsuit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Class_action "Class action"),[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-148)[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-149) which was settled in September 2023.[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-150)

[American Eagle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Eagle_Outfitters "American Eagle Outfitters") featured Lawrence in its "Live Your Life" marketing campaign in 2024.[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-151)[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-152)

**William Trevor Lawrence** (born October 6, 1999) is an American professional [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_football "American football")[quarterback](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quarterback "Quarterback") for the [Jacksonville Jaguars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacksonville_Jaguars "Jacksonville Jaguars") of the [National Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League") (NFL). Considered among the highest-touted [college football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_football "College football") prospects, he won the [2019 National Championship Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_College_Football_Playoff_National_Championship "2019 College Football Playoff National Championship") as a freshman with the [Clemson Tigers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clemson_Tigers_football "Clemson Tigers football") and set the school's record for quarterback wins. Lawrence was selected [first overall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_first_overall_NFL_draft_picks "List of first overall NFL draft picks") by the Jaguars in the 2021 NFL draft. In his second season, Lawrence led the Jaguars to their first division title since 2017 and earned [Pro Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pro_Bowl "Pro Bowl") honors. He led the team to another division title in 2025.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Trevor_Lawrence&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/71/Trevor_Lawrence_%28American_football%29_Sept_2017.jpg/250px-Trevor_Lawrence_%28American_football%29_Sept_2017.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Trevor_Lawrence_(American_football)_Sept_2017.jpg)

Lawrence at [Cartersville High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cartersville_High_School "Cartersville High School") in 2017

William Trevor Lawrence was born in [Knoxville, Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knoxville,_Tennessee "Knoxville, Tennessee") on October 6, 1999 and moved to [Cartersville, Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cartersville,_Georgia "Cartersville, Georgia") when he was six.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-jcp-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-3) He later attended [Cartersville High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cartersville_High_School "Cartersville High School"), where he played football and basketball. As a junior in 2016, Lawrence was _[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Atlanta\_Journal-Constitution "The Atlanta Journal-Constitution")_ player of the year after completing 250 of 406 passes for 3,904 yards and 51 [touchdowns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Touchdowns "Touchdowns").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-4) As a sophomore, he passed for 3,655 yards and 43 touchdowns and as a freshman, Lawrence had 3,042 yards and 26 touchdowns.

From his sophomore year to his senior year, Lawrence led the Purple Hurricanes to 41 straight victories, winning two state championships and four region titles while also receiving numerous national high school player of the year honors. In 2017, Lawrence broke the [Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_(U.S._state) "Georgia (U.S. state)") state record for passing yards and passing [touchdowns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Touchdown "Touchdown"), which were previously held by [Deshaun Watson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deshaun_Watson "Deshaun Watson") of Gainesville, who also played for [Clemson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clemson_Tigers_football_team "Clemson Tigers football team").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-6)

Lawrence was a five-star recruit who was regarded as one of the best high school quarterback prospects of all time.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-10) On December 16, 2016, he committed to [Clemson University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clemson_University "Clemson University") to play college football.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-12)

### Freshman year

See also: [2018 Clemson Tigers football team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Clemson_Tigers_football_team "2018 Clemson Tigers football team")

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5a/2019_CFP_-_Clemson_offense.JPG/250px-2019_CFP_-_Clemson_offense.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2019_CFP_-_Clemson_offense.JPG)

Lawrence (#16) during the [2019 College Football Playoff National Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_College_Football_Playoff_National_Championship "2019 College Football Playoff National Championship")

Lawrence started his freshman season behind [Kelly Bryant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kelly_Bryant_(American_football) "Kelly Bryant (American football)") on Clemson's depth chart, but was given equal playing time in the season's first games. Head coach [Dabo Swinney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dabo_Swinney "Dabo Swinney") named Lawrence the new starter after four games, after which Bryant announced his intention to transfer schools.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-13) Lawrence led [Clemson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Clemson_Tigers_football_team "2018 Clemson Tigers football team") to an undefeated regular season, a 42–10 victory over [Pittsburgh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Pittsburgh_Panthers_football_team "2018 Pittsburgh Panthers football team") in the [ACC Championship Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_ACC_Championship_Game "2018 ACC Championship Game"), and a bid to play in the [College Football Playoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_Football_Playoff "College Football Playoff"). The Tigers were ranked No. 2 in the College Football Playoff rankings, and defeated No. 3 [Notre Dame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Notre_Dame_Fighting_Irish_football_team "2018 Notre Dame Fighting Irish football team"), 30–3, in the [2018 Cotton Bowl Classic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Cotton_Bowl_Classic "2018 Cotton Bowl Classic").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-14) They advanced to the [2019 College Football Playoff National Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_College_Football_Playoff_National_Championship "2019 College Football Playoff National Championship") game, where they defeated [Alabama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Alabama_Crimson_Tide_football_team "2018 Alabama Crimson Tide football team"), 44–16, handing the Crimson Tide their worst loss of the [Nick Saban](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Saban "Nick Saban") era.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-15) Lawrence was named Offensive MVP of the game and became the first [true freshman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/True_freshman "True freshman") quarterback to start for a national champion since [Jamelle Holieway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamelle_Holieway "Jamelle Holieway") in [1985](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985_NCAA_Division_I-A_football_season "1985 NCAA Division I-A football season") for [Oklahoma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985_Oklahoma_Sooners_football_team "1985 Oklahoma Sooners football team").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-16)

Lawrence threw for 3,280 passing yards and 30 touchdowns on the season, and was awarded the National Freshman of the Year and [Archie Griffin Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Touchdown_Club_of_Columbus#Archie_Griffin_Award "Touchdown Club of Columbus") by the [Touchdown Club of Columbus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Touchdown_Club_of_Columbus "Touchdown Club of Columbus").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-17) He was also awarded ACC Rookie of the Year honors.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-18)

They defeated Notre Dame in the rematch in the conference title game with Lawrence starting at quarterback and were selected to a spot in the College Football Playoff.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-29) In the CFP semifinal, the [Sugar Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Sugar_Bowl "2021 Sugar Bowl"), Lawrence and the Tigers lost to [Ohio State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Ohio_State_Buckeyes_football_team "2020 Ohio State Buckeyes football team").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-30)

One of the NFL's highest-regarded amateur prospects, Lawrence was nearly unanimously projected to be taken [first overall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_first_overall_National_Football_League_draft_picks "List of first overall National Football League draft picks") in the 2021 NFL draft.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-CatchLawrence-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-DraftOdds-38) He drew comparisons to [Pro Football Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pro_Football_Hall_of_Fame "Pro Football Hall of Fame") quarterbacks [John Elway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Elway "John Elway") and [Peyton Manning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peyton_Manning "Peyton Manning") and 2012 first overall pick [Andrew Luck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Luck "Andrew Luck"),[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-Pollack-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-Rank-40) with the slogan "[Tank for Trevor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanking_(sports)#Encouragement_by_fans "Tanking (sports)")" gaining popularity among fans of struggling teams.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-Tank-41)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-LawrenceResponse-42)_[ESPN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ESPN "ESPN")_'s[Mel Kiper Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mel_Kiper_Jr. "Mel Kiper Jr.") ranked Lawrence as the fourth highest-graded quarterback he had ever evaluated, behind Elway, Luck, and Manning.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-Kiper-43)

### 2021

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Trevor_Lawrence&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: 2021")]

See also: [2021 Jacksonville Jaguars season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Jacksonville_Jaguars_season "2021 Jacksonville Jaguars season")

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/01/Trevor_Lawrence_TEN_video.png/250px-Trevor_Lawrence_TEN_video.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Trevor_Lawrence_TEN_video.png)

Lawrence in 2021

After undergoing surgery to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder, Lawrence was officially selected first overall by the [Jacksonville Jaguars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacksonville_Jaguars "Jacksonville Jaguars"), which had finished with a league-worst 1–15 record the previous season.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-44)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-45)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-46) On July 5, 2021, he signed his four-year rookie contract, worth $36.8 million with a $24.1 million signing bonus.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-47)

Ahead of the final week of preseason, Lawrence was named the Jaguars' starting quarterback for 2021.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-48)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-49) Making his NFL debut in the season-opener against the [Houston Texans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_Texans "Houston Texans"), Lawrence finished with 332 passing yards, three touchdowns, and three interceptions in the 37–21 road loss. The loss was Lawrence's first in a regular season game.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-50) In the next game against the [Denver Broncos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver_Broncos "Denver Broncos"), he threw a touchdown pass on the opening drive, but completed only eight of 25 passes afterwards and was intercepted twice as the Jaguars lost 23–13.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-OpeningTD-51) Two weeks later against the [Cincinnati Bengals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cincinnati_Bengals "Cincinnati Bengals") on _[Thursday Night Football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thursday\_Night\_Football "Thursday Night Football")_, Lawrence had a stronger performance, completing 17 of 24 passes for 204 yards and scored his first rushing touchdown, also making it his first NFL game without an interception. Despite his efforts, the Jaguars lost on the road 24–21.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-BurrowSpoils-52)

Lawrence won his first NFL game in Week 6 against the [Miami Dolphins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_Dolphins "Miami Dolphins"), throwing for 319 yards and a touchdown during the 23–20 victory. Having played the game at [Tottenham Hotspur Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tottenham_Hotspur_Stadium "Tottenham Hotspur Stadium"), Lawrence became the first NFL rookie to win in London. The victory was also the Jaguars' first since Week 1 of the 2020 season, ending a 20-game losing streak.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-EndStreak-53)

Following a Week 8 31–7 road loss to the [Seattle Seahawks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seattle_Seahawks "Seattle Seahawks"), Lawrence took part in the season's biggest upset when he helped the 15.5-point underdog Jaguars defeat the [Buffalo Bills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buffalo_Bills "Buffalo Bills") 9–6.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-SeventhLargest-54) However, the victory began a stretch that saw Lawrence throw only two touchdown passes in nine games, including seven games without any touchdowns, while having eight interceptions.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-FightingOpponents-55) The Jaguars also went on an eight-game losing streak, dropping them to the league's worst record for a second consecutive year. Nevertheless, Lawrence concluded the season with his strongest performance in the regular season finale, completing 23 of 32 passes for 223 yards and two touchdowns to secure a 26–11 victory over the [Indianapolis Colts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indianapolis_Colts "Indianapolis Colts").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-ShockingWin-56)

Lawrence finished his rookie year with 3,641 passing yards, 12 touchdowns, and a league-leading 17 interceptions to go along with 73 carries for 334 yards and two touchdowns. Lawrence's passing yards ranked second for rookies, only behind [Mac Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mac_Jones "Mac Jones").[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-NFL2021-57)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-58)
