After losing to the [Washington Commanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Commanders "Washington Commanders") in the season opener, Lawrence won his next two games against the Colts and [Los Angeles Chargers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Chargers "Los Angeles Chargers"), throwing for a combined 497 yards and five touchdowns.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-TakeLeap-59)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-TheStar-60) The latter also marked Lawrence's first road victory and earned him AFC Offensive Player of the Week honors.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-WorthIt-61)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-62) However, the Jaguars went on a five-game losing streak, during which Lawrence completed 57.8% of his passes for 1,068 yards, five touchdowns, and five interceptions.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-ToughToTake-63) He also had two games without any touchdown passes.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-Texans13Jaguars6-64)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-Giants23Jaguars17-65) The losing streak ended with a Week 9 victory over the [Las Vegas Raiders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas_Raiders "Las Vegas Raiders"), which saw Lawrence help Jacksonville overcome a 20–10 halftime deficit to win 27–20.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-TheComeback-66)

The Week 9 victory kicked off the Jaguars winning seven of their last nine games, with Lawrence throwing for 2,273 yards, 15 touchdowns, and two interceptions. During this period, he led a game-winning drive against the [Baltimore Ravens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltimore_Ravens "Baltimore Ravens") in the final two minutes of their Week 12 matchup and helped overcome a 17-point third quarter deficit in Week 15 to beat the [Dallas Cowboys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas_Cowboys "Dallas Cowboys") in overtime.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-67)[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-68)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-69) Lawrence was also named AFC Offensive Player of the Week in Week 14 after completing 30 of 42 passes for 368 yards and three touchdowns while also rushing for a touchdown during a 36–22 road victory over the [Tennessee Titans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee_Titans "Tennessee Titans").[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-70) In the season finale against the Titans to determine the [AFC South](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFC_South "AFC South"), he completed 20 of 32 passes for 212 yards and a touchdown to win 20–16 and clinch the Jaguars' first division title since 2017.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-71)

Lawrence finished his second professional season with 4,113 passing yards, 25 touchdowns, and eight interceptions to go along with 62 carries for 291 yards and five touchdowns, all noted improvements from his rookie campaign.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-72) Lawrence was named as an alternate to the [Pro Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Pro_Bowl "2023 Pro Bowl") and was the first Jaguars quarterback to receive Pro Bowl honors since [David Garrard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Garrard "David Garrard") in 2009.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-73) He was ranked 96th by his fellow players on the [NFL Top 100 Players of 2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_Top_100_Players_of_2023 "NFL Top 100 Players of 2023").[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-74) During the [Wild Card Round](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_NFL_playoffs#AFC:_Jacksonville_Jaguars_31,_Los_Angeles_Chargers_30 "2022–23 NFL playoffs") against the Chargers, Lawrence threw four interceptions in the first half, three of which were in the first quarter, which contributed to the Chargers taking a 27–0 lead.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-75)[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-76) However, Lawrence rebounded by throwing a touchdown pass before halftime and completing 18 of 23 passes for 211 yards and three touchdowns in the second half to secure a narrow 31–30 victory.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-77) The Jaguars' 27-point comeback was the third-largest in NFL history.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-78) In the [Divisional Round](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_NFL_playoffs#AFC:_Kansas_City_Chiefs_27,_Jacksonville_Jaguars_20 "2022–23 NFL playoffs") against the eventual [Super Bowl LVII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LVII "Super Bowl LVII") champion [Kansas City Chiefs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City_Chiefs "Kansas City Chiefs"), Lawrence completed 24 of 39 passes for 217 yards, a touchdown, and an interception during the 27–20 road loss, marking his first defeat on a Saturday.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-79)

During the season-opening 31–21 road victory over the Colts, Lawrence completed 24 of 32 passes for 241 yards, two touchdowns, and an interception.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-80)[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-81) In the next game against the Chiefs, he had 216 passing yards during the 17–9 loss.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-82) The following week against the Texans, Lawrence threw for 279 yards with a touchdown and an interception in the 37–17 loss.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-83)

During a Week 4 23–7 victory over the [Atlanta Falcons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta_Falcons "Atlanta Falcons") at [Wembley Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wembley_Stadium "Wembley Stadium"), Lawrence completed 23 of 30 passes for 207 yards and a touchdown.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-84) In the next game against the Bills at [Tottenham Hotspur Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tottenham_Hotspur_Stadium "Tottenham Hotspur Stadium"), he threw for 315 yards and a touchdown during the 25–20 victory, despite losing two fumbles.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-85) Returning to Jacksonville the following week, Lawrence had 181 passing yards, including two touchdowns and an interception in a 37–20 victory over the Colts.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-indvsjagweek62023-86)[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-87) However, Lawrence left the game late with a sprained left knee.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-indvsjagweek62023-86)[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-novsjagweek72023-88)

During Week 7 against the [New Orleans Saints](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans_Saints "New Orleans Saints") on _Thursday Night Football_, despite still being hampered by his sprained knee, Lawrence completed 20-of-29 passes for 204 yards and a touchdown in the 31–24 road victory.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-novsjagweek72023-88) In the next game against the [Pittsburgh Steelers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_Steelers "Pittsburgh Steelers"), Lawrence completed 24 of 32 passes for 292 yards, a touchdown, and an interception during the 20–10 road victory.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-89)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-90)

Following a Week 9 [bye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bye_(sports) "Bye (sports)"), Lawrence threw for 185 yards and two interceptions and lost a fumble during a 34–3 loss to the [San Francisco 49ers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_49ers "San Francisco 49ers").[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-91)[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-92) He bounced back from his poor performance against the Titans in the next game, completing 24 of 32 attempts for 262 yards and two touchdowns, plus rushing for another two touchdowns to secure a 34–14 victory.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-93)[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-94)[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-lawrence2023week11afcoff-95) Lawrence was named AFC Offensive Player of the Week after his performance in Week 11.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-lawrence2023week11afcoff-95) Two weeks later against the Bengals on _[Monday Night Football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monday\_Night\_Football "Monday Night Football")_, Lawrence completed 22-of-29 passes for 259 yards and two touchdowns while also rushing for a touchdown before leaving the eventual 34–31 overtime loss in the fourth quarter with an ankle sprain.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-96) Despite his injury, Lawrence played in Week 14 to the [Cleveland Browns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland_Browns "Cleveland Browns"), where he threw for 257 yards, three touchdowns, and three interceptions during the 31–27 road loss.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-97)

During Week 15 against the [Baltimore Ravens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltimore_Ravens "Baltimore Ravens") on _[Sunday Night Football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC\_Sunday\_Night\_Football "NBC Sunday Night Football")_, Lawrence had 264 passing yards and a touchdown in the 23–7 loss.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-98) In the next game against the [Tampa Bay Buccaneers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tampa_Bay_Buccaneers "Tampa Bay Buccaneers"), he struggled, throwing for 211 yards, a touchdown, and two interceptions before leaving the eventual 30–12 road loss during the third quarter with a shoulder injury.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-99)[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-100) As a result, Lawrence did not play the following week against [Carolina Panthers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carolina_Panthers "Carolina Panthers"), marking the first missed game in his NFL career.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-101) Lawrence returned in the regular-season finale against the Titans, where he threw for 280 yards, two touchdowns, and two interceptions while the Jaguars also turned the ball over on downs thrice during the 28–20 road loss, finishing the season having lost Lawrence's last five starts and missing the playoffs.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-102)

Lawrence finished the 2023 season with 4,016 passing yards, 21 touchdowns, and 14 interceptions to go along with 70 carries for 339 yards and four touchdowns in 16 games and starts despite dealing with four separate injuries.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-103)[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-104) He was ranked 94th by his fellow players on the [NFL Top 100 Players of 2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_Top_100_Players_of_2024 "NFL Top 100 Players of 2024").[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-105)

### 2024

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Trevor_Lawrence&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: 2024")]

See also: [2024 Jacksonville Jaguars season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Jacksonville_Jaguars_season "2024 Jacksonville Jaguars season")

[![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/98/501st_CSW_Honor_Guard_perform_at_NFL_London_game_%288710703%29_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-501st_CSW_Honor_Guard_perform_at_NFL_London_game_%288710703%29_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:501st_CSW_Honor_Guard_perform_at_NFL_London_game_(8710703)_(cropped).jpg)

Lawrence in 2024

On April 29, 2024, the Jaguars picked up the fifth-year option on Lawrence's contract.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-106) On June 14, he signed a five-year, $275 million contract extension with $142 million guaranteed, which tied him with [Joe Burrow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow "Joe Burrow") as the highest paid player in NFL history at the time of the signing.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-107)

After the Jaguars dropped to 0–4 and Lawrence suffered his ninth consecutive loss as a starter, he threw for a career-high 371 yards and two touchdowns in Week 5 against the Colts, leading the team to a 37–34 victory on his 25th birthday.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-108) Two weeks later against the [New England Patriots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_England_Patriots "New England Patriots") in London, Lawrence completed 15 of 20 passes for 193 yards and a touchdown during the 32–16 victory.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-109) Returning to Jacksonville the following week against the [Green Bay Packers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Bay_Packers "Green Bay Packers"), Lawrence had 308 passing yards, two touchdowns, and an interception to go along with 10 rushing yards and a touchdown in the 30–27 loss.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-110)

During a Week 9 28–23 road loss to the [Philadelphia Eagles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_Eagles "Philadelphia Eagles"), Lawrence threw for 169 yards and two interceptions while also rushing for two touchdowns.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-111) However, he sustained a left shoulder injury that was later identified as a significant AC joint sprain and he was declared inactive for the next two games.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-112) Following a Week 12 bye, Lawerence returned to the lineup against the Texans. He left the eventual 23–20 loss in the second quarter with a concussion after a violent hit from [Azeez Al-Shaair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Azeez_Al-Shaair "Azeez Al-Shaair") during a slide, sparking a sideline brawl.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-113) On December 4, Lawrence was placed on injured reserve.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-114)

Lawrence finished the 2024 season with 2,045 passing yards, 11 touchdowns, and seven interceptions to go along with 26 carries for 119 yards and three touchdowns in 10 games and starts.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-115) The Jaguars finished with a 4–13 record with Lawrence leading them to a record of 2–8 under center, missing the playoffs.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-116)

### 2025

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Trevor_Lawrence&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: 2025")]

See also: [2025 Jacksonville Jaguars season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Jacksonville_Jaguars_season "2025 Jacksonville Jaguars season")

Lawrence began the 2025 season throwing for 178 yards, a touchdown, and an interception in the season-opening 26–10 victory over the Panthers.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-117) In the next game against the Bengals, he had 271 passing yards, three touchdowns, and two interceptions during the 31–27 road loss.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-118) Two weeks later against the 49ers, Lawrence completed 21 of 31 passes for 174 yards and a touchdown in the 26–21 road victory.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-119)

During Week 5, against the Chiefs on his 26th birthday, Lawrence completed 18 of 25 passes for 221 yards, a touchdown, and an interception while also rushing 10 times for 54 yards and two touchdowns in the 31–28 comeback victory on _Monday Night Football_. The second touchdown run happened after Lawrence was tripped by his own right guard, stumbled getting back up, then breaking a tackle before diving into the endzone for the go ahead score.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-120) In the next game against the Seahawks, Lawrence threw for 258 yards and two touchdowns during the 20–12 loss.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-121) The following week against the [Los Angeles Rams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Rams "Los Angeles Rams") in London, he had 296 passing yards and a touchdown in the 35–7 loss.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-122)

Following a Week 8 bye, the Jaguars went on the road to face the Raiders. Despite facing an illness, Lawrence completed 23 of 34 passes for 220 yards and an interception while also rushing for 24 yards and two touchdowns in the narrow 30–29 overtime victory.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-123) In the next game against the Texans, he threw for 158 yards, a touchdown, and an interception during the 36–29 road loss.[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-124) The following week against the Chargers, he had 153 passing yards, a touchdown, and an interception to go along with a rushing touchdown in the 35–6 victory.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-125)

During Week 12, Lawrence had 256 passing yards, three touchdowns, and three interceptions in a 27–24 overtime road victory over the Cardinals.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-126) In the next game against the Titans, he threw for 229 yards and two touchdowns during the 25–3 road victory.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-127) The following week against the Colts, Lawrence had 244 passing yards and two touchdowns in the 36–19 victory.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-128)

During Week 15, Lawrence had 330 passing yards and five touchdowns to go along with five carries for 51 yards and a touchdown in a 48–20 victory over the [New York Jets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Jets "New York Jets").[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-129) He became the first player in NFL history to record five or more passing touchdowns, one or more rushing touchdowns, and 50 or more rushing yards in a single game, and was named AFC Offensive Player of the Week for his performance.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-130) He was named AFC Offensive Player of the Month for December.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-131)

During the final week of the season, Lawrence had 255 passing yards and three passing touchdowns, to finish the regular season with 29 touchdowns passing and nine rushing. In this game, he broke the franchise record for total touchdowns in a single season with 38, previously held by [Blake Bortles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blake_Bortles "Blake Bortles").[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-132) He was also voted to be the FedEx Air and Ground player of the week for the third time in the 2025 season.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-133) He also surpassed 4,000 passing yards for this season, and clinched a division win for the first time since 2022 and the 3 seed in the playoffs.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-134) In the Wild Card Round against the Bills, he had 207 yards, three touchdowns, and two interceptions in the 27–24 loss.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-135)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Trevor_Lawrence&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Lawrence is [Baptist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baptist "Baptist").[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-FloridaTimes2021-138)[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-Independent2023-139) He is noted for his long blond hair.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-140)[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-141)[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-142) Lawrence's older brother, Chase, is a visual artist for whom Trevor has posed.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-143) On April 10, 2021, Lawrence married Marissa Mowry, whom he had been dating since high school.[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-144)[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-145) In June 2024, they announced they were expecting their first child.[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-146) Their daughter, Shae Lynn, was born on January 4, 2025.[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-147)

In 2021, Lawrence, among other high-profile athletes and celebrities, was a paid spokesperson for [FTX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FTX "FTX"), a cryptocurrency exchange. In November 2022, [FTX filed for bankruptcy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bankruptcy_of_FTX "Bankruptcy of FTX"), wiping out billions of dollars in customer funds. Lawrence, alongside other spokespeople, was sued for promoting unregistered securities through a [class-action lawsuit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Class_action "Class action"),[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-148)[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-149) which was settled in September 2023.[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-150)

[American Eagle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Eagle_Outfitters "American Eagle Outfitters") featured Lawrence in its "Live Your Life" marketing campaign in 2024.[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-151)[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Lawrence#cite_note-152)

**Zachary Kapono Wilson** (born August 3, 1999) is an American professional [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_football "American football")[quarterback](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quarterback "Quarterback") for the [New Orleans Saints](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans_Saints "New Orleans Saints") of the [National Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League") (NFL). He played [college football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_football "College football") for the [BYU Cougars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BYU_Cougars_football "BYU Cougars football") and was selected [second overall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_second_overall_NFL_draft_picks "List of second overall NFL draft picks") by the [New York Jets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Jets "New York Jets") in the 2021 NFL draft. Wilson served as the Jets' starter during his first three seasons, but inconsistent play led to his departure from the team. He spent his next two seasons as a backup with the [Denver Broncos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver_Broncos "Denver Broncos") and [Miami Dolphins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_Dolphins "Miami Dolphins") before joining the Saints in 2026.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zach_Wilson&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Wilson was born in [Draper, Utah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Draper,_Utah "Draper, Utah"),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-2)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-3) on August 3, 1999.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-Hawaiian-4) He attended [Corner Canyon High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corner_Canyon_High_School "Corner Canyon High School"), where he played [high school football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_school_football "High school football").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-5) He passed for 2,986 yards and 24 [touchdowns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Touchdown "Touchdown") while also rushing for 752 yards and eight touchdowns as a senior. Wilson originally committed to play [quarterback](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quarterback "Quarterback") at [Boise State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boise_State_University "Boise State University") before later decommitting and choosing to attend [Brigham Young University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brigham_Young_University "Brigham Young University") (BYU).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-6)

## College career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zach_Wilson&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: College career")]

As a true freshman at [BYU](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BYU_Cougars_football "BYU Cougars football") in 2018, Wilson played in nine games and made seven starts.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-7) He started his first career game against the [Hawaii Rainbow Warriors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Hawaii_Rainbow_Warriors_football_team "2018 Hawaii Rainbow Warriors football team"), becoming the youngest quarterback to start a game for BYU.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-8) He finished the season having completed 120 of 182 passes for 1,578 yards with 12 touchdowns and three interceptions.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-Neeleman-9) He was named the MVP of the [2018 Famous Idaho Potato Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Famous_Idaho_Potato_Bowl "2018 Famous Idaho Potato Bowl") after completing all 18 of his passes for 317 yards and four touchdowns in the 49–18 victory over the [Western Michigan Broncos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Western_Michigan_Broncos_football_team "2018 Western Michigan Broncos football team").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-10)

As a sophomore in 2019, Wilson started nine games, completing 199 of 319 passes for 2,382 yards, 11 touchdowns and nine interceptions.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-11)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-12) That season, the Cougars were invited to the [2019 Hawaii Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Hawaii_Bowl "2019 Hawaii Bowl"), where Wilson was named BYU's MVP in the Cougars' 38–34 loss to the [Hawaii Rainbow Warriors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Hawaii_Rainbow_Warriors_football_team "2019 Hawaii Rainbow Warriors football team").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-13)

As a junior in 2020, Wilson started 12 games and completed 247 of 336 passes for 3,692 yards, 33 touchdowns and three interceptions while rushing for 255 yards and 10 touchdowns, breaking [Steve Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Young "Steve Young")'s school completion percentage in a season at 73.5 percent.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-Hawaiian-4)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-14)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-15) He helped lead BYU to a 10–1 regular season mark.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-16) He was named the offensive MVP of the [2020 Boca Raton Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Boca_Raton_Bowl "2020 Boca Raton Bowl") after completing 26 of 34 passes for 425 yards and three touchdowns in the 49–23 victory over the [UCF Knights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UCF_Knights_football_team "2020 UCF Knights football team").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-17) He and [USC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USC_Trojans_football "USC Trojans football") safety [Talanoa Hufanga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talanoa_Hufanga "Talanoa Hufanga") were selected as recipients of the 2020 Polynesian College Football Player of the Year Award.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-Hawaiian-4)

Wilson in 2021

A top quarterback prospect in the 2021 NFL draft, Wilson was selected second overall by the [New York Jets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Jets "New York Jets"). He was the second of five quarterbacks taken in the first round and the highest-ever drafted from [BYU](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BYU_Cougars_football_team "BYU Cougars football team").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-21)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-22) Wilson signed a four-year deal on July 29, 2021, that was worth $35.15 million fully guaranteed, along with a $22.9 million signing bonus and a fifth year option.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-23)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-24)

In his debut against the [Carolina Panthers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carolina_Panthers "Carolina Panthers"), Wilson had an interception in the first half, but finished with 258 passing yards, two touchdowns, and a rushing 2-point conversion in the 19–14 defeat.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-25) During the Jets' home opener in Week 2, Wilson threw four interceptions against the [New England Patriots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_England_Patriots "New England Patriots"), including on his first two pass attempts. The Jets subsequently lost 25–6.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-4INTs-26)

Following a 26–0 shutout loss to the [Denver Broncos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver_Broncos "Denver Broncos"), in which he threw for 160 yards and two interceptions, Wilson earned his first career win against the [Tennessee Titans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee_Titans "Tennessee Titans") in Week 4. Wilson had one interception, but also threw two touchdowns and completed 21 of 34 passes for 297 yards. One of his touchdowns was a 53-yard pass to wide receiver [Corey Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corey_Davis_(wide_receiver) "Corey Davis (wide receiver)") that gave the Jets a 24–17 lead in the fourth quarter, with the team going on to win 27–24 in overtime.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-Electric-27) Wilson threw his ninth interception during a Week 5 defeat to the [Atlanta Falcons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta_Falcons "Atlanta Falcons"), making him the fourth NFL quarterback after [DeShone Kizer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeShone_Kizer "DeShone Kizer"), [Zach Mettenberger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Mettenberger "Zach Mettenberger"), and [Blake Bortles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blake_Bortles "Blake Bortles") to be intercepted in each of his first five starts.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-Beleaguered-28)

During Week 7 against the Patriots, Wilson suffered a knee injury in the second quarter after being hit by linebacker [Matthew Judon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matthew_Judon "Matthew Judon"). He was ruled out for the remainder of the game, with [Mike White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_White_(quarterback) "Mike White (quarterback)") replacing him in the 54–13 loss.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-JetsDestroyed-29) Following the defeat, it was announced that Wilson had a sprained [posterior cruciate ligament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Posterior_cruciate_ligament "Posterior cruciate ligament") in his right knee, which caused him to miss four games.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-SprainedPCL-30) Wilson returned in Week 12 and won his first road game over the [Houston Texans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_Texans "Houston Texans"). He also scored his first rushing touchdown during the game.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-LeadsWin-31) Wilson lost four of his last five matchups, with his final win of the season coming against the [Jacksonville Jaguars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacksonville_Jaguars "Jacksonville Jaguars") in Week 16.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-32) However, he improved his turnover differential by not throwing an interception in the five games.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-CanImprove-33) Wilson finished his rookie season with 2,334 passing yards, nine passing touchdowns, 11 interceptions, and a 3–10 record.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-34)

#### 2022

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zach_Wilson&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 2022")]

See also: [2022 New York Jets season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_New_York_Jets_season "2022 New York Jets season")

Wilson missed the first three games of 2022 season due to a non-contact bone bruise and [meniscus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meniscus_(anatomy) "Meniscus (anatomy)") tear he suffered in the preseason opener against the [Philadelphia Eagles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_Eagles "Philadelphia Eagles").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-35) He made his season debut in Week 4 against the [Pittsburgh Steelers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_Steelers "Pittsburgh Steelers") and despite throwing two interceptions, had a 2-yard receiving touchdown from wide receiver [Braxton Berrios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Braxton_Berrios "Braxton Berrios") and led the Jets on a fourth quarter comeback drive to secure the 24–20 victory.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-ComesUp-36) The victory began a four-game winning streak for the Jets, although Wilson did not throw a touchdown pass in his next three games.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-GettingComfortable-37) New York's streak ended with a 22–17 loss to the Patriots, in which Wilson had a career-high 355 passing yards and two touchdowns, but also three interceptions.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-TurnoverMachine-38) Wilson rebounded the following week when he completed 18 of 25 passes for 154 yards and a touchdown to help secure a 20–17 upset over the [Buffalo Bills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buffalo_Bills "Buffalo Bills").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-ShockingUpset-39)

After completing only 9 of 22 passes in a 10–3 loss to the Patriots the next game, Wilson was criticized for not attributing the loss to his performance.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-40) Wilson was subsequently demoted to the third-string backup behind [Mike White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_White_(quarterback) "Mike White (quarterback)") and second-string backup [Joe Flacco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Flacco "Joe Flacco").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-BestHeCan-41) Ahead of Week 15, he was promoted to the second option and started the Jets' next two games due to an injury to White.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-42) However, after struggling against the [Jacksonville Jaguars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacksonville_Jaguars "Jacksonville Jaguars") during Week 16, Wilson was benched for [Chris Streveler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Streveler "Chris Streveler") in the Jets' eventual 19–3 defeat.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-43) Wilson was demoted back to third-string behind White and Flacco following White's return and did not take the field again for the remainder of the season.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-44)

#### 2023

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zach_Wilson&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2023")]

See also: [2023 New York Jets season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_New_York_Jets_season "2023 New York Jets season")

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/dc/Rodgers_with_Wilson_in_background.jpg/250px-Rodgers_with_Wilson_in_background.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rodgers_with_Wilson_in_background.jpg)

Wilson (#2) standing on the sidelines shortly before the injury of Aaron Rodgers (#8) against the [Buffalo Bills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buffalo_Bills "Buffalo Bills") in 2023

After the Jets acquired four-time [MVP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League_Most_Valuable_Player_Award "National Football League Most Valuable Player Award") quarterback [Aaron Rodgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Rodgers "Aaron Rodgers"), Wilson was named Rodgers' backup for the 2023 season, but took the field in the Week 1 _[Monday Night Football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monday\_Night\_Football "Monday Night Football")_ matchup against the Bills when Rodgers suffered a season-ending injury on his first drive.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-45) Wilson completed 14 of 21 passes for 140 yards, a touchdown, and an interception in the 22–16 victory.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-46) He was subsequently promoted to starting quarterback.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-47) After struggling in his first two starts of the season,[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-48) Wilson had a strong performance against the [Kansas City Chiefs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City_Chiefs "Kansas City Chiefs") on _[Sunday Night Football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC\_Sunday\_Night\_Football "NBC Sunday Night Football")_, throwing for 245 yards and 2 touchdowns to overcome a 17–0 deficit to tie the game at 20.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-49) However, he lost a fumble in the fourth quarter that allowed Kansas City to win 23–20.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-50)

Wilson led the Jets to three straight wins the following weeks, including an upset win over the reigning NFC champion Philadelphia Eagles, as well as driving 58 yards in 24 seconds with no timeouts on the game-tying drive against the Giants.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-51) However, following three weeks of struggles, Wilson was benched for [Tim Boyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Boyle_(American_football) "Tim Boyle (American football)") late in the third quarter of a 32–6 Week 11 loss to the Buffalo Bills. He finished the game completing 7 of 15 passes for 81 yards and an interception, although he threw the Jets' first touchdown in 13 quarters of play.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-52) Following the Bills loss, Wilson was demoted to third-string quarterback behind Boyle and [Trevor Siemian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Siemian "Trevor Siemian").[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-53)

After losing both games Boyle started in, the Jets released Boyle and renamed Wilson as their starter for Week 14 against the Texans.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-54) In his return, Wilson completed 27 of 36 passes for 301 yards, two touchdowns, and zero interceptions as the Jets won 30–6. He also finished the game with a 117.9 [passer rating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passer_rating "Passer rating"), the highest mark of his career.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-55) Wilson was named [American Football Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Football_Conference "American Football Conference") Offensive Player of the Week for his performance.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-56) The following week against the [Miami Dolphins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_Dolphins "Miami Dolphins"), Wilson suffered a concussion during the second quarter and did not return. He was later ruled out for the remainder of the season.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-57)

### Denver Broncos

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zach_Wilson&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Denver Broncos")]

On April 23, 2024, the [Denver Broncos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver_Broncos "Denver Broncos") announced that they had acquired Wilson and a 2024 seventh-round pick (No. 256; [Nick Gargiulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Gargiulo "Nick Gargiulo")) from the Jets in exchange for a 2024 sixth-round pick (No. 203; the [Minnesota Vikings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota_Vikings "Minnesota Vikings") selected [Will Reichard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_Reichard "Will Reichard")).[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-58) The Broncos declined the fifth-year option on Wilson's contract, making him a free agent after the 2024 season.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-e530-59) Denver announced that Wilson would begin the season as the team’s third-string quarterback, behind [Bo Nix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bo_Nix "Bo Nix") and [Jarrett Stidham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jarrett_Stidham "Jarrett Stidham").[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-60) He did not appear in a game during the season.

### Miami Dolphins

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zach_Wilson&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Miami Dolphins")]

On March 17, 2025, Wilson signed a one-year, $6 million contract with the [Miami Dolphins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_Dolphins "Miami Dolphins").[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-61)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-62) Wilson appeared in four games for Miami, completing six of his 11 pass attempts for 32 yards.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-63)

### New Orleans Saints

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zach_Wilson&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: New Orleans Saints")]

On March 26, 2026, Wilson signed a one-year, $1.4 million contract with the [New Orleans Saints](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans_Saints "New Orleans Saints").[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-64)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zach_Wilson&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Wilson was born to Michael and Lisa Wilson ([née](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birth_name#Maiden_and_married_names "Birth name")Neeleman) and has three brothers, one of whom is college quarterback [Isaac Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isaac_Wilson_(American_football) "Isaac Wilson (American football)"), and two sisters.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-66)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-Neeleman-9) He is part [Hawaiian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_Hawaiians "Native Hawaiians") on his father's side, with his middle name [Kapono](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kapono "Kapono") meaning "righteous" in the [Hawaiian language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaiian_language "Hawaiian language").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-Hawaiian-4)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-Neeleman-9) Some other members of his family include airline entrepreneur [David Neeleman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Neeleman "David Neeleman") and [HealthEquity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HealthEquity "HealthEquity") co-founder Stephen Neeleman.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-Neeleman-9)

Wilson was diagnosed with [attention deficit hyperactivity disorder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attention_deficit_hyperactivity_disorder "Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder") (ADHD) as a child, a trait that runs in his family.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-Neeleman-9)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-Church-67) Wilson was baptized as a member of [the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Church_of_Jesus_Christ_of_Latter-day_Saints "The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints"). He has said that he "didn't grow up active in the church [and] was never really a churchgoer..." He considers himself a spiritual person, telling _[Deseret News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deseret\_News "Deseret News")_ "I have always had a good relationship with God in my life."[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-Church-67)

Wilson has been friends with former BYU Cougars teammate [Dax Milne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dax_Milne "Dax Milne") since childhood.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-68)

In June 2024, Wilson announced his engagement to girlfriend Nicolette Dellanno.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-69) On June 28, 2025, Wilson and Dellanno were married in New York City.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-70)

**Zachary Kapono Wilson** (born August 3, 1999) is an American professional [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_football "American football")[quarterback](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quarterback "Quarterback") for the [New Orleans Saints](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans_Saints "New Orleans Saints") of the [National Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League") (NFL). He played [college football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_football "College football") for the [BYU Cougars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BYU_Cougars_football "BYU Cougars football") and was selected [second overall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_second_overall_NFL_draft_picks "List of second overall NFL draft picks") by the [New York Jets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Jets "New York Jets") in the 2021 NFL draft. Wilson served as the Jets' starter during his first three seasons, but inconsistent play led to his departure from the team. He spent his next two seasons as a backup with the [Denver Broncos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver_Broncos "Denver Broncos") and [Miami Dolphins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_Dolphins "Miami Dolphins") before joining the Saints in 2026.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zach_Wilson&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Wilson was born in [Draper, Utah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Draper,_Utah "Draper, Utah"),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-2)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-3) on August 3, 1999.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-Hawaiian-4) He attended [Corner Canyon High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corner_Canyon_High_School "Corner Canyon High School"), where he played [high school football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_school_football "High school football").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-5) He passed for 2,986 yards and 24 [touchdowns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Touchdown "Touchdown") while also rushing for 752 yards and eight touchdowns as a senior. Wilson originally committed to play [quarterback](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quarterback "Quarterback") at [Boise State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boise_State_University "Boise State University") before later decommitting and choosing to attend [Brigham Young University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brigham_Young_University "Brigham Young University") (BYU).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-6)

## College career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zach_Wilson&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: College career")]

As a true freshman at [BYU](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BYU_Cougars_football "BYU Cougars football") in 2018, Wilson played in nine games and made seven starts.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-7) He started his first career game against the [Hawaii Rainbow Warriors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Hawaii_Rainbow_Warriors_football_team "2018 Hawaii Rainbow Warriors football team"), becoming the youngest quarterback to start a game for BYU.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-8) He finished the season having completed 120 of 182 passes for 1,578 yards with 12 touchdowns and three interceptions.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-Neeleman-9) He was named the MVP of the [2018 Famous Idaho Potato Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Famous_Idaho_Potato_Bowl "2018 Famous Idaho Potato Bowl") after completing all 18 of his passes for 317 yards and four touchdowns in the 49–18 victory over the [Western Michigan Broncos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Western_Michigan_Broncos_football_team "2018 Western Michigan Broncos football team").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-10)

As a sophomore in 2019, Wilson started nine games, completing 199 of 319 passes for 2,382 yards, 11 touchdowns and nine interceptions.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-11)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-12) That season, the Cougars were invited to the [2019 Hawaii Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Hawaii_Bowl "2019 Hawaii Bowl"), where Wilson was named BYU's MVP in the Cougars' 38–34 loss to the [Hawaii Rainbow Warriors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Hawaii_Rainbow_Warriors_football_team "2019 Hawaii Rainbow Warriors football team").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-13)

As a junior in 2020, Wilson started 12 games and completed 247 of 336 passes for 3,692 yards, 33 touchdowns and three interceptions while rushing for 255 yards and 10 touchdowns, breaking [Steve Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Young "Steve Young")'s school completion percentage in a season at 73.5 percent.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-Hawaiian-4)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-14)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-15) He helped lead BYU to a 10–1 regular season mark.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-16) He was named the offensive MVP of the [2020 Boca Raton Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Boca_Raton_Bowl "2020 Boca Raton Bowl") after completing 26 of 34 passes for 425 yards and three touchdowns in the 49–23 victory over the [UCF Knights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_UCF_Knights_football_team "2020 UCF Knights football team").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-17) He and [USC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USC_Trojans_football "USC Trojans football") safety [Talanoa Hufanga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talanoa_Hufanga "Talanoa Hufanga") were selected as recipients of the 2020 Polynesian College Football Player of the Year Award.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-Hawaiian-4)

### New York Jets

#### 2021

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zach_Wilson&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2021")]

See also: [2021 New York Jets season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_New_York_Jets_season "2021 New York Jets season")

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/78/Zach_Wilson_Jets-Falcons_2021_%28cropped%29.png/250px-Zach_Wilson_Jets-Falcons_2021_%28cropped%29.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Zach_Wilson_Jets-Falcons_2021_(cropped).png)

Wilson in 2021

A top quarterback prospect in the 2021 NFL draft, Wilson was selected second overall by the [New York Jets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Jets "New York Jets"). He was the second of five quarterbacks taken in the first round and the highest-ever drafted from [BYU](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BYU_Cougars_football_team "BYU Cougars football team").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-21)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-22) Wilson signed a four-year deal on July 29, 2021, that was worth $35.15 million fully guaranteed, along with a $22.9 million signing bonus and a fifth year option.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-23)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-24)

In his debut against the [Carolina Panthers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carolina_Panthers "Carolina Panthers"), Wilson had an interception in the first half, but finished with 258 passing yards, two touchdowns, and a rushing 2-point conversion in the 19–14 defeat.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-25) During the Jets' home opener in Week 2, Wilson threw four interceptions against the [New England Patriots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_England_Patriots "New England Patriots"), including on his first two pass attempts. The Jets subsequently lost 25–6.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-4INTs-26)

Following a 26–0 shutout loss to the [Denver Broncos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver_Broncos "Denver Broncos"), in which he threw for 160 yards and two interceptions, Wilson earned his first career win against the [Tennessee Titans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee_Titans "Tennessee Titans") in Week 4. Wilson had one interception, but also threw two touchdowns and completed 21 of 34 passes for 297 yards. One of his touchdowns was a 53-yard pass to wide receiver [Corey Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corey_Davis_(wide_receiver) "Corey Davis (wide receiver)") that gave the Jets a 24–17 lead in the fourth quarter, with the team going on to win 27–24 in overtime.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-Electric-27) Wilson threw his ninth interception during a Week 5 defeat to the [Atlanta Falcons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta_Falcons "Atlanta Falcons"), making him the fourth NFL quarterback after [DeShone Kizer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeShone_Kizer "DeShone Kizer"), [Zach Mettenberger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Mettenberger "Zach Mettenberger"), and [Blake Bortles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blake_Bortles "Blake Bortles") to be intercepted in each of his first five starts.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-Beleaguered-28)

During Week 7 against the Patriots, Wilson suffered a knee injury in the second quarter after being hit by linebacker [Matthew Judon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matthew_Judon "Matthew Judon"). He was ruled out for the remainder of the game, with [Mike White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_White_(quarterback) "Mike White (quarterback)") replacing him in the 54–13 loss.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-JetsDestroyed-29) Following the defeat, it was announced that Wilson had a sprained [posterior cruciate ligament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Posterior_cruciate_ligament "Posterior cruciate ligament") in his right knee, which caused him to miss four games.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-SprainedPCL-30) Wilson returned in Week 12 and won his first road game over the [Houston Texans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_Texans "Houston Texans"). He also scored his first rushing touchdown during the game.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-LeadsWin-31) Wilson lost four of his last five matchups, with his final win of the season coming against the [Jacksonville Jaguars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacksonville_Jaguars "Jacksonville Jaguars") in Week 16.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-32) However, he improved his turnover differential by not throwing an interception in the five games.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-CanImprove-33) Wilson finished his rookie season with 2,334 passing yards, nine passing touchdowns, 11 interceptions, and a 3–10 record.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-34)

#### 2022

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zach_Wilson&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 2022")]

See also: [2022 New York Jets season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_New_York_Jets_season "2022 New York Jets season")

Wilson missed the first three games of 2022 season due to a non-contact bone bruise and [meniscus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meniscus_(anatomy) "Meniscus (anatomy)") tear he suffered in the preseason opener against the [Philadelphia Eagles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_Eagles "Philadelphia Eagles").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-35) He made his season debut in Week 4 against the [Pittsburgh Steelers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_Steelers "Pittsburgh Steelers") and despite throwing two interceptions, had a 2-yard receiving touchdown from wide receiver [Braxton Berrios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Braxton_Berrios "Braxton Berrios") and led the Jets on a fourth quarter comeback drive to secure the 24–20 victory.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-ComesUp-36) The victory began a four-game winning streak for the Jets, although Wilson did not throw a touchdown pass in his next three games.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-GettingComfortable-37) New York's streak ended with a 22–17 loss to the Patriots, in which Wilson had a career-high 355 passing yards and two touchdowns, but also three interceptions.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-TurnoverMachine-38) Wilson rebounded the following week when he completed 18 of 25 passes for 154 yards and a touchdown to help secure a 20–17 upset over the [Buffalo Bills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buffalo_Bills "Buffalo Bills").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-ShockingUpset-39)

After completing only 9 of 22 passes in a 10–3 loss to the Patriots the next game, Wilson was criticized for not attributing the loss to his performance.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-40) Wilson was subsequently demoted to the third-string backup behind [Mike White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_White_(quarterback) "Mike White (quarterback)") and second-string backup [Joe Flacco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Flacco "Joe Flacco").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-BestHeCan-41) Ahead of Week 15, he was promoted to the second option and started the Jets' next two games due to an injury to White.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-42) However, after struggling against the [Jacksonville Jaguars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacksonville_Jaguars "Jacksonville Jaguars") during Week 16, Wilson was benched for [Chris Streveler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Streveler "Chris Streveler") in the Jets' eventual 19–3 defeat.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-43) Wilson was demoted back to third-string behind White and Flacco following White's return and did not take the field again for the remainder of the season.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-44)

#### 2023

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zach_Wilson&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2023")]

See also: [2023 New York Jets season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_New_York_Jets_season "2023 New York Jets season")

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/dc/Rodgers_with_Wilson_in_background.jpg/250px-Rodgers_with_Wilson_in_background.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rodgers_with_Wilson_in_background.jpg)

Wilson (#2) standing on the sidelines shortly before the injury of Aaron Rodgers (#8) against the [Buffalo Bills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buffalo_Bills "Buffalo Bills") in 2023

After the Jets acquired four-time [MVP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League_Most_Valuable_Player_Award "National Football League Most Valuable Player Award") quarterback [Aaron Rodgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Rodgers "Aaron Rodgers"), Wilson was named Rodgers' backup for the 2023 season, but took the field in the Week 1 _[Monday Night Football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monday\_Night\_Football "Monday Night Football")_ matchup against the Bills when Rodgers suffered a season-ending injury on his first drive.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-45) Wilson completed 14 of 21 passes for 140 yards, a touchdown, and an interception in the 22–16 victory.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-46) He was subsequently promoted to starting quarterback.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-47) After struggling in his first two starts of the season,[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-48) Wilson had a strong performance against the [Kansas City Chiefs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City_Chiefs "Kansas City Chiefs") on _[Sunday Night Football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC\_Sunday\_Night\_Football "NBC Sunday Night Football")_, throwing for 245 yards and 2 touchdowns to overcome a 17–0 deficit to tie the game at 20.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-49) However, he lost a fumble in the fourth quarter that allowed Kansas City to win 23–20.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-50)

Wilson led the Jets to three straight wins the following weeks, including an upset win over the reigning NFC champion Philadelphia Eagles, as well as driving 58 yards in 24 seconds with no timeouts on the game-tying drive against the Giants.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-51) However, following three weeks of struggles, Wilson was benched for [Tim Boyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Boyle_(American_football) "Tim Boyle (American football)") late in the third quarter of a 32–6 Week 11 loss to the Buffalo Bills. He finished the game completing 7 of 15 passes for 81 yards and an interception, although he threw the Jets' first touchdown in 13 quarters of play.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-52) Following the Bills loss, Wilson was demoted to third-string quarterback behind Boyle and [Trevor Siemian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Siemian "Trevor Siemian").[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-53)

After losing both games Boyle started in, the Jets released Boyle and renamed Wilson as their starter for Week 14 against the Texans.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-54) In his return, Wilson completed 27 of 36 passes for 301 yards, two touchdowns, and zero interceptions as the Jets won 30–6. He also finished the game with a 117.9 [passer rating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passer_rating "Passer rating"), the highest mark of his career.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-55) Wilson was named [American Football Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Football_Conference "American Football Conference") Offensive Player of the Week for his performance.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-56) The following week against the [Miami Dolphins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_Dolphins "Miami Dolphins"), Wilson suffered a concussion during the second quarter and did not return. He was later ruled out for the remainder of the season.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-57)

### Denver Broncos

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zach_Wilson&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Denver Broncos")]

On April 23, 2024, the [Denver Broncos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver_Broncos "Denver Broncos") announced that they had acquired Wilson and a 2024 seventh-round pick (No. 256; [Nick Gargiulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Gargiulo "Nick Gargiulo")) from the Jets in exchange for a 2024 sixth-round pick (No. 203; the [Minnesota Vikings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota_Vikings "Minnesota Vikings") selected [Will Reichard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_Reichard "Will Reichard")).[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-58) The Broncos declined the fifth-year option on Wilson's contract, making him a free agent after the 2024 season.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-e530-59) Denver announced that Wilson would begin the season as the team’s third-string quarterback, behind [Bo Nix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bo_Nix "Bo Nix") and [Jarrett Stidham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jarrett_Stidham "Jarrett Stidham").[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-60) He did not appear in a game during the season.

### Miami Dolphins

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zach_Wilson&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Miami Dolphins")]

On March 17, 2025, Wilson signed a one-year, $6 million contract with the [Miami Dolphins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_Dolphins "Miami Dolphins").[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-61)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-62) Wilson appeared in four games for Miami, completing six of his 11 pass attempts for 32 yards.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-63)

### New Orleans Saints

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zach_Wilson&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: New Orleans Saints")]

On March 26, 2026, Wilson signed a one-year, $1.4 million contract with the [New Orleans Saints](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans_Saints "New Orleans Saints").[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-64)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zach_Wilson&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Wilson was born to Michael and Lisa Wilson ([née](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birth_name#Maiden_and_married_names "Birth name")Neeleman) and has three brothers, one of whom is college quarterback [Isaac Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isaac_Wilson_(American_football) "Isaac Wilson (American football)"), and two sisters.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-66)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-Neeleman-9) He is part [Hawaiian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_Hawaiians "Native Hawaiians") on his father's side, with his middle name [Kapono](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kapono "Kapono") meaning "righteous" in the [Hawaiian language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaiian_language "Hawaiian language").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-Hawaiian-4)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-Neeleman-9) Some other members of his family include airline entrepreneur [David Neeleman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Neeleman "David Neeleman") and [HealthEquity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HealthEquity "HealthEquity") co-founder Stephen Neeleman.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-Neeleman-9)

Wilson was diagnosed with [attention deficit hyperactivity disorder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attention_deficit_hyperactivity_disorder "Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder") (ADHD) as a child, a trait that runs in his family.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-Neeleman-9)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-Church-67) Wilson was baptized as a member of [the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Church_of_Jesus_Christ_of_Latter-day_Saints "The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints"). He has said that he "didn't grow up active in the church [and] was never really a churchgoer..." He considers himself a spiritual person, telling _[Deseret News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deseret\_News "Deseret News")_ "I have always had a good relationship with God in my life."[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-Church-67)

Wilson has been friends with former BYU Cougars teammate [Dax Milne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dax_Milne "Dax Milne") since childhood.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-68)

In June 2024, Wilson announced his engagement to girlfriend Nicolette Dellanno.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-69) On June 28, 2025, Wilson and Dellanno were married in New York City.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zach_Wilson#cite_note-70)

The **2020 NFL draft** was the 85th annual meeting of [National Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League") (NFL) franchises to select newly eligible players for the [2020 NFL season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_NFL_season "2020 NFL season"). The first round was held on April 23, followed by the second and third rounds on April 24. The draft concluded with rounds 4–7 on April 25. The NFL originally planned to hold the event live in [Paradise, Nevada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paradise,_Nevada "Paradise, Nevada"), before all public events related to it were canceled due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"). Instead, all team selections took place via [videoconferencing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Videoconferencing "Videoconferencing") with league commissioner [Roger Goodell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Goodell "Roger Goodell") announcing picks from his home.

The [Washington Redskins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Redskins "Washington Redskins") retired their name two months after the 2020 draft, making it the final draft where players were selected under the Redskins branding. The draft is noteworthy for producing five playoff starters at the [quarterback](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quarterback "Quarterback") position: [Joe Burrow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow "Joe Burrow"), [Tua Tagovailoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tua_Tagovailoa "Tua Tagovailoa"), [Justin Herbert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert "Justin Herbert"), [Jordan Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan_Love "Jordan Love") and [Jalen Hurts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jalen_Hurts "Jalen Hurts"). Burrow became the first to reach a Super Bowl in [Super Bowl LVI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LVI "Super Bowl LVI"), while Hurts became the first Super Bowl–winner of the group in [Super Bowl LIX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LIX "Super Bowl LIX").

## Format

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2020_NFL_draft&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Format")]

The host city was chosen among finalists [Denver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver "Denver"), [Kansas City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City,_Missouri "Kansas City, Missouri"), [Las Vegas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas "Las Vegas"), [Nashville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nashville "Nashville") and [Cleveland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland "Cleveland")/[Canton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canton,_Ohio "Canton, Ohio") in May 2018 during the NFL Spring League Meeting,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_NFL_draft#cite_note-1) when Nashville was chosen to host the [2019 draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_NFL_draft "2019 NFL draft"). However, the host city for 2020 was deferred. After Denver withdrew, citing scheduling conflicts,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_NFL_draft#cite_note-2) Las Vegas was chosen as the original host on December 12, 2018, coinciding with the [Las Vegas Raiders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas_Raiders "Las Vegas Raiders")' [arrival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oakland_Raiders_relocation_to_Las_Vegas "Oakland Raiders relocation to Las Vegas") in the city.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_NFL_draft#cite_note-3) Plans were announced for a main stage near the [Caesars Forum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caesars_Forum "Caesars Forum") convention center and a "[red carpet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_carpet "Red carpet")" stage for arrivals on a floating platform in front of the [Bellagio resort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bellagio_resort "Bellagio resort"), with players being transported to and from the stage by boat.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_NFL_draft#cite_note-4) However, due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_the_United_States "COVID-19 pandemic in the United States"), the NFL announced on March 16 that it had canceled all public festivities associated with the event.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_NFL_draft#cite_note-5)

Instead, the draft was held remotely, with team coaches and GMs convening via [Microsoft Teams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft_Teams "Microsoft Teams") due to all team facilities also being closed.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_NFL_draft#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_NFL_draft#cite_note-7) NFL commissioner [Roger Goodell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Goodell "Roger Goodell") announced the picks for rounds 1–3 from his home in [Bronxville, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronxville,_New_York "Bronxville, New York"), with the rest of the rounds being announced by [Dave Gardi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Gardi "Dave Gardi").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_NFL_draft#cite_note-variety-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_NFL_draft#cite_note-9) During the event Goodell announced that Las Vegas would host the [2022 NFL draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NFL_draft "2022 NFL draft").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_NFL_draft#cite_note-10)

The **2020 NFL draft** was the 85th annual meeting of [National Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League") (NFL) franchises to select newly eligible players for the [2020 NFL season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_NFL_season "2020 NFL season"). The first round was held on April 23, followed by the second and third rounds on April 24. The draft concluded with rounds 4–7 on April 25. The NFL originally planned to hold the event live in [Paradise, Nevada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paradise,_Nevada "Paradise, Nevada"), before all public events related to it were canceled due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"). Instead, all team selections took place via [videoconferencing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Videoconferencing "Videoconferencing") with league commissioner [Roger Goodell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Goodell "Roger Goodell") announcing picks from his home.

The [Washington Redskins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Redskins "Washington Redskins") retired their name two months after the 2020 draft, making it the final draft where players were selected under the Redskins branding. The draft is noteworthy for producing five playoff starters at the [quarterback](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quarterback "Quarterback") position: [Joe Burrow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow "Joe Burrow"), [Tua Tagovailoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tua_Tagovailoa "Tua Tagovailoa"), [Justin Herbert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert "Justin Herbert"), [Jordan Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan_Love "Jordan Love") and [Jalen Hurts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jalen_Hurts "Jalen Hurts"). Burrow became the first to reach a Super Bowl in [Super Bowl LVI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LVI "Super Bowl LVI"), while Hurts became the first Super Bowl–winner of the group in [Super Bowl LIX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LIX "Super Bowl LIX").

## Format

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2020_NFL_draft&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Format")]

The host city was chosen among finalists [Denver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver "Denver"), [Kansas City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City,_Missouri "Kansas City, Missouri"), [Las Vegas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas "Las Vegas"), [Nashville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nashville "Nashville") and [Cleveland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland "Cleveland")/[Canton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canton,_Ohio "Canton, Ohio") in May 2018 during the NFL Spring League Meeting,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_NFL_draft#cite_note-1) when Nashville was chosen to host the [2019 draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_NFL_draft "2019 NFL draft"). However, the host city for 2020 was deferred. After Denver withdrew, citing scheduling conflicts,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_NFL_draft#cite_note-2) Las Vegas was chosen as the original host on December 12, 2018, coinciding with the [Las Vegas Raiders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas_Raiders "Las Vegas Raiders")' [arrival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oakland_Raiders_relocation_to_Las_Vegas "Oakland Raiders relocation to Las Vegas") in the city.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_NFL_draft#cite_note-3) Plans were announced for a main stage near the [Caesars Forum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caesars_Forum "Caesars Forum") convention center and a "[red carpet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_carpet "Red carpet")" stage for arrivals on a floating platform in front of the [Bellagio resort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bellagio_resort "Bellagio resort"), with players being transported to and from the stage by boat.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_NFL_draft#cite_note-4) However, due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_the_United_States "COVID-19 pandemic in the United States"), the NFL announced on March 16 that it had canceled all public festivities associated with the event.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_NFL_draft#cite_note-5)

Instead, the draft was held remotely, with team coaches and GMs convening via [Microsoft Teams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft_Teams "Microsoft Teams") due to all team facilities also being closed.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_NFL_draft#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_NFL_draft#cite_note-7) NFL commissioner [Roger Goodell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Goodell "Roger Goodell") announced the picks for rounds 1–3 from his home in [Bronxville, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronxville,_New_York "Bronxville, New York"), with the rest of the rounds being announced by [Dave Gardi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Gardi "Dave Gardi").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_NFL_draft#cite_note-variety-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_NFL_draft#cite_note-9) During the event Goodell announced that Las Vegas would host the [2022 NFL draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NFL_draft "2022 NFL draft").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_NFL_draft#cite_note-10)
