### Chicago Bears

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Justin_Fields&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Chicago Bears")]

#### 2021 season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Justin_Fields&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: 2021 season")]

See also: [2021 Chicago Bears season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Chicago_Bears_season "2021 Chicago Bears season")

Fields was selected 11th overall in the 2021 NFL draft by the [Chicago Bears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Bears "Chicago Bears"), who traded up with the [New York Giants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Giants "New York Giants") in exchange for the 20th overall pick, their fifth-round pick in 2021, and their first and fourth-round picks in 2022.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-34) A top quarterback prospect in the draft, Fields was one of five taken in the first round. He signed his four-year rookie contract, worth $18.8 million fully guaranteed, on June 10, 2021.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-35)

Although Fields was named the second-string quarterback behind [Andy Dalton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Dalton "Andy Dalton"), he made his NFL debut in the season opener against the [Los Angeles Rams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Rams "Los Angeles Rams"), taking the field on four plays. He scored a five-yard rushing touchdown and completed two passes for 10 yards in the 34–14 defeat.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-36) After Dalton suffered a knee injury in Week 2 against the [Cincinnati Bengals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cincinnati_Bengals "Cincinnati Bengals"), Fields entered the game in the third quarter. Fields completed 6 of 13 passes for 60 yards with one interception, while also rushing for 31 yards, as the Bears won 20–17.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-Replaces-37) With Dalton sidelined from his injury, Fields was named the starter in the following week's matchup against the [Cleveland Browns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland_Browns "Cleveland Browns").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-38) His starting debut saw him sacked 9 times, 4.5 of which were delivered by defensive end [Myles Garrett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Myles_Garrett "Myles Garrett"), while completing 6 of 20 passes for 68 yards. The Bears, who finished with 47 yards of offense, lost 26–6.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-39)

Fields won in his second career start the next week in a 24–14 victory against the [Detroit Lions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detroit_Lions "Detroit Lions"). He completed 11 of 17 passes for 209 yards and had one interception off a deflected pass.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-BrandNew-40) After Fields was named the starter for the remainder of the season, he led the Bears to a 20–9 victory over the [Las Vegas Raiders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas_Raiders "Las Vegas Raiders") in Week 5, completing 12 of 20 passes for 111 yards and throwing his first touchdown pass to tight end [Jesper Horsted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesper_Horsted "Jesper Horsted").[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-CommitsTo-41)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-OutplayVegas-42) In Week 7 against the [Tampa Bay Buccaneers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tampa_Bay_Buccaneers "Tampa Bay Buccaneers"), Fields committed 5 turnovers – 3 interceptions and 2 lost fumbles – as the Bears were defeated 38–3.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-FiveTurnovers-43) Fields had his first 100-yard rushing game the next week against the [San Francisco 49ers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco_49ers "San Francisco 49ers"), throwing for 175 yards and a touchdown, and also scored a rushing touchdown. However, the game ended in a 33–22 defeat, with Fields throwing an interception on the Bears' final drive.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-BrilliantTD-44) In the following week's _[Monday Night Football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monday\_Night\_Football "Monday Night Football")_ matchup with the [Pittsburgh Steelers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_Steelers "Pittsburgh Steelers"), Fields threw for a career-high 291 yards, but despite rallying to give the Bears a 27–26 lead in the fourth quarter, the Steelers pulled away to win 29–27.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-45)

In Week 11 against the [Baltimore Ravens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltimore_Ravens "Baltimore Ravens"), Fields exited the game in the third quarter with an injury to his ribs. He was replaced by Dalton in the 16–13 loss.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-RibsInjury-46) After the game, it was announced Fields had multiple cracked ribs, which forced him to miss the Bears' next two matchups.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-47)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-RibsHurt-48) He returned in a Week 14 loss to the [Green Bay Packers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Bay_Packers "Green Bay Packers"), but an ankle injury in the following week's defeat to the [Minnesota Vikings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota_Vikings "Minnesota Vikings") sidelined him for another two games.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-LimitedInjury-49) Fields tested positive for [COVID-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19 "COVID-19") ahead of the season finale, making the Week 15 game the last of his rookie year.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-50) He finished the season fifth in quarterback rushing yards at 420, the most among rookies, but also had the third-most quarterback fumbles at 12 and the second-most lost fumbles at 5.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-RookieGrades-51)

#### 2022 season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Justin_Fields&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: 2022 season")]

See also: [2022 Chicago Bears season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Chicago_Bears_season "2022 Chicago Bears season")

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/98/Justin_Fields_2022_Bears_Camp.jpg/250px-Justin_Fields_2022_Bears_Camp.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Justin_Fields_2022_Bears_Camp.jpg)

Fields (right) with a Bears fan at [training camp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Training_camp_(NFL) "Training camp (NFL)") in 2022

Fields' 2022 season began with a comeback 19–10 victory over the 49ers, completing 8 of 17 passes for 121 yards, two touchdowns, and an interception.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-52) The Bears lost four of their next five games, including a three-game losing streak, which saw Fields complete 56.1% of his passes for 748 yards, two touchdowns, and four interceptions, and rush for 254 yards on 43 carries.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-53) The losing streak ended in Week 7 with a _Monday Night Football_ victory over the [New England Patriots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_England_Patriots "New England Patriots"), during which Fields completed 13 of 21 passes for 179 yards, a touchdown, and an interception, and rushed for 82 yards and a touchdown on 14 carries to secure the 33–14 upset.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-54)

In Week 9 against the [Miami Dolphins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_Dolphins "Miami Dolphins"), Fields set the NFL single-game regular season record for quarterback rushing yards at 178, surpassing [Michael Vick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Vick "Michael Vick")'s 20-year record.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-55) He also became the first NFL player to have three touchdown passes and rush for at least 150 yards in the same game and scored the Bears franchise's longest quarterback rushing touchdown at 61 yards.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-56) Although the Bears lost 35–32, Fields was named NFC Offensive Player of the Week.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-57)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-58) In the next week's matchup with the Lions, Fields became the first NFL quarterback to rush for 140 yards in consecutive games and the first in the Super Bowl era to have multiple rushing touchdowns of over 60 yards. However, the Bears lost 31–30.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-MonsterPerformance-59)

During a Week 11 loss to the [Atlanta Falcons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta_Falcons "Atlanta Falcons"), Fields suffered an injury to his non-throwing shoulder, which sidelined him for a week.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-60)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-61) He returned in Week 13 against the Packers and became the first quarterback in the Super Bowl era to rush for a touchdown in six consecutive games, although the Bears would lose 28–19.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-62) Fields suffered a hip injury in a Week 17 loss to the Lions, which caused him to miss the season finale against the Vikings.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-63) Fields and the Bears would not win another game in 2022 after their Week 7 victory, dropping the team to a league-worst 3–14 record.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-2022ReportCard-64)

Fields finished his second year with 1,143 rushing yards, making him the third NFL quarterback after Vick and [Lamar Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lamar_Jackson "Lamar Jackson") to rush for 1,000 yards in a season.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-65) However, he also led the league in sacks taken at 55 and fumbles at 16.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-66)[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-67) He was ranked 86th by his fellow players on the [NFL Top 100 Players of 2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_Top_100_Players_of_2023 "NFL Top 100 Players of 2023").[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-68)

#### 2023 season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Justin_Fields&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: 2023 season")]

See also: [2023 Chicago Bears season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Chicago_Bears_season "2023 Chicago Bears season")

Fields' [2023 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Chicago_Bears_season "2023 Chicago Bears season") began with a 38–20 loss against the Packers, completing 24 of 37 passes for 216 yards, one touchdown, and an interception that became a pick-six. In Week 2 against the Buccaneers, Fields completed 16 passes on 29 attempts for 211 yards, and one touchdown to two interceptions. With the loss, the Bears started 0–2 for the first time since [2017](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Chicago_Bears_season "2017 Chicago Bears season"). In Week 3, the Bears traveled to [Arrowhead Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arrowhead_Stadium "Arrowhead Stadium") in [Kansas City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City "Kansas City") to face [Patrick Mahomes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Mahomes "Patrick Mahomes") and the [Kansas City Chiefs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City_Chiefs "Kansas City Chiefs"), losing 41–10. Fields completed 11 passes on 22 attempts for 99 yards, one touchdown, and an interception, and rushed 11 times for 47 yards. The Bears started 0–3 for the first time since [2016](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Chicago_Bears_season "2016 Chicago Bears season").[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-69) Despite suffering a head injury, Fields did not miss a play.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-70)

In Week 4 against the [Denver Broncos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver_Broncos "Denver Broncos"), Fields started a perfect 16 for 16 in the first half, which was a Bears franchise record. Fields also had his first career 300-yard passing game. Fields and the Bears had a 28–7 lead in the 3rd quarter, but ultimately lost 31–28. In the fourth quarter, a fumble by Fields was recovered for a touchdown by [Jonathon Cooper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathon_Cooper "Jonathon Cooper"). In total, Fields completed 28 of 35 passes for 335 yards, and threw four touchdown passes and one interception.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-71) The following week against the [Washington Commanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Commanders "Washington Commanders"), Fields would finally lead the Bears to their first win of the year, a 40–20 victory that saw Fields toss four touchdowns for the second straight week, three of which were to star wideout [D. J. Moore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D._J._Moore "D. J. Moore").[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-72)

In Week 6 against the Vikings, Fields struggled mightily, being pressured constantly and only completing 6 of his 10 passes for 58 yards and an interception along with 4 sacks. Early in the third quarter, Fields dislocated his shoulder and thumb while being sacked by [Danielle Hunter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danielle_Hunter "Danielle Hunter") and was replaced by undrafted rookie [Tyson Bagent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyson_Bagent "Tyson Bagent") for the rest of the game as the Bears lost 19–13 to fall to 1–5. Fields would go on to miss the next four games. He returned in Week 11 against the Lions, in which the Bears took a 26–14 lead late in the fourth quarter, but ended up losing, dropping to 3–8. Fields finished the game with 169 yards passing and a touchdown while also rushing eighteen times for a team-high 104 yards. Fields and the Bears then played the Vikings on _Monday Night Football_ in Week 12, where the Bears won 12–10 off a game-winning field goal with 10 seconds left. Fields threw for 217 yards, including the 36-yard pass to [DJ Moore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D._J._Moore "D. J. Moore") that put the Bears in field goal range late in the 4th quarter, and rushed for an additional 59 yards.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-73)

Fields finished his third season setting career-highs in completion percentage (61.4%) and passing yards (2,562) along with throwing a career-low nine interceptions.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-74) With the Bears holding the first overall pick in the 2024 NFL draft, Fields headed into the offseason facing uncertainty about his future as the team's starting quarterback, with questions arising over whether Chicago would stick with Fields or select a new quarterback in the draft.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-75)

### Pittsburgh Steelers

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Justin_Fields&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Pittsburgh Steelers")]

See also: [2024 Pittsburgh Steelers season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Pittsburgh_Steelers_season "2024 Pittsburgh Steelers season")

On March 16, 2024, Fields was traded to the [Pittsburgh Steelers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_Steelers "Pittsburgh Steelers") in exchange for a conditional sixth-round pick in the [2025 NFL draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_NFL_draft "2025 NFL draft") that would have converted to a fourth if he played 51% of the team's snaps, however, he played in less than the said threshold, failing the condition to convert it to a fourth.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-76)[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-77) The Steelers declined the fifth-year option on Fields' contract, making him a free agent after the 2024 season.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-78) Following a preseason quarterback competition between Fields and [Russell Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russell_Wilson "Russell Wilson"), the Steelers announced that Fields would back up Wilson to start the season.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-79) Prior to Week 1, Wilson reaggravated a calf injury during practice. He was later ruled out, thrusting Fields into the starting role for the season opener against the [Atlanta Falcons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta_Falcons "Atlanta Falcons").[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-80) He completed 17-of-23 pass attempts for 156 yards, zero touchdowns, and zero turnovers. He also added 57 rushing yards as the Steelers won 18–10.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-81) With Wilson still not cleared to play in Week 2 against the [Denver Broncos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver_Broncos "Denver Broncos"), Fields was once again named the team's starter. During the game, Fields committed no turnovers and scored his first touchdown as a Steeler on a five yard pass to tight end [Darnell Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darnell_Washington "Darnell Washington"). The Steelers would defeat the Broncos with a final score of 13-6, giving Fields his second consecutive win as the Steelers' starting quarterback.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-82) His style of play through his three starts as a dynamic quarterback drew comparisons with former Steelers quarterback/wide receiver [Kordell Stewart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kordell_Stewart "Kordell Stewart").[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-83) Through his first three starts with the Steelers, Fields completed 73.3% of his passes (55 of 75), averaging 6.9 yards per throw and committed one turnover against three total touchdowns, two passing and one rushing.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-84) This marks the first time in Fields' professional career where he has led his team to three straight wins in the starting position.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-i975-85) Fields would follow up his three straight victories with two straight losses to the [Indianapolis Colts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Indianapolis_Colts_season "2024 Indianapolis Colts season") and [Dallas Cowboys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Dallas_Cowboys_season "2024 Dallas Cowboys season") with a combined three touchdowns and 443 passing yards.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-86)

On October 15, 2024, Fields was demoted to backup quarterback duties as Wilson's calf injury had healed.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-h572-87) The change at quarterback came following a Steelers 32–13 win over the [Las Vegas Raiders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Las_Vegas_Raiders_season "2024 Las Vegas Raiders season") in which Fields completed 14-of-24 passes for 145 yards, committing no turnovers and scoring two rushing touchdowns.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-88) During Week 11's 18–16 victory over the [Baltimore Ravens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Baltimore_Ravens_season "2024 Baltimore Ravens season"), Fields returned to the quarterback position for one play. In the closing seconds of regulation, Fields took a snap and ran to his left before sliding just a yard shy of a [first down](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_down "First down") to run time off the [play clock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Play_clock "Play clock") and secure a Steelers victory.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-i775-89)

Throughout much of the season following his benching, Fields was utilized in multiple "package plays" that typically included quarterback sneak plays and blitz-countering scramble short passes, typically to convert third and fourth downs.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-p585-90) He finished the 2024 season completing 65% of his passes for 1,106 yards, 10 total touchdowns (five passing, five rushing) and just one interception. He appeared in 10 total games, starting six. He briefly appeared in two package plays during the Steelers' 28–14 loss to the [Baltimore Ravens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltimore_Ravens "Baltimore Ravens") in AFC Wild Card playoff game, handing off the ball to [Jaylen Warren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaylen_Warren "Jaylen Warren") on an read pass option play as well as throwing an incomplete pass intended for [Darnell Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darnell_Washington "Darnell Washington").[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-f871-91)

### New York Jets

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Justin_Fields&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: New York Jets")]

On March 13, 2025, Fields signed a two-year, $40 million contract with the [New York Jets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Jets "New York Jets").[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-92)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-93)[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-94) On March 30, general manager [Darren Mougey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darren_Mougey "Darren Mougey") announced Fields would be the team's starting quarterback.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-95) On October 12, against the [Denver Broncos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Denver_Broncos_season "2025 Denver Broncos season"), Fields threw for only 45 yards in a full game of action in what [ESPN.com](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ESPN.com "ESPN.com") called the "worst passing performance in New York Jets history".[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-Cimini-96)[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-10-12-2025-97) The Jets' -10 net passing yards (which includes nine sacks for 55 yards) was the worst in the NFL since the [San Diego Chargers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego_Chargers "San Diego Chargers") had -19 net passing yards on September 20, 1998.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-Cimini-96)[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-10-12-2025-97)

After a winless start to the season through seven games, Jets owner [Woody Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woody_Johnson "Woody Johnson") criticized Fields' play, saying that it was "hard" to win "when you have a quarterback with a rating that he's got."[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-98) Following the 0–7 start, the Jets won back-to-back games over the [Cincinnati Bengals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Cincinnati_Bengals_season "2025 Cincinnati Bengals season") and [Cleveland Browns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Cleveland_Browns_season "2025 Cleveland Browns season"), with a bye week in between. The team then lost to the [New England Patriots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_New_England_Patriots_season "2025 New England Patriots season"), and Fields was benched the following week in favor of [Tyrod Taylor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyrod_Taylor "Tyrod Taylor") for the team's Week 12 matchup against the [Baltimore Ravens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Baltimore_Ravens_season "2025 Baltimore Ravens season").[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-99) After dealing with knee soreness, he was subsequently ruled out for the team's Week 14 matchup against the [Miami Dolphins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Miami_Dolphins_season "2025 Miami Dolphins season").[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-100) Fields was placed on injured reserve on December 23, ending his season.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-101)

### Kansas City Chiefs

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Justin_Fields&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Kansas City Chiefs")]

On March 18, 2026, the Jets traded Fields to the [Kansas City Chiefs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City_Chiefs "Kansas City Chiefs") in exchange for a sixth-round pick in the [2027 NFL draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2027_NFL_draft "2027 NFL draft").[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-102) As part of the trade negotiations, the Jets agreed to pay $8 million to Fields while the Chiefs will pay him $3 million totaling $11 million in guarantees.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-103)

### Records

NFL records
*   Most rushing yards by a quarterback in a single game: 178 (November 6, 2022, vs. [Miami Dolphins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Miami_Dolphins_season "2022 Miami Dolphins season"))[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-104)
*   Most rushing yards by a quarterback over a five-game span in the Super Bowl era: 568 ([2022](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NFL_season "2022 NFL season"))[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-Records-105)
*   Most consecutive games by a quarterback with a rushing touchdown: 6 (2022)[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-106)
    *   Tied with [Johnny Lujack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Lujack "Johnny Lujack") ([1950](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1950_NFL_season "1950 NFL season"))

*   Most consecutive games with 1+ rushing and passing touchdown: 5 (2022)[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-Records-105)
    *   Tied with [Kyler Murray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyler_Murray "Kyler Murray") ([2020](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_NFL_season "2020 NFL season"))

*   First player to rush for 140+ yards and throw 3+ touchdowns in a single game (November 6, 2022, vs. Miami Dolphins)[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-107)
*   First player to rush for 100+ yards, throw 2+ touchdowns, and rush for 2+ touchdowns in a single game (November 13, 2022, vs. [Detroit Lions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Detroit_Lions_season "2022 Detroit Lions season"))[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-Records-105)
*   Only quarterback in the Super Bowl era with multiple 60+ yard rushing touchdowns[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-108)
*   Only quarterback since [1925](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1925_NFL_season "1925 NFL season") to score three rushing touchdowns over 50 yards[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-Records-105)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Justin_Fields&action=edit&section=25 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Fields is a [Christian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian "Christian").[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-109) Fields was diagnosed with [epilepsy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epilepsy "Epilepsy") as a freshman in high school. His condition was made public during his pre-draft interviews with NFL teams in 2021.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-110)[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-111) In high school, he had a score of 29 on his [ACT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACT_(test) "ACT (test)") and held a 3.9 [grade point average](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grade_point_average "Grade point average").[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-112) Fields is a [pescetarian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pescetarianism "Pescetarianism").[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-113) His sister, Jaiden, played [college softball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_softball "College softball") for [Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_Bulldogs_softball "Georgia Bulldogs softball"), while his youngest sister, Jessica, plays [college basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_basketball "College basketball") for [Michigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michigan_Wolverines_women's_basketball "Michigan Wolverines women's basketball").[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-114)[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-115) Fields graduated with a degree in consumer and family financial services from Ohio State in May 2023.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-116)[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Fields#cite_note-117)

**Joseph Lee Burrow** (born December 10, 1996) is an American professional [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_football "American football") player who is a [quarterback](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quarterback "Quarterback") for the [Cincinnati Bengals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cincinnati_Bengals "Cincinnati Bengals") of the [National Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League") (NFL). After three seasons of [college football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_football "College football") with the [Ohio State Buckeyes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohio_State_Buckeyes_football "Ohio State Buckeyes football"), he played two seasons for the [LSU Tigers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LSU_Tigers_football "LSU Tigers football"), winning the [Heisman Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heisman_Trophy "Heisman Trophy") and the [College Football Playoff National Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_College_Football_Playoff_National_Championship "2020 College Football Playoff National Championship") in 2019. He was selected by the Bengals [first overall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_first_overall_NFL_draft_picks "List of first overall NFL draft picks") in the 2020 NFL draft.

Burrow had a breakout season in 2021 when he led the Bengals to their first playoff win since 1990, ending the longest active drought in the [four major North American sports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_professional_sports_leagues_in_the_United_States_and_Canada "Major professional sports leagues in the United States and Canada"), and an appearance in [Super Bowl LVI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LVI "Super Bowl LVI"), and was awarded [Comeback Player of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_Comeback_Player_of_the_Year "NFL Comeback Player of the Year"). In 2023, Burrow signed, at the time, the [largest contract in NFL history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_largest_sports_contracts "List of largest sports contracts") in terms of annual salary and led the Bengals to their first consecutive division title in franchise history. Despite Cincinnati missing the playoffs in 2024, Burrow led the league in passing yards and passing touchdowns and was awarded his second Comeback Player of the Year Award. Burrow has been nicknamed "**Joe Cool**" and "**Joe Brrr**" by sportswriters and other players for his calmness under pressure.

## Early life

Burrow was born in [Ames, Iowa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ames,_Iowa "Ames, Iowa"), on December 10, 1996,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-5)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-6) the son of Robin and [Jim Burrow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Burrow "Jim Burrow"). Jim is a former football player and coach whose career lasted over 40 years.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-7) Burrow was born while his father was on the coaching staff at [Iowa State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_Iowa_State_Cyclones_football_team "1996 Iowa State Cyclones football team").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-8) According to a 2019 _[Sports Illustrated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports\_Illustrated "Sports Illustrated")_ story, "The Burrow athletic lineage dates back nearly a century." In the 1940s, his paternal grandmother set a Mississippi state high school record with an 82-point game in basketball.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-9)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-10) His paternal grandfather played basketball at [Mississippi State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mississippi_State_Bulldogs_men's_basketball "Mississippi State Bulldogs men's basketball"); his uncle, John Burrow, played football at [Ole Miss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ole_Miss_Rebels_football "Ole Miss Rebels football") (the [University of Mississippi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Mississippi "University of Mississippi")); and two older brothers also played football at [Nebraska](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nebraska_Cornhuskers_football "Nebraska Cornhuskers football").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-Dellenger-11)

He attended the [2002 Rose Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_Rose_Bowl "2002 Rose Bowl") at age five, because his father was an assistant coach for the [University of Nebraska](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_Nebraska_Cornhuskers_football_team "2001 Nebraska Cornhuskers football team") in [Lincoln](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lincoln,_Nebraska "Lincoln, Nebraska"). Not long after, he began playing in youth football leagues. Unlike his father, uncle, and brothers, who all played on defense, Burrow started out as a quarterback, because his first youth team had no one else who could play the position.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-Dellenger-11) The Burrow family moved to [North Dakota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Dakota "North Dakota") in 2003 when his father was hired as the defensive coordinator at [North Dakota State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2003_North_Dakota_State_Bison_football_team "2003 North Dakota State Bison football team") in [Fargo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fargo,_North_Dakota "Fargo, North Dakota"). One day, while Jim was visiting his office, future [Central Michigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Michigan_Chippewas_football "Central Michigan Chippewas football") head coach [Dan Enos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Enos "Dan Enos") commented that the seven-year-old Joe had a future in football.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-12) The Burrows spent two years in Fargo before Jim accepted the defensive coordinator position at [Ohio University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_Ohio_Bobcats_football_team "2005 Ohio Bobcats football team") in [Athens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athens,_Ohio "Athens, Ohio").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-13)

Burrow attended [Athens High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athens_High_School_(Ohio) "Athens High School (Ohio)") (2011–2014) in [The Plains, Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Plains,_Ohio "The Plains, Ohio"), leading the school to three straight playoff appearances and the school's first seven playoff victories in school history.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-lsu_bio-14) During his career, he passed for 11,416 yards with 157 passing [touchdowns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Touchdowns "Touchdowns") and rushed for 2,067 yards with 27 rushing touchdowns.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-15) He was awarded the state's [Mr. Football Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr._Football_Award_(Ohio) "Mr. Football Award (Ohio)") and Gatorade Player of the Year award as a senior in 2014. He and his Bulldog teammates went 14–1 that season. He was also a standout basketball player, and was named first-team all-state at point guard his senior year.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-lsu_bio-14) Burrow was rated as a four-star football recruit, and was the eighth-highest ranked [dual-threat quarterback](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dual-threat_quarterback "Dual-threat quarterback") in the class of 2015, according to the [247Sports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/247Sports "247Sports") Composite.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-16) He committed to [Ohio State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohio_State_Buckeyes_football "Ohio State Buckeyes football") to play football on May 27, 2014.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-17)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-18)

In December 2019, the Athens City School District school board unanimously approved a measure to rename the school's football stadium in honor of Burrow.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-19) Burrow's connection with the area remains strong as such that during the 2020 NFL draft, he wore a T-shirt with the number [740](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Area_code_740 "Area code 740") in reference to the [area code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Area_code "Area code") for Athens as well as [Appalachian Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appalachian_Ohio "Appalachian Ohio") in general.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-20)

## College career

### Ohio State

After [redshirting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Redshirt_(college_sports) "Redshirt (college sports)") his first year at Ohio State in 2015, Burrow spent the next two years as a backup to [J. T. Barrett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._T._Barrett "J. T. Barrett"), during which he played in 10 games, completing 29 of 39 passes for 287 yards and two touchdowns.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-21) In 2016, Burrow and [Dwayne Haskins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwayne_Haskins "Dwayne Haskins") were backups for Barrett in that season's [CFP Semifinal at the Fiesta Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Fiesta_Bowl_(December) "2016 Fiesta Bowl (December)") against [Clemson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Clemson_Tigers_football_team "2016 Clemson Tigers football team").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-22)

During Ohio State's spring game in 2018, Burrow completed 15 of 22 pass attempts for 238 yards and two touchdowns.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-Bender-23) The game was further part of Ohio State's competition for the starting quarterback position, contested by Burrow, [Tate Martell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tate_Martell "Tate Martell"), and Dwayne Haskins.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-Bender-23) Following the game, Burrow told reporters "I didn't come here to sit on the bench for four years. I know I'm a pretty good quarterback. I want to play somewhere."[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-Bender-23) Realizing that Haskins would be named starting quarterback at Ohio State, Burrow transferred to [Louisiana State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana_State_University "Louisiana State University") (LSU) on May 18, 2018.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-24)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-25) Burrow had graduated from Ohio State in three years with a degree in consumer and family financial services, and was immediately eligible as a graduate transfer.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-fox_starter-26)

#### 2018

In his first year at LSU, Burrow was named the starting quarterback as a redshirt junior in [2018](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_LSU_Tigers_football_team "2018 LSU Tigers football team").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-fox_starter-26) In an early season road trip to then-No. 7 [Auburn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Auburn_Tigers_football_team "2018 Auburn Tigers football team"), Burrow threw for 249 yards and a touchdown en route to a 22–21 win. He was named the [Southeastern Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southeastern_Conference "Southeastern Conference") (SEC) Offensive Player of the Week following the victory.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-27) He again earned SEC Offensive Player of the Week honors following a 292-yard, three-touchdown performance against [Ole Miss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Ole_Miss_Rebels_football_team "2018 Ole Miss Rebels football team") two weeks later.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-28) Burrow played in [LSU's 7-overtime and 5-hour long loss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_LSU_vs._Texas_A&M_football_game "2018 LSU vs. Texas A&M football game") to [Texas A&M](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Texas_A&M_Aggies_football_team "2018 Texas A&M Aggies football team").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-Dellenger2019-07-29) After the game, Burrow experienced fatigue and had to receive [IV therapy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intravenous_therapy "Intravenous therapy") from trainers.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-Dellenger2019-07-29) Burrow helped lead the Tigers to a 10–3 record, including a win over [UCF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_UCF_Knights_football_team "2018 UCF Knights football team") in the [Fiesta Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Fiesta_Bowl_(January) "2019 Fiesta Bowl (January)"), and a No. 6 ranking in the final AP Poll.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-30)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-31) Burrow finished the season with 2,894 yards passing, 16 touchdowns, and five interceptions. He added 399 rushing yards and seven rushing touchdowns.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-32)

#### 2019

Burrow (center) with LSU head coach [Ed Orgeron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ed_Orgeron "Ed Orgeron") (left) and linebacker [Patrick Queen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Queen "Patrick Queen") (right) at LSU's 2020 National Championship post-game press event

Burrow was again named LSU's starting quarterback heading into his redshirt senior season in [2019](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_LSU_Tigers_football_team "2019 LSU Tigers football team"). In the Tigers' season opener against [Georgia Southern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Georgia_Southern_Eagles_football_team "2019 Georgia Southern Eagles football team"), Burrow threw for 278 yards and five touchdowns in a 55–3 win, and was later named SEC Co-Offensive Player of the Week (with [Tua Tagovailoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tua_Tagovailoa "Tua Tagovailoa")).[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-33) In a Week 2 road trip to ninth-ranked [Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Texas_Longhorns_football_team "2019 Texas Longhorns football team"), Burrow threw for 471 yards, four touchdowns, and an interception in a 45–38 win. His 471 yards were the second-most in school history and the most since [Rohan Davey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rohan_Davey "Rohan Davey")'s 528 against Alabama in 2001.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-34) He was named Walter Camp National Offensive Player of the Week and SEC Offensive Player of the Week following the performance.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-35) Burrow earned his third SEC Offensive Player of the Week honors on September 21 during LSU's game against [Vanderbilt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Vanderbilt_Commodores_football_team "2019 Vanderbilt Commodores football team"). He threw for 398 yards and a school-record six passing touchdowns in the Tigers' 66–38 win.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-36) He became the first LSU quarterback to throw for over 350 yards in three consecutive games.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-37)

In a 42–6 win over [Utah State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Utah_State_Aggies_football_team "2019 Utah State Aggies football team"), Burrow threw for 344 yards and five touchdowns, and became the first Tiger quarterback to throw for 300-plus yards in four consecutive games.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-38) The streak came to an end the next week against seventh-ranked [Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Florida_Gators_football_team "2019 Florida Gators football team"), but Burrow's 293 yards and three touchdown passes helped lead the Tigers to another win, 42–28.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-39) The next week, in LSU's seventh game of the season, Burrow eclipsed the LSU single-season passing touchdowns record of 28 when he added four more in a win against [Mississippi State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Mississippi_State_Bulldogs_football_team "2019 Mississippi State Bulldogs football team").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-40) In their next game, Burrow led LSU against ninth-ranked [Auburn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Auburn_Tigers_football_team "2019 Auburn Tigers football team") and LSU defeated another top 10 opponent, as Burrow's 321-yard, two-total-touchdowns performance set a new school record of eight career 300-yard games.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-41)

When LSU played [Alabama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Alabama_Crimson_Tide_football_team "2019 Alabama Crimson Tide football team")[on November 9](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_LSU_vs._Alabama_football_game "2019 LSU vs. Alabama football game"), the two schools were ranked higher than they had been since they had played in the [2012 BCS National Championship Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_BCS_National_Championship_Game "2012 BCS National Championship Game"); LSU was ranked second and Alabama third when the season's inaugural [College Football Playoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_Football_Playoff "College Football Playoff") rankings had been released the prior week. The game also featured two leading candidates for the [Heisman Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heisman_Trophy "Heisman Trophy") in Burrow and Alabama quarterback [Tua Tagovailoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tua_Tagovailoa "Tua Tagovailoa").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-42) Burrow and the Tigers came away victorious in a 46–41 shootout. Burrow passed for 393 yards and three touchdowns in the game,[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-43) and was again named Walter Camp National Offensive Player of the Week and SEC Co-Offensive Player of the Week, sharing the latter with teammate [Clyde Edwards-Helaire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clyde_Edwards-Helaire "Clyde Edwards-Helaire").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-44)

The following week against [Ole Miss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Ole_Miss_Rebels_football_team "2019 Ole Miss Rebels football team"), Burrow threw for 489 yards and five touchdown passes, and his single-season passing yards surpassed the LSU record set by Rohan Davey in 2001. Burrow also set an LSU record for consecutive completed passes with 17 during the game.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-45) On November 30, Burrow and LSU secured an undefeated regular season with a 50–7 win over [Texas A&M](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Texas_A&M_Aggies_football_team "2019 Texas A&M Aggies football team"), in which Burrow threw for 352 yards and three touchdowns. During the game, he broke the SEC record for single-season passing yards – previously set by [Kentucky's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kentucky_Wildcats_football "Kentucky Wildcats football")[Tim Couch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Couch "Tim Couch") – and tied the conference record for single-season touchdowns (which had been set by [Missouri's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri_Tigers_football "Missouri Tigers football")[Drew Lock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drew_Lock "Drew Lock")).[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-46) Burrow took sole possession of the SEC single-season touchdown record the following week in the [SEC Championship Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_SEC_Championship_Game "2019 SEC Championship Game"), throwing for four touchdowns in LSU's 37–10 win over [Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Georgia_Bulldogs_football_team "2019 Georgia Bulldogs football team") that secured the Tigers' place in the College Football Playoff.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-47)

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d9/LSU_Football_at_the_White_House_%2849400533066%29.jpg/250px-LSU_Football_at_the_White_House_%2849400533066%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:LSU_Football_at_the_White_House_(49400533066).jpg)

Burrow with President [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") at the [White House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House "White House") in 2020 after winning the [Heisman Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heisman_Trophy "Heisman Trophy") and [the college football national championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NCAA_Division_I_Football_Championship "NCAA Division I Football Championship")

On December 14, 2019, Burrow was awarded the 2019 Heisman Trophy, receiving 1,846 more votes than runner-up [Jalen Hurts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jalen_Hurts "Jalen Hurts").[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-48) It was the largest victory margin in the history of the award, with Burrow receiving the highest-ever share of available points.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-49) Burrow's Heisman acceptance speech referred to the rampant poverty and [food insecurity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_insecurity "Food insecurity") affecting his hometown; shortly after his speech, the [Athens County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athens_County "Athens County") food bank was the recipient of $450,000 in donations.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-50) Burrow received many other awards during college football award season, including SEC Offensive Player of the Year,[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-51) AP Player of the Year,[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-52)[Maxwell Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxwell_Award "Maxwell Award"),[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-53)[Walter Camp Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Camp_Award "Walter Camp Award"),[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-54)[Johnny Unitas Golden Arm Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Unitas_Golden_Arm_Award "Johnny Unitas Golden Arm Award"),[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-55)[Davey O'Brien Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Davey_O'Brien_Award "Davey O'Brien Award"),[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-56)[Lombardi Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lombardi_Award "Lombardi Award"),[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-57) and [Manning Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manning_Award "Manning Award").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-58) He was named as a Unanimous All-American.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-59)

In LSU's College Football Playoff semifinal game against fourth-ranked [Oklahoma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Oklahoma_Sooners_football_team "2019 Oklahoma Sooners football team") in the [2019 Peach Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Peach_Bowl "2019 Peach Bowl"), Burrow threw for seven touchdowns during the first half of the contest and had a total of 493 passing yards – along with scoring a rushing touchdown – in a 63–28 victory for the Tigers.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-60) Burrow's eight total touchdowns were all scored within the first 35 minutes[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-61) of the 60-minute game, after which he was taken out for the sake of giving him rest.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-62) Analysts have called the performance one of the greatest in college football history.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-63)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-64)

In the [2020 National Championship Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_College_Football_Playoff_National_Championship "2020 College Football Playoff National Championship") against Clemson, Burrow threw for 463 yards with six total touchdowns, five of which were passing, which led LSU to a 42–25 victory and him being named the game's offensive MVP.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-2019Records-65) He finished his 2019 season with 60 passing touchdowns, which broke the single-season [FBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NCAA_Division_I_Football_Bowl_Subdivision "NCAA Division I Football Bowl Subdivision") record previously set by [Colt Brennan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colt_Brennan "Colt Brennan")'s 58 in 2006.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-2019Records-65)[[c]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-67) Burrow also set a FBS single-season record with 65 total touchdowns (tied by [Bailey Zappe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bailey_Zappe "Bailey Zappe") in 2021).[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-68)[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-Zappe-66) His 5,671 passing yards is now tied (with [Case Keenum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Case_Keenum "Case Keenum") in 2009) for fourth-most in an FBS season.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-2019Records-65) His [passer rating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passer_rating "Passer rating") of 202 for the season was a record at the time.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-2019Records-65)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-69) Several sportswriters deemed the season to be the greatest ever by a college quarterback.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-70)[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-71)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-72)[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-73)
