### 2020

See also: [2020 Cincinnati Bengals season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Cincinnati_Bengals_season "2020 Cincinnati Bengals season")

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/03/Joe_Burrow_Bengals.jpg/250px-Joe_Burrow_Bengals.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Joe_Burrow_Bengals.jpg)

Burrow as a rookie with the [Cincinnati Bengals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cincinnati_Bengals "Cincinnati Bengals"), 2020

Burrow was one of 58 players invited to the 2020 NFL draft, where he was selected [first overall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_first_overall_NFL_draft_picks "List of first overall NFL draft picks") by the [Cincinnati Bengals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cincinnati_Bengals "Cincinnati Bengals").[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-76)[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-77) He was the third-consecutive Heisman-winning quarterback to be selected first overall, following [Baker Mayfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baker_Mayfield "Baker Mayfield") and [Kyler Murray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyler_Murray "Kyler Murray").[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-78) Burrow signed his four-year rookie contract, worth $36.1 million, on July 31, 2020.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-79)

Burrow was the only rookie quarterback from his draft class to start on opening week.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-80) In his debut, Burrow threw for 193 passing yards and an interception, while adding 46 rushing yards and a rushing touchdown in a 16–13 loss against the [Los Angeles Chargers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Chargers "Los Angeles Chargers").[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-81) During the next game against the [Cleveland Browns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland_Browns "Cleveland Browns"), Burrow threw his first career passing touchdown, a 23-yard pass to tight end [C. J. Uzomah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Uzomah "C. J. Uzomah"). Although the Bengals lost the game, 35–30, he attempted 61 passes, completing 37 of them for 316 yards and three touchdowns, which broke the NFL record for most completions by a rookie quarterback in a single game.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-82)[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-83) Two weeks later, Burrow earned his first career win by defeating the [Jacksonville Jaguars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacksonville_Jaguars "Jacksonville Jaguars"). He also became the first rookie quarterback to throw for 300 or more yards in three straight games.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-84)

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0e/Joe_Burrow_after_injury_%282020%29.jpg/250px-Joe_Burrow_after_injury_%282020%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Joe_Burrow_after_injury_(2020).jpg)

Burrow being carted off after a knee injury in 2020

In a Week 7 game against the Browns, Burrow had 406 passing yards, three passing touchdowns, one rushing touchdown, and one interception in a 37–34 loss.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-85) He became the first rookie in NFL history with at least 400 passing yards, three passing touchdowns, and a rushing touchdown in a single game,[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-86) and had completed more passes (221) than any other player in NFL history during their first eight games.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-87)

In the second half of a Week 11 game against the [Washington Football Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Football_Team "Washington Football Team"), Burrow was hit low while throwing a pass and subsequently tore his [ACL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anterior_cruciate_ligament "Anterior cruciate ligament") and [MCL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medial_collateral_ligament "Medial collateral ligament") in his left knee, among other damage to his [PCL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Posterior_cruciate_ligament "Posterior cruciate ligament") and [meniscus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meniscus_(anatomy) "Meniscus (anatomy)").[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-88)[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-89) He was later placed on [injured reserve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Injured_reserve "Injured reserve"), ending his rookie season.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-90) Undergoing knee surgery in December, Burrow continued to review game film despite being out for the season.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-Rapien2020-12b-91)

Burrow finished his rookie outing with 264 completions against 404 attempts for 2,688 yards, 13 touchdowns and five interceptions.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-g886-92) His interception percentage of 1.2% is the fourth lowest for a rookie in NFL history (only behind [Dak Prescott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dak_Prescott "Dak Prescott"), [C. J. Stroud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud "C. J. Stroud") and [Caleb Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caleb_Williams "Caleb Williams")) and the best ever for a rookie quarterback for the Bengals in franchise history.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-f834-93) Despite his strong numbers, Burrow was only able to record a record of 2-7-1 as a rookie with the Bengals finishing their 2020 campaign with a season record of 4-11 and placing fourth in the [AFC North](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFC_North "AFC North"), missing the playoffs.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-l169-94)

### 2021

See also: [2021 Cincinnati Bengals season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Cincinnati_Bengals_season "2021 Cincinnati Bengals season")

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c0/Ravens_vs_Bengals_OCT2021_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Ravens_vs_Bengals_OCT2021_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ravens_vs_Bengals_OCT2021_(cropped).jpg)

Burrow playing against the [Baltimore Ravens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltimore_Ravens "Baltimore Ravens") at [M&T Bank Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M&T_Bank_Stadium "M&T Bank Stadium") in [Baltimore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltimore "Baltimore") in October 2021

On September 6, the Bengals confirmed Burrow had completed his rehab and would be the starter for Week 1.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-95) Burrow returned from his injury and helped lead the Bengals to a 2–1 start. In Week 4, Burrow completed 25 of 32 passes for 348 yards and two touchdowns in a 24–21 win over the Jaguars, earning AFC Offensive Player of the Week.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-96)

Against the [Baltimore Ravens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltimore_Ravens "Baltimore Ravens") in Week 16, Burrow completed 37 of 46 passes, threw for a career-high [525 yards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_500-yard_passing_games_in_the_National_Football_League "List of 500-yard passing games in the National Football League"), while also throwing four touchdowns without an interception, for a career-high 143.2 passer rating in the 41–21 win. Burrow's 525 yards were the fourth most passing yards in a game in NFL history, and broke [Boomer Esiason](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boomer_Esiason "Boomer Esiason")'s franchise record for most passing yards in a game as a result.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-97) The victory in this game was Cincinnati's ninth of the year, clinching the first winning record for the team since the [2015 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Cincinnati_Bengals_season "2015 Cincinnati Bengals season"), and put the Bengals in first place of the [AFC North](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFC_North "AFC North"). Burrow was named AFC Offensive Player of the Week as a result of his performance.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-98)

The next week against the [Kansas City Chiefs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City_Chiefs "Kansas City Chiefs"), Burrow threw for 446 yards, four touchdowns, and no interceptions in the 34–31 win. The win helped the Bengals clinch the AFC North and a playoff berth for the first time since 2015.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-99) Burrow finished the season playing in 16 games with 4,611 passing yards and 34 passing touchdowns, both franchise records.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-100) He also led the league in completion percentage (70.4%) and yards per pass attempt (8.9), but also led the league in sacks taken.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-101) He was named Comeback Player of the Year by the Associated Press and the PFWA.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-102)[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-103)

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/33/Joe_Burrow_2021_%281%29.jpg/250px-Joe_Burrow_2021_%281%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Joe_Burrow_2021_(1).jpg)

Burrow in 2021

In his playoff debut, Burrow threw for 244 yards and two touchdowns in the 26–19 win against the [Las Vegas Raiders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas_Raiders "Las Vegas Raiders") in the [Wild Card Round](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_NFL_playoffs#AFC:_Cincinnati_Bengals_26,_Las_Vegas_Raiders_19 "2021–22 NFL playoffs"), ending the Bengals' playoff win drought that had been active since the [1990 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_Cincinnati_Bengals_season "1990 Cincinnati Bengals season").[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-104) During the [Divisional Round](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_NFL_playoffs#AFC:_Cincinnati_Bengals_19,_Tennessee_Titans_16 "2021–22 NFL playoffs") against the top-seeded [Tennessee Titans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee_Titans "Tennessee Titans"), Burrow threw for 348 yards and an interception in the 19–16 win, which was the first time in franchise history the Bengals won a playoff game on the road.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-105) The victory occurred despite Burrow being sacked nine times, tying [Warren Moon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warren_Moon "Warren Moon") in 1993 for the most times sacked in a playoff game and becoming the most-sacked quarterback to win a playoff game.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-106) In the [AFC Championship Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_NFL_Playoffs#AFC:_Cincinnati_Bengals_27,_Kansas_City_Chiefs_24_(OT) "2021–22 NFL Playoffs") against the Chiefs, Burrow threw for 250 yards, two touchdowns, an interception, and helped the Bengals overcome a 21–3 deficit to win 27–24 in overtime. The 18-point comeback was tied with the [Indianapolis Colts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indianapolis_Colts "Indianapolis Colts") in 2006 for the largest in a conference championship.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-107) With the victory, the Bengals reached [Super Bowl LVI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LVI "Super Bowl LVI"), their first appearance since [Super Bowl XXIII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XXIII "Super Bowl XXIII") in [1988](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988_Cincinnati_Bengals_season "1988 Cincinnati Bengals season").[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-108)

In the Super Bowl, Burrow threw for 263 yards and a touchdown, but was sacked 7 times, ultimately losing to the [Los Angeles Rams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Rams "Los Angeles Rams") 23–20.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-109) Burrow set a playoff record for most times sacked in a single postseason, being sacked 19 times, surpassing the previous record set by [Wade Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wade_Wilson_(American_football) "Wade Wilson (American football)") in 1987, with 14.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-110) He was ranked 21st by his fellow players on the [NFL Top 100 Players of 2022](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_Top_100_Players_of_2022 "NFL Top 100 Players of 2022").[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-:0-111)

### 2022

See also: [2022 Cincinnati Bengals season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Cincinnati_Bengals_season "2022 Cincinnati Bengals season")

Burrow underwent emergency surgery to remove his [appendix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appendix_(anatomy) "Appendix (anatomy)") on July 26, 2022, as a result of severe [appendicitis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appendicitis "Appendicitis").[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-112) In Week 1 against the [Pittsburgh Steelers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_Steelers "Pittsburgh Steelers"), Burrow committed a career-high five turnovers, which included losing a fumble and throwing four interceptions, along with being sacked seven times in the 23–20 overtime loss.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-113) Burrow returned to the state of Louisiana in Week 6 against the [New Orleans Saints](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_New_Orleans_Saints_season "2022 New Orleans Saints season"), returning to the [Caesars Superdome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caesars_Superdome "Caesars Superdome") for the first time since winning the College National Championship. Burrow threw for 300 yards and three touchdowns in the 30–26 victory, two of which to former college teammate [Ja'Marr Chase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ja'Marr_Chase "Ja'Marr Chase").[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-114) The following week against the [Atlanta Falcons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta_Falcons "Atlanta Falcons"), Burrow finished the game throwing for 481 yards in the 35–17 win.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-115) The game was Burrow's fifth game with over 400 passing yards, setting an NFL record for the most 400-yard games in a player's first three seasons. It was also his second game with over 500 yards of offense and four touchdowns, making him the first player to accomplish this multiple times.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-116) Burrow was named AFC Offensive Player of the Week as a result of his performance.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-117)

In Week 13, Burrow threw for 286 yards and two touchdowns, along with 46 rushing yards and a touchdown in a 27–24 win over the Chiefs, earning AFC Offensive Player of the Week.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-118) On December 21, Burrow was selected to the [Pro Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pro_Bowl "Pro Bowl") for the first time in his career.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-119) In their Week 15 matchup against the [Tampa Bay Buccaneers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Tampa_Bay_Buccaneers_season "2022 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season"), the Bengals found themselves down 17–3 at halftime. Burrow orchestrated a remarkable comeback in the second half, leading the team to 31 unanswered points and throwing four touchdown passes to four different receivers to lead the team to a 34–23 win.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-120) The next week, Burrow threw for 375 yards and three touchdowns in a 22–18 win over the [New England Patriots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_New_England_Patriots_season "2022 New England Patriots season"), earning his third AFC Offensive Player of the Week honor of the season.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-121)

The Bengals' Week 17 game against the [Buffalo Bills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buffalo_Bills "Buffalo Bills") was declared a no contest due to Bills' safety [Damar Hamlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Damar_Hamlin "Damar Hamlin") suffering cardiac arrest in-game.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-122) This resulted in the Bengals being declared AFC North champions ahead of their final week match against Baltimore, marking the first time the franchise won consecutive division titles.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-123) He finished the season ranked fifth in the NFL in both completions (414) and passing yards (4,475), while his franchise record 35 touchdown passes ranked in 2nd.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-124)[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-125) Meanwhile, the Bengals finished 12–4 on the season, their best record since [2015](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Cincinnati_Bengals_season "2015 Cincinnati Bengals season"), and won their last eight games consecutively.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-126)

In the [2022–23 NFL playoffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_NFL_playoffs "2022–23 NFL playoffs"), Burrow led the Bengals to a narrow win over the Ravens in the [Wild Card Round](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_NFL_playoffs#AFC:_Cincinnati_Bengals_24,_Baltimore_Ravens_17 "2022–23 NFL playoffs") and a decisive victory over the Bills in the [Divisional Round](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_NFL_playoffs#AFC:_Cincinnati_Bengals_27,_Buffalo_Bills_10 "2022–23 NFL playoffs") en route to their second consecutive AFC Championship appearance.[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-Sam2023-127)[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-Wetzel-128) In a rematch of the previous [AFC Championship Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_NFL_playoffs#AFC_Championship_Game:_Kansas_City_Chiefs_23,_Cincinnati_Bengals_20 "2022–23 NFL playoffs"), the Bengals lost to the [eventual Super Bowl champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LVII "Super Bowl LVII") Chiefs 23–20.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-129) He was ranked 6th by his fellow players on the [NFL Top 100 Players of 2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_Top_100_Players_of_2023 "NFL Top 100 Players of 2023"), his first ever appearance in the top ten on the list.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-:0-111)

### 2023

See also: [2023 Cincinnati Bengals season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Cincinnati_Bengals_season "2023 Cincinnati Bengals season")

Ahead of the season, Burrow suffered a right calf strain during training camp.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-130) Bengals head coach [Zac Taylor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zac_Taylor "Zac Taylor") initially stated that Burrow was to be sidelined for "several weeks",[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-131) with no clear timeline in place for his return, but later made a bold announcement that he was "better than he's ever looked," implying a more positive than expected recovery.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-132) On September 7, 2023, Burrow signed a five-year, $275 million contract extension, surpassing [Justin Herbert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert "Justin Herbert") to become the highest-paid player in NFL history on an annual basis, with an average annual salary of $55 million.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-133)

In Week 8, Burrow threw for 283 yards and three touchdowns while completing 87.5% of passes in a 31–17 win over the 49ers, earning AFC Offensive Player of the Week honors.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-134) During the first half of the game, Burrow reset his career high with 19 consecutive completed passes.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-135)

On November 16, Burrow suffered a torn [Scapholunate ligament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scapholunate_ligament "Scapholunate ligament") in his right wrist in the first half of the Bengals' Week 11 game against the Ravens.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-136) The next day, the Bengals announced that Burrow was to miss the remainder of the season.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-137) Burrow was placed on the injured reserve on November 25,[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-138) and soon thereafter underwent surgery.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-139) On November 17, 2023, NFL launched an investigation into whether the Bengals were compliant with the injury report policy as the Bengals had posted then deleted a video on X of Burrow wearing what appeared to be a soft cast on his right hand the day before.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-140) On December 9, 2023, NFL concluded their investigation and found the Bengals were compliant with the league's injury report policy.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-141)

Burrow continued to be involved with team activities and supported his teammates, particularly backup quarterback [Jake Browning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Browning "Jake Browning"), from the sidelines for all remaining games of the 2023 season.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-142)[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-143)[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-144) He was ranked 39th by his fellow players on the [NFL Top 100 Players of 2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_Top_100_Players_of_2024 "NFL Top 100 Players of 2024").[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-145)

### 2024

See also: [2024 Cincinnati Bengals season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Cincinnati_Bengals_season "2024 Cincinnati Bengals season")

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/58/Cincinnati_Bengals_%2851155388038%29.jpg/250px-Cincinnati_Bengals_%2851155388038%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Cincinnati_Bengals_(51155388038).jpg)

Burrow's locker at [Paycor Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paycor_Stadium "Paycor Stadium")

Burrow fully recovered from his wrist surgery in time for the 2024 season. He and the Bengals opened the season 0–2 for the third consecutive season following losses to the Patriots and Chiefs.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-146) They dropped to 0–3 following a loss to the [Washington Commanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Commanders "Washington Commanders"), despite 324 yards, three passing touchdowns, and zero turnovers from Burrow.[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-147) Before their Week 4 matchup against the [Carolina Panthers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carolina_Panthers "Carolina Panthers"), Burrow delivered an uncharacteristic pregame speech. The speech resonated with the team as the Bengals won their first game of the season, with Burrow passing for 232 yards and two touchdowns, both of which came in the first half.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-148)

In Week 5, Burrow threw for 353 yards and a career-high five touchdown passes in a 41–38 overtime loss to the [Baltimore Ravens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltimore_Ravens "Baltimore Ravens").[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-149) Sitting at 1–4, Burrow led victories over the [New York Giants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Giants "New York Giants") and [Cleveland Browns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland_Browns "Cleveland Browns"), including a career-long 47-yard touchdown run against the Giants and two second half touchdowns against the Browns.[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-150)[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-151) In Week 9, Burrow threw for 251 yards, a career-high-tying five touchdown passes and one interception in a 41–24 win over the [Las Vegas Raiders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas_Raiders "Las Vegas Raiders").[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-152) After beating the Raiders, Burrow threw for 428 yards and four touchdowns against the Ravens, followed by a 356-yard, three-touchdown performance against the Chargers. Despite his efforts, the Bengals lost both games, making Burrow the first player to throw for over 300 yards with at least three touchdowns and no interceptions in consecutive games and lose both in regulation.[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-153) He was named AFC Offensive Player of the Month for November.[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-s988-154)

Against the Steelers in Week 13, Burrow had another prolific passing day, finishing with 309 yards and three touchdowns, but he also committed three turnovers as the Bengals lost 44–38 and dropped to 4–8 on the season.[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-155) With their playoff hopes dwindling, Burrow led the Bengals on a four-game winning streak to reach 8–8 heading into the final week. During the streak, Burrow completed over 75% of his passes for 1,304 yards, 12 touchdowns, and three interceptions for a 116 passer rating, highlighted by a 412-yard, four-touchdown performance against the [Denver Broncos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver_Broncos "Denver Broncos") in an elimination scenario.[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-156) The performance also marked Burrow's eighth consecutive outing with at least 250 passing yards and three touchdowns, the longest streak in NFL history.[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-157) He was named AFC Offensive Player of the Week for Week 17.[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-v270-158) He was named AFC Offensive Player of the Month for December.[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-c265-159) Burrow led the Bengals to victory in Week 18 against the Steelers to cap the season off on a five-game winning streak, but a win from the Broncos the following day eliminated them from playoff contention.[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-g780-160)[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-161) He earned his second Pro Bowl nomination.[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-m532-162)

Returning from wrist surgery, Burrow finished the 2024 season with a career-best 4,918 passing yards and 43 touchdowns, leading the NFL in both statistics.[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-163)[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-164) He became the third quarterback to have at least 4,500 passing yards, 40 passing touchdowns, and fewer than 10 interceptions, joining [Tom Brady](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Brady "Tom Brady") in 2007 and [Aaron Rodgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Rodgers "Aaron Rodgers") in 2011.[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-165) Burrow won the Comeback Player of the Year Award, joining [Chad Pennington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chad_Pennington "Chad Pennington") as the only player to win the award twice.[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-166) He was ranked sixth by his fellow players on the [NFL Top 100 Players of 2025](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_Top_100_Players_of_2025 "NFL Top 100 Players of 2025").[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-167)

### 2025

See also: [2025 Cincinnati Bengals season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Cincinnati_Bengals_season "2025 Cincinnati Bengals season")

[![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/25/Commanders_vs._Bengals_-_54751463192.jpg/250px-Commanders_vs._Bengals_-_54751463192.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Commanders_vs._Bengals_-_54751463192.jpg)

Burrow playing against the [Washington Commanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Commanders "Washington Commanders") in the 2025 preseason

During the Bengals season opener against division rival [Cleveland Browns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Cleveland_Browns_season "2025 Cleveland Browns season"), Burrow would throw for 113 yards and a single touchdown to newly acquired [tight end](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tight_end "Tight end")[Noah Fant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noah_Fant "Noah Fant") from [Seattle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Seattle_Seahawks_season "2025 Seattle Seahawks season").[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-168) In the Bengals week two game against the [Jacksonville Jaguars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Jacksonville_Jaguars_season "2025 Jacksonville Jaguars season"), Burrow would take a sack during the second quarter of the game. After medical examination, he was ruled out for the remainder of the game with a left toe injury.[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-169) He finished the game with 76 yards and 1 touchdown before backup quarterback [Jake Browning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Browning "Jake Browning") took his place.[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-170) Later that day, it was reported that Burrow suffered a [metatarsophalangeal joint sprain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metatarsophalangeal_joint_sprain "Metatarsophalangeal joint sprain") known as [turf toe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turf_toe "Turf toe") as well as "significant ligament damage".[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-171) The next day, it was announced that his injury would require surgery, and his estimated recovery time was set at a minimum of 3 months.[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-172) He was officially put on [injured reserve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Injured_reserve "Injured reserve") on September 16.[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-173) Burrow was activated on November 26, ahead of Cincinnati's [Thanksgiving matchup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_on_Thanksgiving_Day "NFL on Thanksgiving Day") against the [Baltimore Ravens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Baltimore_Ravens_season "2025 Baltimore Ravens season").[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-174) Burrow led the team to a 32–14 victory with two touchdown passes in his return.[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-175) In Week 16, Burrow completed 25 of 32 passes for 309 yards and four touchdowns in a 45–21 win over the Miami Dolphins, earning AFC Offensive Player of the Week honors.[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-176) Burrow played in eight games in the 2025 season. He finished with 1,809 yards, 17 touchdowns, and five interceptions.[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-177) He earned Pro Bowl honors for the third time.[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-178)

## Player profile

> "Burrow is considered a relatively quiet, occasionally quirky guy. But he's beloved in the LSU locker room, largely because he plays with a competitiveness that borders on fanatical."

—Robert Mays of _[The Ringer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Ringer\_(website) "The Ringer (website)")_ in a [profile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feature_story#Types "Feature story") about Burrow (November 2019).[[186]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-Mays2019-189)

At the NFL combine, Burrow was measured to be 6 ft 3 in and 221 lbs; his hands were measured to be 9 inches.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-combineprofile-75) In 2021, _[Sports Illustrated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports\_Illustrated "Sports Illustrated")_ writer Mike Santagata wrote that Burrow is "bigger than he looks at about 230 pounds," while also noting his athleticism and strength.[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-Santagata2021-190)

Through his junior year at LSU, Burrow "initial run through the [NFL's] scouting machine resulted in such an underwhelming consensus".[[186]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-Mays2019-189) Many scouts viewed Burrow as an "NFL draft afterthought", and considered him "a late-round project and potential backup."[[186]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-Mays2019-189) He was seen as having limited physical traits and average production prior to his senior season.[[186]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-Mays2019-189) SEC analyst [Jordan Rodgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan_Rodgers "Jordan Rodgers") opined that Burrow was "wildly inconsistent, and frankly very poor against good competition" in 2018.[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-Dellenger2019-191) Burrow's 2019 season was cited as helping draw more attention to scouts to reconsider their evaluation of him,[[186]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-Mays2019-189) and his [football IQ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Football_IQ "Football IQ"), accuracy, pocket mobility, and playmaking outside of the pocket have all been cited as strengths of his game.[[189]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-Goldsmith2021-192) The Bengals caught attention of these traits in 2019, making Burrow the top pick in the 2020 NFL draft.[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-Santagata2021-190)[[189]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-Goldsmith2021-192)

### Football IQ

Burrow's football IQ has often been cited by writers, coaches, coordinators, and other players as a critical aspect of Burrow's game. He has been analyzed as being capable of processing opposing defenses quickly.[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-Santagata2021-190) Burrow participated in game plan meetings during his tenure at LSU to discuss the next opponent, where he pitched game plan ideas with LSU passing game coordinator [Joe Brady](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Brady_(American_football_coach) "Joe Brady (American football coach)") and offensive coordinator [Steve Ensminger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Ensminger "Steve Ensminger").[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-Dellenger2019-191) The two coaches also trusted Burrow with presnap play calls and Burrow was noted by _Sports Illustrated_ for his tendency to "often change receiver routes based on defensive formations."[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-Dellenger2019-191)[_College GameDay_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_GameDay_(football_TV_program) "College GameDay (football TV program)") analyst [Kirk Herbstreit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kirk_Herbstreit "Kirk Herbstreit") likened Burrow to a "co-offensive coordinator", stating "That's the NFL model, when you have a quarterback able to invest and communicate at that level. [Burrow] is the cutting edge of that mold. When I watch LSU, it's not just Joe Brady's offense—it's Joe Brady _and_ Joe Burrow's offense."[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-Dellenger2019-191) As a Bengal, Burrow was noted to have successfully called his own plays during the 2021 Divisional Round game against Tennessee.[[190]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-193)

Burrow plays chess in his spare time, as well as during game preparation. He keeps a chessboard in his locker.[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-Baby2022-194) Prior to [Super Bowl LVI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LVI "Super Bowl LVI"), Burrow played ten matches of online chess.[[192]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-195) Cornerback [Chidobe Awuzie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chidobe_Awuzie "Chidobe Awuzie"), who plays chess with Burrow and was teammates with him from 2021 through 2023, commented "The fact that he plays chess lets you know that he's able to prioritize certain things and articulate things very fast and have formation recognition."[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-Baby2022-194)

### Accuracy and physical traits

[![Image 18](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b3/Burrow_and_Bernard.jpg/250px-Burrow_and_Bernard.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Burrow_and_Bernard.jpg)

Burrow delivers a pass to Bengals running back [Giovani Bernard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giovani_Bernard "Giovani Bernard") in November 2020.

Sportswriters have praised Burrow's accuracy, calling his ball placement elite.[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-Santagata2021-190)[Brian Callahan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Callahan "Brian Callahan"), during his tenure as Bengals offensive coordinator, stated that Burrow has "an uncanny ability to place the ball accurately on the move anywhere on the field."[[189]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-Goldsmith2021-192) Charlie Goldsmith of _[The Cincinnati Enquirer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Cincinnati\_Enquirer "The Cincinnati Enquirer")_ wrote that Burrow possess elite traits in regards to his "combination of picking up the blitz and his accuracy outside the pocket".[[189]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-Goldsmith2021-192)

Burrow's pocket management, particularly his movement and footwork within the pocket to help him avoid sacks, has been noted by sportswriters.[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-Santagata2021-190)_[The Athletic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Athletic "The Athletic")_ wrote positively of Burrow's "ability to work a broken pocket," stating that Burrow evades defenders and is able to both find space to deliver a throw or run with the ball himself.[[193]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-Dehner2022-196)

### Intangibles

Former [New England Patriots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_England_Patriots "New England Patriots") running back [Kevin Faulk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Faulk "Kevin Faulk") compared Burrow to [Tom Brady](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Brady "Tom Brady"), noting the former's poise and competitiveness.[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-Dellenger2019-191) Once in the NFL, Burrow drew further comparisons to Brady from Chiefs defensive coordinator [Steve Spagnuolo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Spagnuolo "Steve Spagnuolo").[[194]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-Roling2021-197)

Burrow's leadership has also been noted by teammates and opponents alike; veteran [Mike Daniels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Daniels_(American_football) "Mike Daniels (American football)") spoke on Burrow being voted a team captain as a rookie, stating that Burrow earned the respect of his veteran teammates before even playing.[[195]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-Rapien2020-12a-198) Kansas City Chiefs quarterback [Patrick Mahomes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Mahomes "Patrick Mahomes") has stated "Not only is he a great football player, I think he's a great leader. He has that special knack where he can lead anybody."[[194]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-Roling2021-197) Mahomes and linebacker [Patrick Queen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Queen "Patrick Queen") have also noted Burrow's "swag" or "swagger".[[194]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-Roling2021-197)[[196]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-199) Indeed, Burrow has been noted by writers for his "cool" demeanor both on and off the field.[[197]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-200)[[198]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-201)_[ProFootballTalk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ProFootballTalk "ProFootballTalk")_ writer [Peter King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_King_(sportswriter) "Peter King (sportswriter)") wrote that "Burrow's steely mentality and his right arm are putting him on the path to greatness. I wouldn't bet against him."[[199]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-202) Burrow's attitude has been attributed as a factor in his ability to remain calm under pressure in-game, earning him the "Joe Cool" and "Joe Brrr" nicknames.[[200]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-203)[[201]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-204)[[202]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-Ogwude-205)

## Flag football

In March 2026, Burrow competed in the [Fanatics Flag Football Classic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fanatics_Flag_Football_Classic "Fanatics Flag Football Classic") as a member of the Wildcats FFC.[[203]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-206) The event was a round-robin tournament between three teams; Burrow led the team to a victory over Founders FFC, but lost to Team USA in the championship round.[[204]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-Baby-2026-207) Burrow expressed interest in playing for the [United States men's national flag football team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_men's_national_flag_football_team "United States men's national flag football team") at the [2028 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flag_football_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Flag football at the Summer Olympics").[[204]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-Baby-2026-207)

## Personal life

[![Image 19](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a5/Joe_Burrow_-_Lordstown_interview_%282%29.png/250px-Joe_Burrow_-_Lordstown_interview_%282%29.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Joe_Burrow_-_Lordstown_interview_(2).png)

Burrow during an interview with [Lordstown Motors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lordstown_Motors "Lordstown Motors") in November 2022

Burrow spent one summer during college interning at [Goldman Sachs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goldman_Sachs "Goldman Sachs").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-Dellenger2019-07-29) After signing his rookie contract with the Bengals, Burrow stated that he planned to save all of his contract money and instead live through income received from endorsements.[[205]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-208)

Burrow is a fan of the _[Super Smash Bros.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super\_Smash\_Bros. "Super Smash Bros.")_ video game series.[[206]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-209) In a 2023 interview, Burrow stated that he usually plays _[Super Smash Bros. Ultimate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super\_Smash\_Bros.\_Ultimate "Super Smash Bros. Ultimate")_ on flights to road games with his teammates, and that he frequently plays as [Ness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ness_(EarthBound) "Ness (EarthBound)") from _[Earthbound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mother\_(video\_game\_series) "Mother (video game series)")_.[[207]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-210)

Burrow is an avid fan of [Kid Cudi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kid_Cudi "Kid Cudi"), often listening to his music prior to Bengals games.[[208]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-211) In February 2022, Burrow appeared on-stage with Cudi during a Super Bowl afterparty.[[209]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-212) Later in the year, Cudi included a bonus track named after Burrow on his [_Entergalactic_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entergalactic_(album) "Entergalactic (album)") album.[[210]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-213)

In January 2023, Burrow was among a coalition of about a dozen athletes, including [Blake Griffin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blake_Griffin "Blake Griffin") and [Kevin Gausman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Gausman "Kevin Gausman"), who purchased a 104-acre (42 ha) north Iowa farm with plans to further acquire a diverse set of agricultural assets.[[211]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-214)

In 2024, Burrow bought one of the ten replicas of the [Batmobile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batmobile "Batmobile") from [_The Dark Knight_ film trilogy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dark_Knight_trilogy "The Dark Knight trilogy") for $2.9 million to add to his car collection.[[212]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-215)

### Political views

In the wake of the _[Roe v. Wade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roe\_v.\_Wade "Roe v. Wade")_ being overturned in June 2022, Burrow spoke out on Instagram in favor of [abortion rights in the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abortion_in_the_United_States "Abortion in the United States").[[213]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-216) Following the [Uvalde school shooting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uvalde_school_shooting "Uvalde school shooting"), Burrow expressed his support for stricter [gun control](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gun_control "Gun control") reforms during a press conference.[[214]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Burrow#cite_note-217)

The **2023 NFL draft** was the 88th annual meeting of [National Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League") (NFL) franchises to select newly eligible players for the [2023 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_NFL_season "2023 NFL season"). The [draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_draft "NFL draft") was held outside of [Union Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City_Union_Station "Kansas City Union Station") in [Kansas City, Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City,_Missouri "Kansas City, Missouri"), from April 27–29, 2023.

The [Chicago Bears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Bears "Chicago Bears") originally owned the [first pick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_first_overall_NFL_draft_picks "List of first overall NFL draft picks") for the first time since [1947](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1947_NFL_draft "1947 NFL draft") before trading it prior to the draft to the [Carolina Panthers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carolina_Panthers "Carolina Panthers") for multiple draft picks and wide receiver [D. J. Moore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D._J._Moore "D. J. Moore"). The Panthers selected Alabama quarterback [Bryce Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young "Bryce Young") first overall and the [Los Angeles Rams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Rams "Los Angeles Rams") selected [Desjuan Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desjuan_Johnson "Desjuan Johnson") with the final pick.

## Host city and events

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2023_NFL_draft&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Host city and events")]

[Kansas City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City,_Missouri "Kansas City, Missouri") was chosen as the host city on May 22, 2019.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_NFL_draft#cite_note-1) Prior to the start of the draft, the NFL paid tribute to the three victims of the [2022 University of Virginia shooting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_University_of_Virginia_shooting "2022 University of Virginia shooting"), who were named honorary draft picks for their favorite teams: the [Jacksonville Jaguars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacksonville_Jaguars "Jacksonville Jaguars"), [Baltimore Ravens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltimore_Ravens "Baltimore Ravens") and [Miami Dolphins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_Dolphins "Miami Dolphins"), respectively.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_NFL_draft#cite_note-2) The NFL Draft House Band, [Lost Wax Band](https://lostwaxband.com/), was selected to entertain the NFL Draft crowd for all three nights.

The **2023 NFL draft** was the 88th annual meeting of [National Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League") (NFL) franchises to select newly eligible players for the [2023 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_NFL_season "2023 NFL season"). The [draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_draft "NFL draft") was held outside of [Union Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City_Union_Station "Kansas City Union Station") in [Kansas City, Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City,_Missouri "Kansas City, Missouri"), from April 27–29, 2023.

The [Chicago Bears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Bears "Chicago Bears") originally owned the [first pick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_first_overall_NFL_draft_picks "List of first overall NFL draft picks") for the first time since [1947](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1947_NFL_draft "1947 NFL draft") before trading it prior to the draft to the [Carolina Panthers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carolina_Panthers "Carolina Panthers") for multiple draft picks and wide receiver [D. J. Moore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D._J._Moore "D. J. Moore"). The Panthers selected Alabama quarterback [Bryce Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young "Bryce Young") first overall and the [Los Angeles Rams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Rams "Los Angeles Rams") selected [Desjuan Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desjuan_Johnson "Desjuan Johnson") with the final pick.

## Host city and events

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2023_NFL_draft&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Host city and events")]

[Kansas City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City,_Missouri "Kansas City, Missouri") was chosen as the host city on May 22, 2019.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_NFL_draft#cite_note-1) Prior to the start of the draft, the NFL paid tribute to the three victims of the [2022 University of Virginia shooting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_University_of_Virginia_shooting "2022 University of Virginia shooting"), who were named honorary draft picks for their favorite teams: the [Jacksonville Jaguars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacksonville_Jaguars "Jacksonville Jaguars"), [Baltimore Ravens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltimore_Ravens "Baltimore Ravens") and [Miami Dolphins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_Dolphins "Miami Dolphins"), respectively.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_NFL_draft#cite_note-2) The NFL Draft House Band, [Lost Wax Band](https://lostwaxband.com/), was selected to entertain the NFL Draft crowd for all three nights.

**Bryce Christopher Young** (born July 25, 2001) is an American professional [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_football "American football")[quarterback](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quarterback "Quarterback") for the [Carolina Panthers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carolina_Panthers "Carolina Panthers") of the [National Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League") (NFL). He played [college football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_football "College football") for the [Alabama Crimson Tide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alabama_Crimson_Tide_football "Alabama Crimson Tide football"), where he set the school single-game passing yards record with 559 yards and won the [Heisman Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heisman_Trophy "Heisman Trophy") in 2021. Young was selected [first overall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_first_overall_NFL_draft_picks "List of first overall NFL draft picks") by the Panthers in the 2023 NFL draft. In the 2025 season, he set the Panthers' single-game passing yards record and helped Carolina win its first [NFC South](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFC_South "NFC South") title since 2015.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bryce_Young&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Young was born on July 25, 2001, at [Lankenau Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lankenau_Medical_Center "Lankenau Medical Center") in [Wynnewood, Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wynnewood,_Pennsylvania "Wynnewood, Pennsylvania"), near [Philadelphia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia "Philadelphia").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-ESPNProfile-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-Jensen2022-2) He grew up mostly in [Pasadena, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pasadena,_California "Pasadena, California"), and is the only child of Craig Young, a mental health therapist, and Julie Young, a former special education teacher who played college soccer at [Cal Poly Pomona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cal_Poly_Pomona_Broncos "Cal Poly Pomona Broncos").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-Trepel2023-3) His maternal grandfather was born in [Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico "Mexico").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-Manzano2023-4)

Young attended [Cathedral High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cathedral_High_School_(Los_Angeles) "Cathedral High School (Los Angeles)") in Los Angeles before transferring to [Mater Dei High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mater_Dei_High_School_(Santa_Ana,_California) "Mater Dei High School (Santa Ana, California)") in [Santa Ana, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Ana,_California "Santa Ana, California"), in 2018.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-Albano2018-5) As a senior at Mater Dei, he was named the _[Los Angeles Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los\_Angeles\_Times "Los Angeles Times")_ Player of the Year, California's [Gatorade Football Player of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gatorade_Player_of_the_Year_awards "Gatorade Player of the Year awards"), and the _[USA Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USA\_Today "USA Today")_ High School Offensive Player of the Year after throwing for 4,528 yards and 58 touchdowns.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-Sondheimer2019-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-Gatorade2019-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-USAToday2019-8) He finished his high school career with 13,250 passing yards and 152 passing touchdowns.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-Gatorade2019-7)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-RollTideBio-9) A five-star recruit, Young was ranked by the 247Sports Composite as the No. 2 overall prospect and No. 1 dual-threat quarterback in the 2020 class.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-RollTideBio-9) After initially committing to [USC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USC_Trojans_football "USC Trojans football"), Young changed his commitment to [Alabama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alabama_Crimson_Tide_football "Alabama Crimson Tide football") in September 2019.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-ESPN2019-10)

Young became friends with [C. J. Stroud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud "C. J. Stroud") while both were high school quarterbacks in Southern California. They were selected first and second overall, respectively, in the 2023 NFL draft.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-Cooney2023-11)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-Manzano2023-4)

## College career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bryce_Young&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: College career")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4a/Bryce_Young_2021_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Bryce_Young_2021_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bryce_Young_2021_(cropped).jpg)

### Freshman year

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bryce_Young&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Freshman year")]

See also: [2020 Alabama Crimson Tide football team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Alabama_Crimson_Tide_football_team "2020 Alabama Crimson Tide football team")

During his freshman year at Alabama, Young was the backup to junior quarterback [Mac Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mac_Jones "Mac Jones") throughout the [2020 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Alabama_Crimson_Tide_football_team "2020 Alabama Crimson Tide football team"). On September 26, 2020, Young made his collegiate debut in the late third quarter against [Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Missouri_Tigers_football_team "2020 Missouri Tigers football team") at [Faurot Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faurot_Field "Faurot Field"). That night, Young went 5-of-8 for 54 passing yards with two rushing yards on four attempts.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-12) On November 21, he threw his first collegiate touchdown pass in a 63–3 victory over [Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Kentucky_Wildcats_football_team "2020 Kentucky Wildcats football team").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-13) Young appeared in nine games in 2020, finishing the season with 156 passing yards and one touchdown.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-14)

### Sophomore year

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bryce_Young&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Sophomore year")]

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/dc/CM28792-fotor-202307249344by.jpg/250px-CM28792-fotor-202307249344by.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:CM28792-fotor-202307249344by.jpg)

Young warming up before a game with Alabama

See also: [2021 Alabama Crimson Tide football team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Alabama_Crimson_Tide_football_team "2021 Alabama Crimson Tide football team")

On September 4, 2021, Young made his debut as the Crimson Tide's starting quarterback.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-15) In a 44–13 win over the #14 [Miami Hurricanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Miami_Hurricanes_football_team "2021 Miami Hurricanes football team"), he passed for 344 yards and four touchdowns.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-16)

On November 20, against [Arkansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Arkansas_Razorbacks_football_team "2021 Arkansas Razorbacks football team"), Young threw for 559 yards to break the Alabama school record for passing yards in a game. He had five touchdowns in the 42–35 win.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-i011-17) The previous record was held by [Scott Hunter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Hunter_(American_football) "Scott Hunter (American football)").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-18)

Young won the [Heisman Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heisman_Trophy "Heisman Trophy") following the end of the 2021 season, becoming the first Alabama quarterback to win the award.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-20) In addition to the Heisman Trophy, Young won AP Player of the Year, the [Davey O'Brien Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Davey_O'Brien_Award "Davey O'Brien Award"), the [Manning Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manning_Award "Manning Award"), the [Maxwell Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxwell_Award "Maxwell Award"), [Southeastern Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southeastern_Conference "Southeastern Conference") (SEC) Offensive Player of the Year, and was a consensus [All-American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_Football_All-America_Team "College Football All-America Team").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-26)

Overall, Young passed for 4,872 yards, 47 passing touchdowns, and seven interceptions to go along with three rushing touchdowns in 15 games.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-27) He led the SEC in passing yards and passing touchdowns in the 2021 season.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-28)

### Junior year

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bryce_Young&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Junior year")]

See also: [2022 Alabama Crimson Tide football team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Alabama_Crimson_Tide_football_team "2022 Alabama Crimson Tide football team")

Young started his junior season off strong with 195 passing yards and five passing touchdowns to go along with five carries for 100 rushing yards and one rushing touchdown in the 55–0 victory over [Utah State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Utah_State_Aggies_football_team "2022 Utah State Aggies football team").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-29) In his junior year, Young led the Crimson Tide to an 11–2 record, including a 45–20 victory over No. 14 [Kansas State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_State_Wildcats_football "Kansas State Wildcats football") in the [2022](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Sugar_Bowl_(December) "2022 Sugar Bowl (December)")[Sugar Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sugar_Bowl "Sugar Bowl").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-31) He finished in sixth in Heisman Trophy voting.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-32) He passed for 3,328 yards, 32 passing touchdowns, and five interceptions to go along with 49 carries for 185 rushing yards and four rushing touchdowns in 12 games.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-33) On January 2, 2023, Young announced that he would forgo his senior season and enter the 2023 NFL draft.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-34)

### 2023

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bryce_Young&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2023")]

See also: [2023 Carolina Panthers season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Carolina_Panthers_season "2023 Carolina Panthers season")

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3c/Bryce_Young_Carolina_Panthers_2023_season_%28cropped%29.png/250px-Bryce_Young_Carolina_Panthers_2023_season_%28cropped%29.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bryce_Young_Carolina_Panthers_2023_season_(cropped).png)

Young with the Panthers during his rookie season in 2023

Young was selected by the [Carolina Panthers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carolina_Panthers "Carolina Panthers") with the [first overall pick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_first_overall_National_Football_League_Draft_picks "List of first overall National Football League Draft picks") in the 2023 NFL draft. The Panthers had acquired the pick from the [Chicago Bears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Bears "Chicago Bears") in a trade that included the ninth overall pick, wide receiver [D. J. Moore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D._J._Moore "D. J. Moore"), and additional draft selections.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-37) He signed a four-year, fully guaranteed rookie contract worth $37.9 million on July 21, 2023.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-38)

Young made his NFL debut on September 10, 2023, in a Week 1 loss to the [Atlanta Falcons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta_Falcons "Atlanta Falcons"), throwing his first career touchdown pass to [Hayden Hurst](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayden_Hurst "Hayden Hurst").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-39) He missed Week 3 with an ankle injury.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-40) Young recorded his first NFL win on October 29, when Carolina defeated the [Houston Texans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_Texans "Houston Texans") 15–13.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-41) He finished his rookie season with 2,877 passing yards, 11 touchdowns, and 10 interceptions in 16 starts as the Panthers finished 2–15.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-NFLStats-42)

### 2024

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bryce_Young&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: 2024")]

See also: [2024 Carolina Panthers season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Carolina_Panthers_season "2024 Carolina Panthers season")

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/dd/Bryce_Young_at_W.P.T._Hill_Field_-_2024_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Bryce_Young_at_W.P.T._Hill_Field_-_2024_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bryce_Young_at_W.P.T._Hill_Field_-_2024_(cropped).jpg)

Young in 2024

Young opened the 2024 season as Carolina's starting quarterback but was benched for veteran [Andy Dalton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Dalton "Andy Dalton") after the Panthers lost their first two games by a combined 60 points.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-z264-43) He returned to the starting lineup in Week 8 after Dalton sustained a thumb injury in a car accident.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-n320-44)

After returning to the lineup, Young helped Carolina defeat the [New Orleans Saints](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans_Saints "New Orleans Saints") and [New York Giants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Giants "New York Giants") in consecutive games, the Panthers' first back-to-back wins since 2022.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-45) In the season finale against the Falcons, he passed for three touchdowns and rushed for two more in a 44–38 overtime win.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-46) Young finished the season with 2,403 passing yards, 15 passing touchdowns, nine interceptions, and six rushing touchdowns.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-NFLStats-42) Following the season, head coach [Dave Canales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Canales "Dave Canales") said Young would remain Carolina's starting quarterback entering 2025.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-47)

### 2025

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bryce_Young&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: 2025")]

See also: [2025 Carolina Panthers season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Carolina_Panthers_season "2025 Carolina Panthers season")

Young started 16 games in 2025, completing 304 of 478 passes for 3,011 yards, 23 touchdowns, and 11 interceptions; his yards, touchdowns, completion percentage, and passer rating were career highs.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-NFLStats-42) In Week 11, he passed for 448 yards, three touchdowns, and no interceptions in a 30–27 overtime win over the [Atlanta Falcons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta_Falcons "Atlanta Falcons"), breaking [Cam Newton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cam_Newton "Cam Newton")'s Panthers single-game record of 432 passing yards.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-NFLYoungRecord2025-48) The performance earned Young his first [NFC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_Conference "National Football Conference") Offensive Player of the Week award and the [FedEx Air & Ground Players of the Week](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FedEx_Air_&_Ground_NFL_Players_of_the_Week "FedEx Air & Ground NFL Players of the Week") honor.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-49)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-50)

The Panthers finished the regular season 8–9 and won the [NFC South](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFC_South "NFC South") on a three-way tiebreaker, their first division title since 2015.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-51)[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-52) Young made his postseason debut on January 10, 2026, in a 34–31 wild-card loss to the [Los Angeles Rams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Rams "Los Angeles Rams"), throwing for 264 yards and a touchdown and rushing for another score.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-53) He was ranked No. 98 by his fellow players on the [NFL Top 100 Players of 2026](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_Top_100_Players_of_2026 "NFL Top 100 Players of 2026").[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-54)

### 2026

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bryce_Young&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: 2026")]

On April 29, 2026, the Panthers exercised the fifth-year option on Young's rookie contract, keeping him under contract through the 2027 season.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-55)

**Bryce Christopher Young** (born July 25, 2001) is an American professional [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_football "American football")[quarterback](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quarterback "Quarterback") for the [Carolina Panthers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carolina_Panthers "Carolina Panthers") of the [National Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League") (NFL). He played [college football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_football "College football") for the [Alabama Crimson Tide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alabama_Crimson_Tide_football "Alabama Crimson Tide football"), where he set the school single-game passing yards record with 559 yards and won the [Heisman Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heisman_Trophy "Heisman Trophy") in 2021. Young was selected [first overall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_first_overall_NFL_draft_picks "List of first overall NFL draft picks") by the Panthers in the 2023 NFL draft. In the 2025 season, he set the Panthers' single-game passing yards record and helped Carolina win its first [NFC South](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFC_South "NFC South") title since 2015.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bryce_Young&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Young was born on July 25, 2001, at [Lankenau Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lankenau_Medical_Center "Lankenau Medical Center") in [Wynnewood, Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wynnewood,_Pennsylvania "Wynnewood, Pennsylvania"), near [Philadelphia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia "Philadelphia").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-ESPNProfile-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-Jensen2022-2) He grew up mostly in [Pasadena, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pasadena,_California "Pasadena, California"), and is the only child of Craig Young, a mental health therapist, and Julie Young, a former special education teacher who played college soccer at [Cal Poly Pomona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cal_Poly_Pomona_Broncos "Cal Poly Pomona Broncos").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-Trepel2023-3) His maternal grandfather was born in [Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico "Mexico").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-Manzano2023-4)

Young attended [Cathedral High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cathedral_High_School_(Los_Angeles) "Cathedral High School (Los Angeles)") in Los Angeles before transferring to [Mater Dei High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mater_Dei_High_School_(Santa_Ana,_California) "Mater Dei High School (Santa Ana, California)") in [Santa Ana, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Ana,_California "Santa Ana, California"), in 2018.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-Albano2018-5) As a senior at Mater Dei, he was named the _[Los Angeles Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los\_Angeles\_Times "Los Angeles Times")_ Player of the Year, California's [Gatorade Football Player of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gatorade_Player_of_the_Year_awards "Gatorade Player of the Year awards"), and the _[USA Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USA\_Today "USA Today")_ High School Offensive Player of the Year after throwing for 4,528 yards and 58 touchdowns.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-Sondheimer2019-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-Gatorade2019-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-USAToday2019-8) He finished his high school career with 13,250 passing yards and 152 passing touchdowns.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-Gatorade2019-7)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-RollTideBio-9) A five-star recruit, Young was ranked by the 247Sports Composite as the No. 2 overall prospect and No. 1 dual-threat quarterback in the 2020 class.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-RollTideBio-9) After initially committing to [USC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USC_Trojans_football "USC Trojans football"), Young changed his commitment to [Alabama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alabama_Crimson_Tide_football "Alabama Crimson Tide football") in September 2019.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-ESPN2019-10)

Young became friends with [C. J. Stroud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud "C. J. Stroud") while both were high school quarterbacks in Southern California. They were selected first and second overall, respectively, in the 2023 NFL draft.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-Cooney2023-11)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-Manzano2023-4)
