### Freshman year

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bryce_Young&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Freshman year")]

See also: [2020 Alabama Crimson Tide football team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Alabama_Crimson_Tide_football_team "2020 Alabama Crimson Tide football team")

During his freshman year at Alabama, Young was the backup to junior quarterback [Mac Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mac_Jones "Mac Jones") throughout the [2020 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Alabama_Crimson_Tide_football_team "2020 Alabama Crimson Tide football team"). On September 26, 2020, Young made his collegiate debut in the late third quarter against [Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Missouri_Tigers_football_team "2020 Missouri Tigers football team") at [Faurot Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faurot_Field "Faurot Field"). That night, Young went 5-of-8 for 54 passing yards with two rushing yards on four attempts.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-12) On November 21, he threw his first collegiate touchdown pass in a 63–3 victory over [Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Kentucky_Wildcats_football_team "2020 Kentucky Wildcats football team").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-13) Young appeared in nine games in 2020, finishing the season with 156 passing yards and one touchdown.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-14)

### Sophomore year

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bryce_Young&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Sophomore year")]

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/dc/CM28792-fotor-202307249344by.jpg/250px-CM28792-fotor-202307249344by.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:CM28792-fotor-202307249344by.jpg)

Young warming up before a game with Alabama

See also: [2021 Alabama Crimson Tide football team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Alabama_Crimson_Tide_football_team "2021 Alabama Crimson Tide football team")

On September 4, 2021, Young made his debut as the Crimson Tide's starting quarterback.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-15) In a 44–13 win over the #14 [Miami Hurricanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Miami_Hurricanes_football_team "2021 Miami Hurricanes football team"), he passed for 344 yards and four touchdowns.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-16)

On November 20, against [Arkansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Arkansas_Razorbacks_football_team "2021 Arkansas Razorbacks football team"), Young threw for 559 yards to break the Alabama school record for passing yards in a game. He had five touchdowns in the 42–35 win.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-i011-17) The previous record was held by [Scott Hunter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Hunter_(American_football) "Scott Hunter (American football)").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-18)

Young won the [Heisman Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heisman_Trophy "Heisman Trophy") following the end of the 2021 season, becoming the first Alabama quarterback to win the award.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-20) In addition to the Heisman Trophy, Young won AP Player of the Year, the [Davey O'Brien Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Davey_O'Brien_Award "Davey O'Brien Award"), the [Manning Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manning_Award "Manning Award"), the [Maxwell Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxwell_Award "Maxwell Award"), [Southeastern Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southeastern_Conference "Southeastern Conference") (SEC) Offensive Player of the Year, and was a consensus [All-American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_Football_All-America_Team "College Football All-America Team").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-26)

Overall, Young passed for 4,872 yards, 47 passing touchdowns, and seven interceptions to go along with three rushing touchdowns in 15 games.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-27) He led the SEC in passing yards and passing touchdowns in the 2021 season.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-28)

### Junior year

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bryce_Young&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Junior year")]

See also: [2022 Alabama Crimson Tide football team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Alabama_Crimson_Tide_football_team "2022 Alabama Crimson Tide football team")

Young started his junior season off strong with 195 passing yards and five passing touchdowns to go along with five carries for 100 rushing yards and one rushing touchdown in the 55–0 victory over [Utah State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Utah_State_Aggies_football_team "2022 Utah State Aggies football team").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-29) In his junior year, Young led the Crimson Tide to an 11–2 record, including a 45–20 victory over No. 14 [Kansas State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_State_Wildcats_football "Kansas State Wildcats football") in the [2022](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Sugar_Bowl_(December) "2022 Sugar Bowl (December)")[Sugar Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sugar_Bowl "Sugar Bowl").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-31) He finished in sixth in Heisman Trophy voting.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-32) He passed for 3,328 yards, 32 passing touchdowns, and five interceptions to go along with 49 carries for 185 rushing yards and four rushing touchdowns in 12 games.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-33) On January 2, 2023, Young announced that he would forgo his senior season and enter the 2023 NFL draft.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-34)

Young with the Panthers during his rookie season in 2023

Young was selected by the [Carolina Panthers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carolina_Panthers "Carolina Panthers") with the [first overall pick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_first_overall_National_Football_League_Draft_picks "List of first overall National Football League Draft picks") in the 2023 NFL draft. The Panthers had acquired the pick from the [Chicago Bears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Bears "Chicago Bears") in a trade that included the ninth overall pick, wide receiver [D. J. Moore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D._J._Moore "D. J. Moore"), and additional draft selections.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-37) He signed a four-year, fully guaranteed rookie contract worth $37.9 million on July 21, 2023.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-38)

Young made his NFL debut on September 10, 2023, in a Week 1 loss to the [Atlanta Falcons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta_Falcons "Atlanta Falcons"), throwing his first career touchdown pass to [Hayden Hurst](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayden_Hurst "Hayden Hurst").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-39) He missed Week 3 with an ankle injury.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-40) Young recorded his first NFL win on October 29, when Carolina defeated the [Houston Texans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_Texans "Houston Texans") 15–13.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-41) He finished his rookie season with 2,877 passing yards, 11 touchdowns, and 10 interceptions in 16 starts as the Panthers finished 2–15.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-NFLStats-42)

### 2024

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bryce_Young&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: 2024")]

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/dd/Bryce_Young_at_W.P.T._Hill_Field_-_2024_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Bryce_Young_at_W.P.T._Hill_Field_-_2024_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bryce_Young_at_W.P.T._Hill_Field_-_2024_(cropped).jpg)

Young in 2024

Young opened the 2024 season as Carolina's starting quarterback but was benched for veteran [Andy Dalton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Dalton "Andy Dalton") after the Panthers lost their first two games by a combined 60 points.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-z264-43) He returned to the starting lineup in Week 8 after Dalton sustained a thumb injury in a car accident.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-n320-44)

After returning to the lineup, Young helped Carolina defeat the [New Orleans Saints](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans_Saints "New Orleans Saints") and [New York Giants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Giants "New York Giants") in consecutive games, the Panthers' first back-to-back wins since 2022.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-45) In the season finale against the Falcons, he passed for three touchdowns and rushed for two more in a 44–38 overtime win.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-46) Young finished the season with 2,403 passing yards, 15 passing touchdowns, nine interceptions, and six rushing touchdowns.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-NFLStats-42) Following the season, head coach [Dave Canales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Canales "Dave Canales") said Young would remain Carolina's starting quarterback entering 2025.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-47)

### 2025

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bryce_Young&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: 2025")]

See also: [2025 Carolina Panthers season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Carolina_Panthers_season "2025 Carolina Panthers season")

Young started 16 games in 2025, completing 304 of 478 passes for 3,011 yards, 23 touchdowns, and 11 interceptions; his yards, touchdowns, completion percentage, and passer rating were career highs.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-NFLStats-42) In Week 11, he passed for 448 yards, three touchdowns, and no interceptions in a 30–27 overtime win over the [Atlanta Falcons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta_Falcons "Atlanta Falcons"), breaking [Cam Newton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cam_Newton "Cam Newton")'s Panthers single-game record of 432 passing yards.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-NFLYoungRecord2025-48) The performance earned Young his first [NFC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_Conference "National Football Conference") Offensive Player of the Week award and the [FedEx Air & Ground Players of the Week](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FedEx_Air_&_Ground_NFL_Players_of_the_Week "FedEx Air & Ground NFL Players of the Week") honor.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-49)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-50)

The Panthers finished the regular season 8–9 and won the [NFC South](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFC_South "NFC South") on a three-way tiebreaker, their first division title since 2015.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-51)[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-52) Young made his postseason debut on January 10, 2026, in a 34–31 wild-card loss to the [Los Angeles Rams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Rams "Los Angeles Rams"), throwing for 264 yards and a touchdown and rushing for another score.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-53) He was ranked No. 98 by his fellow players on the [NFL Top 100 Players of 2026](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_Top_100_Players_of_2026 "NFL Top 100 Players of 2026").[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-54)

### 2026

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bryce_Young&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: 2026")]

On April 29, 2026, the Panthers exercised the fifth-year option on Young's rookie contract, keeping him under contract through the 2027 season.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryce_Young#cite_note-55)

**Coleridge Bernard** "**C. J.**" **Stroud IV** (born October 3, 2001) is an American professional [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_football "American football")[quarterback](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quarterback "Quarterback") for the [Houston Texans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_Texans "Houston Texans") of the [National Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League") (NFL). Stroud played [college football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_football "College football") for the [Ohio State Buckeyes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohio_State_Buckeyes_football "Ohio State Buckeyes football"), where he holds several school records, including most passing yards in a single game with 573, as well as being the first player to throw for six touchdowns three times. He was a [Heisman Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heisman_Trophy "Heisman Trophy") finalist in 2021 and 2022, and was subsequently selected by the Houston Texans [second overall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_second_overall_NFL_draft_picks "List of second overall NFL draft picks") in the 2023 NFL draft. In his rookie season, he led the Texans to a division title and playoff victory en route to winning the [Offensive Rookie of the Year Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League_Rookie_of_the_Year_Award "National Football League Rookie of the Year Award").

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=C._J._Stroud&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Stroud was born on October 3, 2001, in [Rancho Cucamonga, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rancho_Cucamonga,_California "Rancho Cucamonga, California"), the youngest of four children.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-:0-2) In 2014, Stroud joined [Snoop Dogg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snoop_Dogg "Snoop Dogg")'s Snoop Youth Football League aged 12 and played as a quarterback in the league for two years.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-3)

In 2016, his father, Coleridge Bernard Stroud III, received a 38-years-to-life sentence after pleading guilty to kidnapping, carjacking and robbery in connection with a drug-related incident under California's [three-strikes law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Three-strikes_law "Three-strikes law").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-4) As of 2023, his father has been incarcerated since Stroud was in middle school,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-:0-2)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-5) and is serving his sentence in [Folsom State Prison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folsom_State_Prison "Folsom State Prison") near [Sacramento](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sacramento "Sacramento"). The incarceration sent the Stroud family into severe financial debt; they lived in a small apartment above a storage facility as Stroud entered [Rancho Cucamonga High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rancho_Cucamonga_High_School "Rancho Cucamonga High School").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-8)

As a senior, he was the _[Inland Valley Daily Bulletin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inland\_Valley\_Daily\_Bulletin "Inland Valley Daily Bulletin")_ offensive player of the year after passing for 3,878 yards and 47 touchdowns.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-9) In 2019, he was the MVP of the [Elite 11](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elite_11 "Elite 11").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-10) Stroud was selected to play in the 2020 [All-American Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All-American_Bowl_(high_school_football) "All-American Bowl (high school football)").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-11) Initially considered a 3-star recruit, Stroud finished high school as the third-highest rated quarterback of his class.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-13) He committed to [Ohio State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohio_State_University "Ohio State University") to play college football.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-16)

Stroud has been friends with [Carolina Panthers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carolina_Panthers "Carolina Panthers") quarterback Bryce Young since the two went to high schools located in [Southern California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_California "Southern California"). The two continued their friendship in college, and ultimately were selected with the first two picks in the 2023 NFL draft.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-Cooney_r007-17)

## College career

### 2020 season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=C._J._Stroud&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 2020 season")]

Stroud spent his true [freshman year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freshman_year "Freshman year") at Ohio State [redshirting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Redshirt_(college_sports) "Redshirt (college sports)") as a backup to Justin Fields.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-19) He played just eight [snaps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snap_(gridiron_football) "Snap (gridiron football)") in 2020, throwing no passes, but did score a 48-yard rushing touchdown against [Michigan State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Michigan_State_Spartans_football_team "2020 Michigan State Spartans football team").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-20) He also played one snap in the [2021 Sugar Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Sugar_Bowl "2021 Sugar Bowl") against [Clemson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Clemson_Tigers_football_team "2020 Clemson Tigers football team") after Fields took a hard hit to the ribs.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-21)

### 2021 season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=C._J._Stroud&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2021 season")]

See also: [2021 Ohio State Buckeyes football team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Ohio_State_Buckeyes_football_team "2021 Ohio State Buckeyes football team")

Stroud was named the starting quarterback as a redshirt freshman following the departure of Fields to the 2021 NFL draft. He was chosen over freshmen [Kyle McCord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyle_McCord "Kyle McCord"), [Quinn Ewers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quinn_Ewers "Quinn Ewers"), and fellow redshirt freshman [Jack Miller III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Miller_III "Jack Miller III"). Coach [Ryan Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Day "Ryan Day") credited his decision-making, leadership skills, and accuracy as the reasons that he earned the starting spot.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-22)

Stroud started every game for the Buckeyes aside from a week 4 game against [Akron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Akron_Zips_football_team "2021 Akron Zips football team") in order to rest a shoulder injury he sustained in the season opener.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-23) Over the season, he earned first-team All-Big Ten Honors; was named the [Big Ten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Ten "Big Ten") quarterback of the year; won Big Ten Freshman of the Week six times; was a finalist for both the [Davey O'Brien Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Davey_O'Brien_Award "Davey O'Brien Award") and the [Heisman Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heisman_Trophy "Heisman Trophy"); and became the only quarterback in Ohio State history to throw five touchdowns against a Big Ten competitor four times in one season.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-24) He led the team to a 10–2 record in the regular season, with losses to [Oregon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Oregon_Ducks_football_team "2021 Oregon Ducks football team") and [bitter rival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michigan%E2%80%93Ohio_State_football_rivalry "Michigan–Ohio State football rivalry")[Michigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Michigan_Wolverines_football_team "2021 Michigan Wolverines football team").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-25) The loss to Michigan cost Ohio State the chance to play in the Big Ten Championship. Ohio State bounced back from this disappointment at the [Rose Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Rose_Bowl "2022 Rose Bowl"); coming back from a 14-point deficit against [Utah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Utah_Utes_football_team "2021 Utah Utes football team") to win 48–45. Stroud broke both school and Rose Bowl records with 573 yards thrown in the Rose Bowl; he also tied a school record and set a Rose Bowl record with six touchdown passes.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-26) He finished fourth in Heisman Trophy voting.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-27)

### 2023 season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=C._J._Stroud&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2023 season")]

See also: [2023 Houston Texans season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Houston_Texans_season "2023 Houston Texans season")

Stroud was selected by the [Houston Texans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_Texans "Houston Texans") with the second overall pick in the 2023 NFL draft on April 27, 2023.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-41) Being second overall, Stroud became the highest drafted quarterback in Ohio State's history.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-42) On July 24, 2023 he signed to a four-year, $36.3 million fully guaranteed rookie contract.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-43)

On September 10, 2023, Stroud made his NFL debut in week 1 against the [Baltimore Ravens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltimore_Ravens "Baltimore Ravens"), where he threw for 242 yards in the 25–9 loss.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-44) During week 2 against the [Indianapolis Colts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indianapolis_Colts "Indianapolis Colts"), Stroud threw his first two NFL touchdowns, one to [Nico Collins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nico_Collins "Nico Collins") and the other to [Tank Dell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tank_Dell "Tank Dell"), and finished with 384 passing yards in the 31–20 loss. Stroud's 384 yards are the second-most in a single game by a Texans rookie quarterback.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-45) The following week, against the [Jacksonville Jaguars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacksonville_Jaguars "Jacksonville Jaguars"), Stroud finished 20-of-30 for 280 yards with two touchdowns as the Texans won 37–17 for his first career win.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-46) He also joined [Cam Newton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cam_Newton "Cam Newton") and [Justin Herbert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert "Justin Herbert") as the only players in NFL history to put up at least 900 passing yards in their first three games.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-47) Stroud was named the Offensive Rookie of the Month for September, finishing the month with 78 completions on 121 attempts with 906 yards and four touchdowns with no interceptions.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-48)

In week 5, Stroud threw his 177th pass attempt without an interception, breaking the previous NFL record set by [Dak Prescott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dak_Prescott "Dak Prescott") for the most pass attempts without an interception to begin a career in NFL history in a 21–19 loss to the [Atlanta Falcons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta_Falcons "Atlanta Falcons").[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-49) The streak ended the following week against the [New Orleans Saints](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans_Saints "New Orleans Saints") at 191 attempts; Saints linebacker [Zack Baun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zack_Baun "Zack Baun") intercepted the pass but had the ball punched out by wide receiver [Nico Collins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nico_Collins "Nico Collins") with offensive tackle [Tytus Howard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tytus_Howard "Tytus Howard") recovering the ball for the Texans.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-50) In week 8, Stroud faced his friend and fellow top draft pick Bryce Young for the first time in the NFL. Young came out on top in a defensive battle, 15–13. Stroud threw for 140 yards and had his first rushing touchdown in the loss.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-51) In week 9, Stroud passed for 470 yards, breaking the single-game passing yard record for a rookie quarterback that was previously set by [Andrew Luck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Luck "Andrew Luck") in 2012. Stroud also passed for five touchdowns, during a 39–37 comeback victory over the [Tampa Bay Buccaneers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tampa_Bay_Buccaneers "Tampa Bay Buccaneers").[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-52) The game also marked just the third time in NFL history a quarterback has thrown for at least 470 yards and five touchdowns with no interceptions, joining [Y.A. Tittle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Y.A._Tittle "Y.A. Tittle") and [Ben Roethlisberger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Roethlisberger "Ben Roethlisberger").[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-53) He was named both AFC Offensive Player of the Month and NFL Rookie of the Month for November becoming the fifth player ever to earn both awards in the same month.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-54)

In week 14 against the [New York Jets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Jets "New York Jets"), Stroud suffered a concussion during the fourth quarter as the Texans lost 30–6.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-55) After a two-game absence, Stroud made his return in week 17 against the [Tennessee Titans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee_Titans "Tennessee Titans"), completing 24 of 32 passes for 213 yards and one touchdown in a 26–3 victory.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-56) In a win-or-go-home situation against the Colts, Stroud completed 20 of 26 passes for 264 yards and two touchdowns in a 23–19 win, clinching the Texans' first playoff berth since 2019.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-57) His performance earned him AFC Offensive Player of the Week.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-58) During this game, Stroud became just the fifth quarterback in NFL history to pass for over 4,000 yards in their rookie season.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-59) Stroud also became the third player in league history to lead the league in passing yards per game (273.9) and touchdown/interception ratio (4.6) in the same season, joining [Tom Brady](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Brady "Tom Brady") in 2007 and [Joe Montana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Montana "Joe Montana") in 1989.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-60) He was named to the PFWA All-Rookie Team.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-61) He was named the [NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_Offensive_Rookie_of_the_Year "NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year").[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-62)

In his playoff debut against the [Cleveland Browns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland_Browns "Cleveland Browns") in the [Wild Card round](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_NFL_playoffs#AFC:_Houston_Texans_45,_Cleveland_Browns_14 "2023–24 NFL playoffs"), Stroud tied the rookie record for most passing touchdowns in a playoff game and became the youngest quarterback to win a playoff game in league history as the Texans won 45–14.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-CBS_Jan_14_2024-63) Stroud finished the game completing 16 of 21 passes for 274 yards, three touchdowns, and a [near-perfect passer rating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_NFL_players_who_have_posted_a_perfect_passer_rating "List of NFL players who have posted a perfect passer rating") of 157.2.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-64) In the [Divisional round](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_NFL_playoffs#AFC:_Baltimore_Ravens_34,_Houston_Texans_10 "2023–24 NFL playoffs") against the top-seeded Ravens in a rematch of week 1, Stroud was held in check, completing 19 of 33 passes for 175 yards and a 72.2 rating as the Texans lost, 34–10.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-65) He was ranked 20th by his fellow players on the [NFL Top 100 Players of 2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_Top_100_Players_of_2024 "NFL Top 100 Players of 2024").[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-66)

### 2024 season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=C._J._Stroud&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: 2024 season")]

See also: [2024 Houston Texans season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Houston_Texans_season "2024 Houston Texans season")

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/57/CJSTROUD2024.jpg/250px-CJSTROUD2024.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:CJSTROUD2024.jpg)

Stroud in 2024

Stroud began the season by leading the Texans to back-to-back victories over the [Indianapolis Colts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indianapolis_Colts "Indianapolis Colts") and [Chicago Bears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Bears "Chicago Bears"), throwing for a combined 494 yards, three touchdowns, and no turnovers.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-z440-67)[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-r628-68) In week 4 against the [Jacksonville Jaguars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacksonville_Jaguars "Jacksonville Jaguars"), Stroud passed for 345 yards and two touchdowns, leading the Texans on a nine-play, 69-yard touchdown drive with under 20 seconds remaining to secure a 24–20 victory.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-69) In week 6, Stroud threw for 192 yards with three touchdowns in the 41–21 win over the [New England Patriots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_England_Patriots "New England Patriots"), improving to 5–1 on the season.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-70)

Despite a strong start, Stroud faced challenges during his sophomore season. In week 7 against the [Green Bay Packers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Bay_Packers "Green Bay Packers"), Stroud completed under half his passes for 86 yards in a 24–22 loss.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-71) Against the [New York Jets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Jets "New York Jets") in week 9, Stroud completed only 11-of-30 passes and was sacked eight times in a 21–13 loss.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-72) On _[Sunday Night Football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC\_Sunday\_Night\_Football "NBC Sunday Night Football")_ in week 10, he recorded 232 passing yards and a touchdown but threw two interceptions to [Detroit Lions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detroit_Lions "Detroit Lions") cornerback [Carlton Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlton_Davis "Carlton Davis") as the Texans lost 26–23, despite leading 23–7 at one point.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-73) Stroud threw two more interceptions in a week 12 upset loss to the Titans as the Texans dropped to 7–5.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-74)

On [Christmas Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_on_Christmas_Day "NFL on Christmas Day") against the [Baltimore Ravens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltimore_Ravens "Baltimore Ravens"), Stroud had one of the worst outings of his career, completing 54.8% of his passes for 185 yards and an interception in a 31–2 loss. His passer rating of 59.2 was one of the lowest of his career.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-f837-75) Stroud finished his second season with 3,727 yards, a 63.2 completion percentage, 20 touchdowns, 12 interceptions, an 87.0 passer rating, and 52 sacks, all of which were a decline from his breakout rookie campaign.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-76) Despite a 5–6 finish to the season, the Texans were still able to clinch their second consecutive AFC South title.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-77) In the Wild Card round against the [Los Angeles Chargers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Chargers "Los Angeles Chargers"), Stroud completed 22 of 33 passes, accompanied with a touchdown and an interception as he led the Texans to a 32–12 home victory[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-z369-78)[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-79) including a busted play in the second quarter where Stroud recovered a botched snap near his own end zone and connected with [Xavier Hutchinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xavier_Hutchinson "Xavier Hutchinson") for a 34-yard gain.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-80) Stroud and the Texans saw their season end once again in the [Divisional Round](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024%E2%80%9325_NFL_playoffs#AFC:_Kansas_City_Chiefs_23,_Houston_Texans_14 "2024–25 NFL playoffs"), this time being a 23–14 loss to the Chiefs.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-c331-81) He was ranked 39th by his fellow players on the [NFL Top 100 Players of 2025](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_Top_100_Players_of_2025 "NFL Top 100 Players of 2025").[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-82)

### 2025 season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=C._J._Stroud&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: 2025 season")]

See also: [2025 Houston Texans season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Houston_Texans_season "2025 Houston Texans season")

In Week 5, Stroud completed 23 of 27 passes for 244 yards and four touchdowns in a 44–10 win over the [Baltimore Ravens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Baltimore_Ravens_season "2025 Baltimore Ravens season"), earning AFC Offensive Player of the Week.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-83)

In a 18–15 loss to the [Denver Broncos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Denver_Broncos_season "2025 Denver Broncos season") in Week 9, Stroud got hit hard by [Kris Abrams-Draine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Abrams-Draine "Kris Abrams-Draine") early in the 2nd quarter, which gave him a concussion.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-84) He missed the next three games.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-85) Stroud finished 2025 with 3,041 yards, 19 touchdowns, and 8 interceptions for a passer rating of 92.9.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-86) In the [wild card round](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025%E2%80%9326_NFL_playoffs#AFC:_Houston_Texans_30,_Pittsburgh_Steelers_6 "2025–26 NFL playoffs") against the [Pittsburgh Steelers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Pittsburgh_Steelers_season "2025 Pittsburgh Steelers season"), Stroud threw for 250 yards, accompanied by a touchdown and an interception in the 30–6 road victory.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-87) In the [divisional round](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025%E2%80%9326_NFL_playoffs#AFC:_New_England_Patriots_28,_Houston_Texans_16 "2025–26 NFL playoffs") matchup vs the [New England Patriots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_New_England_Patriots_season "2025 New England Patriots season"), Stroud struggled heavily, completing 20 for 47 passes for 212 yards with one touchdown and four interceptions in a 28–16 loss.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-88) Stroud's 4 first-half interceptions were tied for the most in an [NFL playoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_playoffs "NFL playoffs") game since [Jake Delhomme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Delhomme "Jake Delhomme") threw 5 in [2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008 "2008").[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-89)

**Coleridge Bernard** "**C. J.**" **Stroud IV** (born October 3, 2001) is an American professional [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_football "American football")[quarterback](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quarterback "Quarterback") for the [Houston Texans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_Texans "Houston Texans") of the [National Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League") (NFL). Stroud played [college football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_football "College football") for the [Ohio State Buckeyes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohio_State_Buckeyes_football "Ohio State Buckeyes football"), where he holds several school records, including most passing yards in a single game with 573, as well as being the first player to throw for six touchdowns three times. He was a [Heisman Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heisman_Trophy "Heisman Trophy") finalist in 2021 and 2022, and was subsequently selected by the Houston Texans [second overall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_second_overall_NFL_draft_picks "List of second overall NFL draft picks") in the 2023 NFL draft. In his rookie season, he led the Texans to a division title and playoff victory en route to winning the [Offensive Rookie of the Year Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League_Rookie_of_the_Year_Award "National Football League Rookie of the Year Award").

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=C._J._Stroud&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Stroud was born on October 3, 2001, in [Rancho Cucamonga, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rancho_Cucamonga,_California "Rancho Cucamonga, California"), the youngest of four children.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-:0-2) In 2014, Stroud joined [Snoop Dogg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snoop_Dogg "Snoop Dogg")'s Snoop Youth Football League aged 12 and played as a quarterback in the league for two years.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-3)

In 2016, his father, Coleridge Bernard Stroud III, received a 38-years-to-life sentence after pleading guilty to kidnapping, carjacking and robbery in connection with a drug-related incident under California's [three-strikes law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Three-strikes_law "Three-strikes law").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-4) As of 2023, his father has been incarcerated since Stroud was in middle school,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-:0-2)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-5) and is serving his sentence in [Folsom State Prison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folsom_State_Prison "Folsom State Prison") near [Sacramento](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sacramento "Sacramento"). The incarceration sent the Stroud family into severe financial debt; they lived in a small apartment above a storage facility as Stroud entered [Rancho Cucamonga High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rancho_Cucamonga_High_School "Rancho Cucamonga High School").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-8)

As a senior, he was the _[Inland Valley Daily Bulletin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inland\_Valley\_Daily\_Bulletin "Inland Valley Daily Bulletin")_ offensive player of the year after passing for 3,878 yards and 47 touchdowns.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-9) In 2019, he was the MVP of the [Elite 11](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elite_11 "Elite 11").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-10) Stroud was selected to play in the 2020 [All-American Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All-American_Bowl_(high_school_football) "All-American Bowl (high school football)").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-11) Initially considered a 3-star recruit, Stroud finished high school as the third-highest rated quarterback of his class.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-13) He committed to [Ohio State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohio_State_University "Ohio State University") to play college football.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-16)

Stroud has been friends with [Carolina Panthers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carolina_Panthers "Carolina Panthers") quarterback Bryce Young since the two went to high schools located in [Southern California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_California "Southern California"). The two continued their friendship in college, and ultimately were selected with the first two picks in the 2023 NFL draft.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-Cooney_r007-17)

## College career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=C._J._Stroud&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: College career")]

### 2020 season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=C._J._Stroud&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 2020 season")]

See also: [2020 Ohio State Buckeyes football team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Ohio_State_Buckeyes_football_team "2020 Ohio State Buckeyes football team")

Stroud spent his true [freshman year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freshman_year "Freshman year") at Ohio State [redshirting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Redshirt_(college_sports) "Redshirt (college sports)") as a backup to Justin Fields.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-19) He played just eight [snaps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snap_(gridiron_football) "Snap (gridiron football)") in 2020, throwing no passes, but did score a 48-yard rushing touchdown against [Michigan State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Michigan_State_Spartans_football_team "2020 Michigan State Spartans football team").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-20) He also played one snap in the [2021 Sugar Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Sugar_Bowl "2021 Sugar Bowl") against [Clemson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Clemson_Tigers_football_team "2020 Clemson Tigers football team") after Fields took a hard hit to the ribs.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-21)

### 2021 season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=C._J._Stroud&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2021 season")]

See also: [2021 Ohio State Buckeyes football team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Ohio_State_Buckeyes_football_team "2021 Ohio State Buckeyes football team")

Stroud was named the starting quarterback as a redshirt freshman following the departure of Fields to the 2021 NFL draft. He was chosen over freshmen [Kyle McCord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyle_McCord "Kyle McCord"), [Quinn Ewers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quinn_Ewers "Quinn Ewers"), and fellow redshirt freshman [Jack Miller III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Miller_III "Jack Miller III"). Coach [Ryan Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Day "Ryan Day") credited his decision-making, leadership skills, and accuracy as the reasons that he earned the starting spot.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-22)

Stroud started every game for the Buckeyes aside from a week 4 game against [Akron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Akron_Zips_football_team "2021 Akron Zips football team") in order to rest a shoulder injury he sustained in the season opener.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-23) Over the season, he earned first-team All-Big Ten Honors; was named the [Big Ten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Ten "Big Ten") quarterback of the year; won Big Ten Freshman of the Week six times; was a finalist for both the [Davey O'Brien Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Davey_O'Brien_Award "Davey O'Brien Award") and the [Heisman Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heisman_Trophy "Heisman Trophy"); and became the only quarterback in Ohio State history to throw five touchdowns against a Big Ten competitor four times in one season.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-24) He led the team to a 10–2 record in the regular season, with losses to [Oregon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Oregon_Ducks_football_team "2021 Oregon Ducks football team") and [bitter rival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michigan%E2%80%93Ohio_State_football_rivalry "Michigan–Ohio State football rivalry")[Michigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Michigan_Wolverines_football_team "2021 Michigan Wolverines football team").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-25) The loss to Michigan cost Ohio State the chance to play in the Big Ten Championship. Ohio State bounced back from this disappointment at the [Rose Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Rose_Bowl "2022 Rose Bowl"); coming back from a 14-point deficit against [Utah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Utah_Utes_football_team "2021 Utah Utes football team") to win 48–45. Stroud broke both school and Rose Bowl records with 573 yards thrown in the Rose Bowl; he also tied a school record and set a Rose Bowl record with six touchdown passes.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-26) He finished fourth in Heisman Trophy voting.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-27)

[NCAA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NCAA_Division_I_Football_Bowl_Subdivision "NCAA Division I Football Bowl Subdivision") with a [passer rating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passer_rating "Passer rating") of 177.7 and was again was named a finalist for the Heisman ### 2023 season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=C._J._Stroud&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2023 season")]

See also: [2023 Houston Texans season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Houston_Texans_season "2023 Houston Texans season")

Stroud was selected by the [Houston Texans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_Texans "Houston Texans") with the second overall pick in the 2023 NFL draft on April 27, 2023.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-41) Being second overall, Stroud became the highest drafted quarterback in Ohio State's history.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-42) On July 24, 2023 he signed to a four-year, $36.3 million fully guaranteed rookie contract.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-43)

On September 10, 2023, Stroud made his NFL debut in week 1 against the [Baltimore Ravens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltimore_Ravens "Baltimore Ravens"), where he threw for 242 yards in the 25–9 loss.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-44) During week 2 against the [Indianapolis Colts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indianapolis_Colts "Indianapolis Colts"), Stroud threw his first two NFL touchdowns, one to [Nico Collins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nico_Collins "Nico Collins") and the other to [Tank Dell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tank_Dell "Tank Dell"), and finished with 384 passing yards in the 31–20 loss. Stroud's 384 yards are the second-most in a single game by a Texans rookie quarterback.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-45) The following week, against the [Jacksonville Jaguars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacksonville_Jaguars "Jacksonville Jaguars"), Stroud finished 20-of-30 for 280 yards with two touchdowns as the Texans won 37–17 for his first career win.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-46) He also joined [Cam Newton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cam_Newton "Cam Newton") and [Justin Herbert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert "Justin Herbert") as the only players in NFL history to put up at least 900 passing yards in their first three games.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-47) Stroud was named the Offensive Rookie of the Month for September, finishing the month with 78 completions on 121 attempts with 906 yards and four touchdowns with no interceptions.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-48)

In week 5, Stroud threw his 177th pass attempt without an interception, breaking the previous NFL record set by [Dak Prescott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dak_Prescott "Dak Prescott") for the most pass attempts without an interception to begin a career in NFL history in a 21–19 loss to the [Atlanta Falcons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta_Falcons "Atlanta Falcons").[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-49) The streak ended the following week against the [New Orleans Saints](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans_Saints "New Orleans Saints") at 191 attempts; Saints linebacker [Zack Baun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zack_Baun "Zack Baun") intercepted the pass but had the ball punched out by wide receiver [Nico Collins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nico_Collins "Nico Collins") with offensive tackle [Tytus Howard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tytus_Howard "Tytus Howard") recovering the ball for the Texans.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-50) In week 8, Stroud faced his friend and fellow top draft pick Bryce Young for the first time in the NFL. Young came out on top in a defensive battle, 15–13. Stroud threw for 140 yards and had his first rushing touchdown in the loss.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-51) In week 9, Stroud passed for 470 yards, breaking the single-game passing yard record for a rookie quarterback that was previously set by [Andrew Luck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Luck "Andrew Luck") in 2012. Stroud also passed for five touchdowns, during a 39–37 comeback victory over the [Tampa Bay Buccaneers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tampa_Bay_Buccaneers "Tampa Bay Buccaneers").[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-52) The game also marked just the third time in NFL history a quarterback has thrown for at least 470 yards and five touchdowns with no interceptions, joining [Y.A. Tittle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Y.A._Tittle "Y.A. Tittle") and [Ben Roethlisberger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Roethlisberger "Ben Roethlisberger").[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-53) He was named both AFC Offensive Player of the Month and NFL Rookie of the Month for November becoming the fifth player ever to earn both awards in the same month.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-54)

In week 14 against the [New York Jets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Jets "New York Jets"), Stroud suffered a concussion during the fourth quarter as the Texans lost 30–6.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-55) After a two-game absence, Stroud made his return in week 17 against the [Tennessee Titans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee_Titans "Tennessee Titans"), completing 24 of 32 passes for 213 yards and one touchdown in a 26–3 victory.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-56) In a win-or-go-home situation against the Colts, Stroud completed 20 of 26 passes for 264 yards and two touchdowns in a 23–19 win, clinching the Texans' first playoff berth since 2019.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-57) His performance earned him AFC Offensive Player of the Week.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-58) During this game, Stroud became just the fifth quarterback in NFL history to pass for over 4,000 yards in their rookie season.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-59) Stroud also became the third player in league history to lead the league in passing yards per game (273.9) and touchdown/interception ratio (4.6) in the same season, joining [Tom Brady](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Brady "Tom Brady") in 2007 and [Joe Montana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Montana "Joe Montana") in 1989.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-60) He was named to the PFWA All-Rookie Team.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-61) He was named the [NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_Offensive_Rookie_of_the_Year "NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year").[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-62)

In his playoff debut against the [Cleveland Browns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland_Browns "Cleveland Browns") in the [Wild Card round](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_NFL_playoffs#AFC:_Houston_Texans_45,_Cleveland_Browns_14 "2023–24 NFL playoffs"), Stroud tied the rookie record for most passing touchdowns in a playoff game and became the youngest quarterback to win a playoff game in league history as the Texans won 45–14.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-CBS_Jan_14_2024-63) Stroud finished the game completing 16 of 21 passes for 274 yards, three touchdowns, and a [near-perfect passer rating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_NFL_players_who_have_posted_a_perfect_passer_rating "List of NFL players who have posted a perfect passer rating") of 157.2.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-64) In the [Divisional round](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_NFL_playoffs#AFC:_Baltimore_Ravens_34,_Houston_Texans_10 "2023–24 NFL playoffs") against the top-seeded Ravens in a rematch of week 1, Stroud was held in check, completing 19 of 33 passes for 175 yards and a 72.2 rating as the Texans lost, 34–10.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-65) He was ranked 20th by his fellow players on the [NFL Top 100 Players of 2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_Top_100_Players_of_2024 "NFL Top 100 Players of 2024").[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-66)

### 2024 season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=C._J._Stroud&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: 2024 season")]

See also: [2024 Houston Texans season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Houston_Texans_season "2024 Houston Texans season")

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/57/CJSTROUD2024.jpg/250px-CJSTROUD2024.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:CJSTROUD2024.jpg)

Stroud in 2024

Stroud began the season by leading the Texans to back-to-back victories over the [Indianapolis Colts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indianapolis_Colts "Indianapolis Colts") and [Chicago Bears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Bears "Chicago Bears"), throwing for a combined 494 yards, three touchdowns, and no turnovers.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-z440-67)[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-r628-68) In week 4 against the [Jacksonville Jaguars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacksonville_Jaguars "Jacksonville Jaguars"), Stroud passed for 345 yards and two touchdowns, leading the Texans on a nine-play, 69-yard touchdown drive with under 20 seconds remaining to secure a 24–20 victory.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-69) In week 6, Stroud threw for 192 yards with three touchdowns in the 41–21 win over the [New England Patriots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_England_Patriots "New England Patriots"), improving to 5–1 on the season.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-70)

Despite a strong start, Stroud faced challenges during his sophomore season. In week 7 against the [Green Bay Packers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Bay_Packers "Green Bay Packers"), Stroud completed under half his passes for 86 yards in a 24–22 loss.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-71) Against the [New York Jets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Jets "New York Jets") in week 9, Stroud completed only 11-of-30 passes and was sacked eight times in a 21–13 loss.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-72) On _[Sunday Night Football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC\_Sunday\_Night\_Football "NBC Sunday Night Football")_ in week 10, he recorded 232 passing yards and a touchdown but threw two interceptions to [Detroit Lions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detroit_Lions "Detroit Lions") cornerback [Carlton Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlton_Davis "Carlton Davis") as the Texans lost 26–23, despite leading 23–7 at one point.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-73) Stroud threw two more interceptions in a week 12 upset loss to the Titans as the Texans dropped to 7–5.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-74)

On [Christmas Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_on_Christmas_Day "NFL on Christmas Day") against the [Baltimore Ravens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltimore_Ravens "Baltimore Ravens"), Stroud had one of the worst outings of his career, completing 54.8% of his passes for 185 yards and an interception in a 31–2 loss. His passer rating of 59.2 was one of the lowest of his career.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-f837-75) Stroud finished his second season with 3,727 yards, a 63.2 completion percentage, 20 touchdowns, 12 interceptions, an 87.0 passer rating, and 52 sacks, all of which were a decline from his breakout rookie campaign.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-76) Despite a 5–6 finish to the season, the Texans were still able to clinch their second consecutive AFC South title.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-77) In the Wild Card round against the [Los Angeles Chargers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Chargers "Los Angeles Chargers"), Stroud completed 22 of 33 passes, accompanied with a touchdown and an interception as he led the Texans to a 32–12 home victory[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-z369-78)[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-79) including a busted play in the second quarter where Stroud recovered a botched snap near his own end zone and connected with [Xavier Hutchinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xavier_Hutchinson "Xavier Hutchinson") for a 34-yard gain.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-80) Stroud and the Texans saw their season end once again in the [Divisional Round](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024%E2%80%9325_NFL_playoffs#AFC:_Kansas_City_Chiefs_23,_Houston_Texans_14 "2024–25 NFL playoffs"), this time being a 23–14 loss to the Chiefs.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-c331-81) He was ranked 39th by his fellow players on the [NFL Top 100 Players of 2025](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_Top_100_Players_of_2025 "NFL Top 100 Players of 2025").[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-82)

### 2025 season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=C._J._Stroud&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: 2025 season")]

See also: [2025 Houston Texans season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Houston_Texans_season "2025 Houston Texans season")

In Week 5, Stroud completed 23 of 27 passes for 244 yards and four touchdowns in a 44–10 win over the [Baltimore Ravens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Baltimore_Ravens_season "2025 Baltimore Ravens season"), earning AFC Offensive Player of the Week.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-83)

In a 18–15 loss to the [Denver Broncos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Denver_Broncos_season "2025 Denver Broncos season") in Week 9, Stroud got hit hard by [Kris Abrams-Draine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Abrams-Draine "Kris Abrams-Draine") early in the 2nd quarter, which gave him a concussion.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-84) He missed the next three games.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-85) Stroud finished 2025 with 3,041 yards, 19 touchdowns, and 8 interceptions for a passer rating of 92.9.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-86) In the [wild card round](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025%E2%80%9326_NFL_playoffs#AFC:_Houston_Texans_30,_Pittsburgh_Steelers_6 "2025–26 NFL playoffs") against the [Pittsburgh Steelers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Pittsburgh_Steelers_season "2025 Pittsburgh Steelers season"), Stroud threw for 250 yards, accompanied by a touchdown and an interception in the 30–6 road victory.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-87) In the [divisional round](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025%E2%80%9326_NFL_playoffs#AFC:_New_England_Patriots_28,_Houston_Texans_16 "2025–26 NFL playoffs") matchup vs the [New England Patriots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_New_England_Patriots_season "2025 New England Patriots season"), Stroud struggled heavily, completing 20 for 47 passes for 212 yards with one touchdown and four interceptions in a 28–16 loss.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-88) Stroud's 4 first-half interceptions were tied for the most in an [NFL playoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_playoffs "NFL playoffs") game since [Jake Delhomme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Delhomme "Jake Delhomme") threw 5 in [2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008 "2008").[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._J._Stroud#cite_note-89)

**Malik Antonio Willis** ([/m ə ˈ l iː k/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English")[_mə-LEEK_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key"); born May 25, 1999) is an American professional [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_football "American football")[quarterback](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quarterback "Quarterback") for the [Miami Dolphins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_Dolphins "Miami Dolphins") of the [National Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League") (NFL). He played [college football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_football "College football") for the [Auburn Tigers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auburn_Tigers_football "Auburn Tigers football") and [Liberty Flames](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberty_Flames_football "Liberty Flames football"), winning the 2020 [Dudley Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dudley_Award "Dudley Award") with the latter. Willis was selected by the [Tennessee Titans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee_Titans "Tennessee Titans") in the third round of the [2022 NFL draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NFL_draft "2022 NFL draft") and was traded to the [Green Bay Packers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Bay_Packers "Green Bay Packers") in 2024. He served as a backup in Green Bay for two seasons before signing with the Dolphins in 2026.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Malik_Willis&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Willis attended [Westlake High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westlake_High_School_(Georgia) "Westlake High School (Georgia)") in [Atlanta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta "Atlanta") before transferring to [Roswell High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roswell_High_School_(Georgia) "Roswell High School (Georgia)") in [Roswell, Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roswell,_Georgia "Roswell, Georgia"), for his senior year.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-1) As a senior, Willis passed for 2,562 yards and rushed for 1,033 yards with 37 total touchdowns. A three star recruit, he committed to [Auburn University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auburn_University "Auburn University") to play [college football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_football "College football").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-3)

## College career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Malik_Willis&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: College career")]

### Auburn

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Malik_Willis&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Auburn")]

Willis spent 2017 and 2018 at Auburn and played in 15 games. During the two years, he completed 11 of 14 passes for 69 yards and a [touchdown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Touchdown "Touchdown") and rushed for 309 yards and two touchdowns.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-5)

### Liberty

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Malik_Willis&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Liberty")]

Willis transferred to [Liberty University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberty_University "Liberty University") in 2019 following a quarterback competition at Auburn with [Bo Nix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bo_Nix "Bo Nix") and sat out the season due to transfer rules.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-6)

In 2020, Willis was named the team's starting quarterback.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-7) Against the [Southern Miss Golden Eagles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Southern_Miss_Golden_Eagles_football_team "2020 Southern Miss Golden Eagles football team"), he threw for six touchdowns and rushed for another. Willis was named the winner of the 2020 [Dudley Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dudley_Award "Dudley Award"), given to the best college football player in the state of [Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia "Virginia"), and was the recipient of the 2021 [Bobby Bowden Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bobby_Bowden_Award "Bobby Bowden Award"), awarded to the best college football player who epitomizes being a [Christian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christianity "Christianity") student-athlete.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-10) He was named MVP of the [2020 Cure Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Cure_Bowl "2020 Cure Bowl") and the [2021 LendingTree Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_LendingTree_Bowl "2021 LendingTree Bowl").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-11)

### Tennessee Titans

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Malik_Willis&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Tennessee Titans")]

#### 2022 season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Malik_Willis&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2022 season")]

Willis was selected in the third round (86th overall) of the [2022 NFL draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NFL_draft "2022 NFL draft") by the [Tennessee Titans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee_Titans "Tennessee Titans").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-15) He was considered a surprise fall in the draft as he was projected by some to be selected as high as second overall.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-17) Willis signed his four-year rookie contract on July 23, 2022.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-18)

Willis made his NFL debut in Week 2 against the [Buffalo Bills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buffalo_Bills "Buffalo Bills") in the third quarter after the Titans benched [Ryan Tannehill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Tannehill "Ryan Tannehill"). He completed one of four passes for six yards and rushed for 16 yards during the 41–7 road loss.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-19) Willis was named the starter for the Week 8 matchup against the [Houston Texans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_Texans "Houston Texans"), relieving Tannehill due to illness.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-20) In his first start, Willis completed 6 of 10 pass attempts for 55 yards and an interception during the 17–10 road victory.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-21) Willis started in place of an injured Tannehill the following week against the [Kansas City Chiefs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City_Chiefs "Kansas City Chiefs") on [_Sunday Night Football_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC_Sunday_Night_Football "NBC Sunday Night Football").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-22) He completed 5-of-16 passes for 80 yards to go along with 40 rushing yards in the 20–17 overtime road loss.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-23) During Week 16 against the Texans, Willis again started in place of Tannehill, who had aggravated an ankle injury. Willis finished the 19–14 loss completing 14-of-23 passes for 99 yards and two interceptions, as well as rushing for 43 yards and a touchdown.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-e374-24)

#### 2023 season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Malik_Willis&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: 2023 season")]

Willis only attempted five passes in 2023.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-pfr-25)

### Green Bay Packers

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Malik_Willis&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Green Bay Packers")]

#### 2024 season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Malik_Willis&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: 2024 season")]

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/dd/2024_GB_vs_TEN_Malik_Willis.png/250px-2024_GB_vs_TEN_Malik_Willis.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2024_GB_vs_TEN_Malik_Willis.png)

Willis in 2024

On August 26, 2024, Willis was traded to the [Green Bay Packers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Bay_Packers "Green Bay Packers") for a seventh-round pick (No. 239) in the [2025 NFL draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_NFL_draft "2025 NFL draft").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-26)

After [Jordan Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan_Love "Jordan Love") suffered an MCL sprain in the season opener against the [Philadelphia Eagles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_Eagles "Philadelphia Eagles"), Willis was named the starter for the Week 2 matchup against the [Indianapolis Colts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indianapolis_Colts "Indianapolis Colts").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-g542-27) In his first start of the season, Willis completed 12-of-14 passes for 122 yards and his first NFL touchdown while also rushing for 41 yards in the 16–10 victory.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-w143-28) In the next game against his former Titans, Willis completed 13-of-19 passes for 202 yards and a touchdown and led the team in rushing with 73 yards and a touchdown during the 30–14 road victory.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-29) With Love healthy, Willis did not appear again until Week 8 against the [Jacksonville Jaguars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacksonville_Jaguars "Jacksonville Jaguars"), leading the Packers to a game-winning drive after Love left with a groin injury in the second half.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-30)

#### 2025 season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Malik_Willis&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: 2025 season")]

Willis did not make an appearance until the Week 11 27–20 road victory against the [New York Giants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_New_York_Giants_season "2025 New York Giants season"). Taking over for an injured Jordan Love, Willis entered the game with the ball on the Giants' 40-yard line and capped a six-play drive with a touchdown pass before Love returned for the next series.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-31) During Week 16 against the [Chicago Bears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Chicago_Bears_season "2025 Chicago Bears season"), Willis entered the game after Love suffered a concussion in the second quarter.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-32) Willis finished the 22–16 overtime road loss completing 9-of-11 passes for 121 yards and a touchdown while also rushing for 44 yards.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-33) He had his first start of the season during Week 17 at home against the [Baltimore Ravens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltimore_Ravens "Baltimore Ravens") while Love was still out on concussion protocol. Willis completed 18-of-21 passes for 288 yards and a touchdown, while also rushing for 60 yards and 2 touchdowns, and finished the game with a 134.6 passer rating.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-34)

### Miami Dolphins

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Malik_Willis&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Miami Dolphins")]

On March 12, 2026, Willis signed with the [Miami Dolphins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_Dolphins "Miami Dolphins") on a three-year, $67.5 million deal.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-35)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Malik_Willis&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Willis' uncle is former NFL linebacker [James Anderson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Anderson_(American_football) "James Anderson (American football)").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-36)

Willis was raised as and remains a [Christian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christianity "Christianity"). Most of his social media posts conclude with "TGFE," which is short for "Thank God for Everything."[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-37)
