**Malik Antonio Willis** ([/m ə ˈ l iː k/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English")[_mə-LEEK_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key"); born May 25, 1999) is an American professional [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_football "American football")[quarterback](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quarterback "Quarterback") for the [Miami Dolphins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_Dolphins "Miami Dolphins") of the [National Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League") (NFL). He played [college football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_football "College football") for the [Auburn Tigers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auburn_Tigers_football "Auburn Tigers football") and [Liberty Flames](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberty_Flames_football "Liberty Flames football"), winning the 2020 [Dudley Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dudley_Award "Dudley Award") with the latter. Willis was selected by the [Tennessee Titans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee_Titans "Tennessee Titans") in the third round of the [2022 NFL draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NFL_draft "2022 NFL draft") and was traded to the [Green Bay Packers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Bay_Packers "Green Bay Packers") in 2024. He served as a backup in Green Bay for two seasons before signing with the Dolphins in 2026.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Malik_Willis&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Willis attended [Westlake High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westlake_High_School_(Georgia) "Westlake High School (Georgia)") in [Atlanta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta "Atlanta") before transferring to [Roswell High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roswell_High_School_(Georgia) "Roswell High School (Georgia)") in [Roswell, Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roswell,_Georgia "Roswell, Georgia"), for his senior year.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-1) As a senior, Willis passed for 2,562 yards and rushed for 1,033 yards with 37 total touchdowns. A three star recruit, he committed to [Auburn University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auburn_University "Auburn University") to play [college football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_football "College football").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-3)

## College career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Malik_Willis&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: College career")]

### Auburn

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Malik_Willis&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Auburn")]

Willis spent 2017 and 2018 at Auburn and played in 15 games. During the two years, he completed 11 of 14 passes for 69 yards and a [touchdown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Touchdown "Touchdown") and rushed for 309 yards and two touchdowns.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-5)

### Liberty

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Malik_Willis&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Liberty")]

Willis transferred to [Liberty University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberty_University "Liberty University") in 2019 following a quarterback competition at Auburn with [Bo Nix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bo_Nix "Bo Nix") and sat out the season due to transfer rules.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-6)

In 2020, Willis was named the team's starting quarterback.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-7) Against the [Southern Miss Golden Eagles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Southern_Miss_Golden_Eagles_football_team "2020 Southern Miss Golden Eagles football team"), he threw for six touchdowns and rushed for another. Willis was named the winner of the 2020 [Dudley Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dudley_Award "Dudley Award"), given to the best college football player in the state of [Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia "Virginia"), and was the recipient of the 2021 [Bobby Bowden Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bobby_Bowden_Award "Bobby Bowden Award"), awarded to the best college football player who epitomizes being a [Christian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christianity "Christianity") student-athlete.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-10) He was named MVP of the [2020 Cure Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Cure_Bowl "2020 Cure Bowl") and the [2021 LendingTree Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_LendingTree_Bowl "2021 LendingTree Bowl").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-11)

### Tennessee Titans

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Malik_Willis&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Tennessee Titans")]

#### 2022 season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Malik_Willis&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2022 season")]

Willis was selected in the third round (86th overall) of the [2022 NFL draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NFL_draft "2022 NFL draft") by the [Tennessee Titans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee_Titans "Tennessee Titans").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-15) He was considered a surprise fall in the draft as he was projected by some to be selected as high as second overall.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-17) Willis signed his four-year rookie contract on July 23, 2022.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-18)

Willis made his NFL debut in Week 2 against the [Buffalo Bills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buffalo_Bills "Buffalo Bills") in the third quarter after the Titans benched [Ryan Tannehill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Tannehill "Ryan Tannehill"). He completed one of four passes for six yards and rushed for 16 yards during the 41–7 road loss.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-19) Willis was named the starter for the Week 8 matchup against the [Houston Texans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_Texans "Houston Texans"), relieving Tannehill due to illness.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-20) In his first start, Willis completed 6 of 10 pass attempts for 55 yards and an interception during the 17–10 road victory.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-21) Willis started in place of an injured Tannehill the following week against the [Kansas City Chiefs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City_Chiefs "Kansas City Chiefs") on [_Sunday Night Football_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC_Sunday_Night_Football "NBC Sunday Night Football").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-22) He completed 5-of-16 passes for 80 yards to go along with 40 rushing yards in the 20–17 overtime road loss.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-23) During Week 16 against the Texans, Willis again started in place of Tannehill, who had aggravated an ankle injury. Willis finished the 19–14 loss completing 14-of-23 passes for 99 yards and two interceptions, as well as rushing for 43 yards and a touchdown.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-e374-24)

#### 2023 season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Malik_Willis&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: 2023 season")]

Willis only attempted five passes in 2023.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-pfr-25)

### Green Bay Packers

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Malik_Willis&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Green Bay Packers")]

#### 2024 season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Malik_Willis&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: 2024 season")]

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/dd/2024_GB_vs_TEN_Malik_Willis.png/250px-2024_GB_vs_TEN_Malik_Willis.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2024_GB_vs_TEN_Malik_Willis.png)

Willis in 2024

On August 26, 2024, Willis was traded to the [Green Bay Packers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Bay_Packers "Green Bay Packers") for a seventh-round pick (No. 239) in the [2025 NFL draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_NFL_draft "2025 NFL draft").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-26)

After [Jordan Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan_Love "Jordan Love") suffered an MCL sprain in the season opener against the [Philadelphia Eagles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_Eagles "Philadelphia Eagles"), Willis was named the starter for the Week 2 matchup against the [Indianapolis Colts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indianapolis_Colts "Indianapolis Colts").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-g542-27) In his first start of the season, Willis completed 12-of-14 passes for 122 yards and his first NFL touchdown while also rushing for 41 yards in the 16–10 victory.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-w143-28) In the next game against his former Titans, Willis completed 13-of-19 passes for 202 yards and a touchdown and led the team in rushing with 73 yards and a touchdown during the 30–14 road victory.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-29) With Love healthy, Willis did not appear again until Week 8 against the [Jacksonville Jaguars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacksonville_Jaguars "Jacksonville Jaguars"), leading the Packers to a game-winning drive after Love left with a groin injury in the second half.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-30)

#### 2025 season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Malik_Willis&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: 2025 season")]

Willis did not make an appearance until the Week 11 27–20 road victory against the [New York Giants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_New_York_Giants_season "2025 New York Giants season"). Taking over for an injured Jordan Love, Willis entered the game with the ball on the Giants' 40-yard line and capped a six-play drive with a touchdown pass before Love returned for the next series.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-31) During Week 16 against the [Chicago Bears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Chicago_Bears_season "2025 Chicago Bears season"), Willis entered the game after Love suffered a concussion in the second quarter.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-32) Willis finished the 22–16 overtime road loss completing 9-of-11 passes for 121 yards and a touchdown while also rushing for 44 yards.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-33) He had his first start of the season during Week 17 at home against the [Baltimore Ravens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltimore_Ravens "Baltimore Ravens") while Love was still out on concussion protocol. Willis completed 18-of-21 passes for 288 yards and a touchdown, while also rushing for 60 yards and 2 touchdowns, and finished the game with a 134.6 passer rating.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-34)

### Miami Dolphins

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Malik_Willis&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Miami Dolphins")]

On March 12, 2026, Willis signed with the [Miami Dolphins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_Dolphins "Miami Dolphins") on a three-year, $67.5 million deal.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-35)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Malik_Willis&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Willis' uncle is former NFL linebacker [James Anderson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Anderson_(American_football) "James Anderson (American football)").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-36)

Willis was raised as and remains a [Christian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christianity "Christianity"). Most of his social media posts conclude with "TGFE," which is short for "Thank God for Everything."[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malik_Willis#cite_note-37)

**Anthony Dashawn Richardson Sr.** (born May 22, 2002) is an American professional [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_football "American football")[quarterback](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quarterback "Quarterback") for the [Indianapolis Colts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indianapolis_Colts "Indianapolis Colts") of the [National Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League") (NFL). He played [college football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_football "College football") for the [Florida Gators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Gators_football "Florida Gators football") and was selected by the Colts fourth overall in the 2023 NFL draft.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Richardson was born on May 22, 2002, in [Miami, Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami "Miami").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-1) He later attended [Loften High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loften_High_School "Loften High School") in [Gainesville, Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gainesville,_Florida "Gainesville, Florida"). However, Richardson played [quarterback](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quarterback "Quarterback") for [Eastside High School's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastside_High_School_(Gainesville,_Florida) "Eastside High School (Gainesville, Florida)") football team.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-3) During his high school career, Richardson had 4,633 passing yards with 37 passing touchdowns to go along with 1,633 rushing yards and 41 touchdowns.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-4) He committed to play [college football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_football "College football") at the [University of Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Florida "University of Florida").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-5)

## College career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: College career")]

Richardson appeared in just four games during his first year at [Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Gators_football "Florida Gators football") in 2020, completing one of two passes for 27 yards with a touchdown and interception.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-7) He was able to [redshirt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Redshirt_(college_sports) "Redshirt (college sports)") his first year of collegiate eligibility.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-8) Richardson entered 2021 as the backup to [Emory Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emory_Jones "Emory Jones").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-11) Against the [LSU Tigers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_LSU_Tigers_football_team "2021 LSU Tigers football team"), he replaced Jones and completed 10 of 19 passes for 167 yards, three touchdowns, and two interceptions to go along with a rushing touchdown.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-12)

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/16/Anthony_Richardson_2022.jpg/250px-Anthony_Richardson_2022.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Anthony_Richardson_2022.jpg)

Richardson in 2022

Richardson officially became the starting quarterback for the Gators in 2022. In the first game of the season, he helped lead a 29–26 upset over the seventh-ranked [Utah Utes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utah_Utes_football "Utah Utes football") on September 3, 2022.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-13) On September 24, in a 38–33 loss to the [Tennessee Volunteers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Tennessee_Volunteers_football_team "2022 Tennessee Volunteers football team"), Richardson had 453 passing yards, two touchdowns, and an interception to go along with 17 carries for 62 yards and two touchdowns.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-14)

Overall, in 2022, Richardson played in 12 games and passed for 2,549 yards, 17 touchdowns and nine interceptions, as well as rushing for 654 yards and 9 touchdowns in his first full season as a starting quarterback for a college team.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-15) During his time at Florida, Richardson amassed a 6–6 record as the starting quarterback for the Gators.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-16)

As a collegiate player, Richardson was stated to have displayed "dynamic talent" as a passer and runner during his college years but lacked accuracy and consistency.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-17) Richardson's physical gifts also helped propel him as a possible first-round NFL draft selection.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-18) Following the end of the 2022 season, Richardson announced that he would enter the 2023 NFL draft.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-19)

### 2023

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2023")]

See also: [2023 Indianapolis Colts season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Indianapolis_Colts_season "2023 Indianapolis Colts season")

Richardson was drafted in the first round by the [Indianapolis Colts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indianapolis_Colts "Indianapolis Colts") with the fourth overall pick in the 2023 NFL draft.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-22)

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6c/Anthony_Richardson_Colts_2023_season_%28cropped%29.png/250px-Anthony_Richardson_Colts_2023_season_%28cropped%29.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Anthony_Richardson_Colts_2023_season_(cropped).png)

Richardson in 2023

During his first training camp with the Colts, Richardson underwent nasal septum surgery to improve his breathing.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-24) On August 15, 2023, Richardson was named by head coach [Shane Steichen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Steichen "Shane Steichen") as the Colts' starting quarterback over [Gardner Minshew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gardner_Minshew "Gardner Minshew") and [Sam Ehlinger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Ehlinger "Sam Ehlinger").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-25)

Richardson made his NFL debut in the season-opener against the [Jacksonville Jaguars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacksonville_Jaguars "Jacksonville Jaguars"). He threw his first touchdown pass to [Michael Pittman Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Pittman_Jr. "Michael Pittman Jr."), ran for a touchdown, and threw his first career interception to [Tyson Campbell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyson_Campbell "Tyson Campbell") in the 31–21 loss.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-26) During Week 2 against the [Houston Texans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_Texans "Houston Texans"), Richardson ran for two touchdowns before leaving the eventual 31–20 road victory with a concussion in the second quarter as a result of a hit taken as he scored his second touchdown.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-27) On September 22, Richardson was declared out in Week 3 due to a concussion he suffered against the Texans.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-28) He returned the following week against the [Los Angeles Rams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Rams "Los Angeles Rams") and recorded two passing touchdowns and a rushing touchdown, erasing a 23-point deficit in a 29–23 overtime loss.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-29) His rushing touchdown in this game marked the first time in NFL history that a rookie quarterback had scored a rushing touchdown in each of his first three starts.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-30) On October 9, Richardson was placed on injured reserve due to a grade three [AC joint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AC_joint "AC joint") sprain he suffered in Week 5 against the [Tennessee Titans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee_Titans "Tennessee Titans"), which was initially announced for him to miss one-to-two months.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-31) On October 18, the Colts announced that Richardson would miss the rest of the season, and he successfully underwent shoulder surgery to repair the sprain six days later.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-33)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2024")]

See also: [2024 Indianapolis Colts season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Indianapolis_Colts_season "2024 Indianapolis Colts season")

Richardson opened the season as the Colts' starter after recovering from shoulder surgery the previous year. He missed Weeks 5 and 6 with an oblique injury.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-34) In Week 8 against the Texans, Richardson completed 10 of 32 passes for 175 yards, a touchdown, and an interception. He also voluntarily took himself out for one play in the third quarter, stating that he "needed a breather" as the Colts lost 23–20.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-35) Richardson was benched the following week in favor of backup quarterback [Joe Flacco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Flacco "Joe Flacco").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-36) Prior to the benching, Richardson had generated an NFL-worst 44.4% completion percentage in six games.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-37)

After two losses with Flacco, the Colts announced that Richardson would be the starter for the remainder of the season, beginning in their Week 11 matchup against the [New York Jets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Jets "New York Jets").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-38) In his return as starter, Richardson completed 67% of his passes for a career-high 272 yards, a touchdown, and added two rushing scores, including the game-winner in the final minute as the Colts won 28–27.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-39) In Week 13, Richardson orchestrated a 19-play, 80-yard touchdown drive, capped off with a go-ahead two-point conversion with under 15 seconds left as the Colts came back to win 25–24 over the [New England Patriots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_England_Patriots "New England Patriots").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-40) Richardson missed the final two games of the season with a back injury as the Colts missed the playoffs with a loss in Week 17 to the [New York Giants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Giants "New York Giants"). He finished the season completing 47.7 percent of his 264 passing attempts for 1,814 yards, eight touchdowns, and 12 interceptions. He also rushed 86 times for 499 yards with six touchdowns.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-41)

### 2025

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 2025")]

See also: [2025 Indianapolis Colts season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Indianapolis_Colts_season "2025 Indianapolis Colts season")

With the signing of quarterback [Daniel Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Jones_(American_football) "Daniel Jones (American football)") in March 2025, Richardson opened the offseason in a competition with Jones for the starting quarterback job.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-42) On August 19, Jones was named the starter, with Richardson named a backup to begin his third NFL season.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-43) On October 13, Richardson was placed on [injured reserve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Injured_reserve_list#NFL_rules "Injured reserve list") after he fractured the [orbital bone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orbital_bone "Orbital bone") in his eye during pregame warmups the previous day.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-44)

### 2026

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2026")]

See also: [2026 Indianapolis Colts season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Indianapolis_Colts_season "2026 Indianapolis Colts season")

On April 30, 2026, the Colts declined the fifth-year option on Richardson's contract, making him a free agent after the 2026 season.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-45)

**Anthony Dashawn Richardson Sr.** (born May 22, 2002) is an American professional [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_football "American football")[quarterback](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quarterback "Quarterback") for the [Indianapolis Colts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indianapolis_Colts "Indianapolis Colts") of the [National Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League") (NFL). He played [college football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_football "College football") for the [Florida Gators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Gators_football "Florida Gators football") and was selected by the Colts fourth overall in the 2023 NFL draft.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Richardson was born on May 22, 2002, in [Miami, Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami "Miami").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-1) He later attended [Loften High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loften_High_School "Loften High School") in [Gainesville, Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gainesville,_Florida "Gainesville, Florida"). However, Richardson played [quarterback](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quarterback "Quarterback") for [Eastside High School's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastside_High_School_(Gainesville,_Florida) "Eastside High School (Gainesville, Florida)") football team.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-3) During his high school career, Richardson had 4,633 passing yards with 37 passing touchdowns to go along with 1,633 rushing yards and 41 touchdowns.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-4) He committed to play [college football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_football "College football") at the [University of Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Florida "University of Florida").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-5)

## College career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: College career")]

Richardson appeared in just four games during his first year at [Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Gators_football "Florida Gators football") in 2020, completing one of two passes for 27 yards with a touchdown and interception.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-7) He was able to [redshirt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Redshirt_(college_sports) "Redshirt (college sports)") his first year of collegiate eligibility.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-8) Richardson entered 2021 as the backup to [Emory Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emory_Jones "Emory Jones").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-11) Against the [LSU Tigers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_LSU_Tigers_football_team "2021 LSU Tigers football team"), he replaced Jones and completed 10 of 19 passes for 167 yards, three touchdowns, and two interceptions to go along with a rushing touchdown.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-12)

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/16/Anthony_Richardson_2022.jpg/250px-Anthony_Richardson_2022.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Anthony_Richardson_2022.jpg)

Richardson in 2022

Richardson officially became the starting quarterback for the Gators in 2022. In the first game of the season, he helped lead a 29–26 upset over the seventh-ranked [Utah Utes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utah_Utes_football "Utah Utes football") on September 3, 2022.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-13) On September 24, in a 38–33 loss to the [Tennessee Volunteers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Tennessee_Volunteers_football_team "2022 Tennessee Volunteers football team"), Richardson had 453 passing yards, two touchdowns, and an interception to go along with 17 carries for 62 yards and two touchdowns.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-14)

Overall, in 2022, Richardson played in 12 games and passed for 2,549 yards, 17 touchdowns and nine interceptions, as well as rushing for 654 yards and 9 touchdowns in his first full season as a starting quarterback for a college team.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-15) During his time at Florida, Richardson amassed a 6–6 record as the starting quarterback for the Gators.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-16)

As a collegiate player, Richardson was stated to have displayed "dynamic talent" as a passer and runner during his college years but lacked accuracy and consistency.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-17) Richardson's physical gifts also helped propel him as a possible first-round NFL draft selection.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-18) Following the end of the 2022 season, Richardson announced that he would enter the 2023 NFL draft.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-19)

### 2023

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2023")]

See also: [2023 Indianapolis Colts season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Indianapolis_Colts_season "2023 Indianapolis Colts season")

Richardson was drafted in the first round by the [Indianapolis Colts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indianapolis_Colts "Indianapolis Colts") with the fourth overall pick in the 2023 NFL draft.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-22)

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6c/Anthony_Richardson_Colts_2023_season_%28cropped%29.png/250px-Anthony_Richardson_Colts_2023_season_%28cropped%29.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Anthony_Richardson_Colts_2023_season_(cropped).png)

Richardson in 2023

During his first training camp with the Colts, Richardson underwent nasal septum surgery to improve his breathing.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-24) On August 15, 2023, Richardson was named by head coach [Shane Steichen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Steichen "Shane Steichen") as the Colts' starting quarterback over [Gardner Minshew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gardner_Minshew "Gardner Minshew") and [Sam Ehlinger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Ehlinger "Sam Ehlinger").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-25)

Richardson made his NFL debut in the season-opener against the [Jacksonville Jaguars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacksonville_Jaguars "Jacksonville Jaguars"). He threw his first touchdown pass to [Michael Pittman Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Pittman_Jr. "Michael Pittman Jr."), ran for a touchdown, and threw his first career interception to [Tyson Campbell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyson_Campbell "Tyson Campbell") in the 31–21 loss.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-26) During Week 2 against the [Houston Texans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_Texans "Houston Texans"), Richardson ran for two touchdowns before leaving the eventual 31–20 road victory with a concussion in the second quarter as a result of a hit taken as he scored his second touchdown.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-27) On September 22, Richardson was declared out in Week 3 due to a concussion he suffered against the Texans.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-28) He returned the following week against the [Los Angeles Rams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Rams "Los Angeles Rams") and recorded two passing touchdowns and a rushing touchdown, erasing a 23-point deficit in a 29–23 overtime loss.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-29) His rushing touchdown in this game marked the first time in NFL history that a rookie quarterback had scored a rushing touchdown in each of his first three starts.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-30) On October 9, Richardson was placed on injured reserve due to a grade three [AC joint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AC_joint "AC joint") sprain he suffered in Week 5 against the [Tennessee Titans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee_Titans "Tennessee Titans"), which was initially announced for him to miss one-to-two months.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-31) On October 18, the Colts announced that Richardson would miss the rest of the season, and he successfully underwent shoulder surgery to repair the sprain six days later.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-33)

### 2024

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2024")]

See also: [2024 Indianapolis Colts season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Indianapolis_Colts_season "2024 Indianapolis Colts season")

Richardson opened the season as the Colts' starter after recovering from shoulder surgery the previous year. He missed Weeks 5 and 6 with an oblique injury.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-34) In Week 8 against the Texans, Richardson completed 10 of 32 passes for 175 yards, a touchdown, and an interception. He also voluntarily took himself out for one play in the third quarter, stating that he "needed a breather" as the Colts lost 23–20.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-35) Richardson was benched the following week in favor of backup quarterback [Joe Flacco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Flacco "Joe Flacco").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-36) Prior to the benching, Richardson had generated an NFL-worst 44.4% completion percentage in six games.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-37)

After two losses with Flacco, the Colts announced that Richardson would be the starter for the remainder of the season, beginning in their Week 11 matchup against the [New York Jets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Jets "New York Jets").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-38) In his return as starter, Richardson completed 67% of his passes for a career-high 272 yards, a touchdown, and added two rushing scores, including the game-winner in the final minute as the Colts won 28–27.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-39) In Week 13, Richardson orchestrated a 19-play, 80-yard touchdown drive, capped off with a go-ahead two-point conversion with under 15 seconds left as the Colts came back to win 25–24 over the [New England Patriots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_England_Patriots "New England Patriots").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-40) Richardson missed the final two games of the season with a back injury as the Colts missed the playoffs with a loss in Week 17 to the [New York Giants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Giants "New York Giants"). He finished the season completing 47.7 percent of his 264 passing attempts for 1,814 yards, eight touchdowns, and 12 interceptions. He also rushed 86 times for 499 yards with six touchdowns.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-41)

### 2025

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 2025")]

See also: [2025 Indianapolis Colts season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Indianapolis_Colts_season "2025 Indianapolis Colts season")

With the signing of quarterback [Daniel Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Jones_(American_football) "Daniel Jones (American football)") in March 2025, Richardson opened the offseason in a competition with Jones for the starting quarterback job.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-42) On August 19, Jones was named the starter, with Richardson named a backup to begin his third NFL season.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-43) On October 13, Richardson was placed on [injured reserve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Injured_reserve_list#NFL_rules "Injured reserve list") after he fractured the [orbital bone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orbital_bone "Orbital bone") in his eye during pregame warmups the previous day.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-44)

### 2026

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2026")]

See also: [2026 Indianapolis Colts season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Indianapolis_Colts_season "2026 Indianapolis Colts season")

On April 30, 2026, the Colts declined the fifth-year option on Richardson's contract, making him a free agent after the 2026 season.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Richardson_(American_football)#cite_note-45)

The 2022 NFL draft was the National Football League's 87th annual draft and was held from April 28–30, 2022, at the Caesars Forum on the Las Vegas Strip in Paradise next to Las Vegas. The first round was held on Thursday, April 28, and was followed by the second and third rounds on Friday, April 29. The draft concluded with rounds 4–7 on Saturday, April 30. It was the first draft to be held in the Las Vegas metropolitan area and the state of Nevada.

The first five selections were defensive players, the second-most taken at the start of a draft after the six in 1991. Along with the 1972 and 2000 drafts, it marked the third time defensive players were the first two picks after the first three picks in the previous year's draft were quarterbacks. Five Georgia defensive players were taken during the first round, the most from an individual school in a draft. In addition to the high number of defensive selections, nine offensive linemen were taken in the first round, the most since 2013. Conversely, only one quarterback was selected in the first round at 20th overall, the lowest for a draft's first quarterback since 1997, and no running backs were taken in the first round for the first time since 2014.

A record nine draft-day trades with first-round picks were made, which resulted in less than half of the first-round selections being made by the teams that initially owned them. Analysts attributed the high number of trades to eight teams entering the draft without a first-round selection and a general absence of highly touted prospects.[1]

Host cityedit

Las Vegas was originally scheduled to host the 2020 NFL draft, coinciding with the Oakland Raiders' relocation to the city. Due to the COVID-19 pandemic the draft was held as a virtual event. Las Vegas was given the 2022 Draft as a result.[2]

Draft activities were held around two main locations on the Las Vegas Strip; invited players walked a floating red carpet on the man-made lake in front of the Bellagio and its fountains. The plans were similar to those originally intended for the 2020 draft, although a plan for players to be transported onto the stage by boat was scrapped in favor of using walkways.[3][4]

Caesars Forum housed infrastructure for the event.[3][4] The Linq Promenade hosted the NFL Draft Experience, which featured fan activities.[3][4] Parts of Flamingo Road and Las Vegas Boulevard were closed to vehicle traffic to allow spectators to travel between the two sites.[5]

Round 1

 No. 7: Chicago → NY Giants (PD). Chicago traded first- and fourth-round selections (7th and 112th overall), and 2021 first- and fourth-round selections to the NY Giants in exchange for a 2021 first-round selection.[trade 1]

Resolution JC-2A selectionsedit

Resolution JC-2A, enacted by the NFL in November 2020, rewards teams for developing minority candidates for head coach and/or general manager positions.[16] The resolution rewards teams whose minority candidates are hired away for one of those positions by awarding draft selections, which are at the end of the third round, after standard compensatory selections; if multiple teams qualify, they are awarded by draft order in the first round. These picks are in addition to, and have no impact on, the standard 32 compensatory selections.[17] Seven picks were awarded for the 2022 draft pursuant to the resolution.

 Cleveland received a third-round selection (99th overall) and a 2023 third-round selection as compensation for Minnesota hiring vice president of football operations Kwesi Adofo-Mensah as general manager.[6]
 Baltimore received a third-round selection (100th overall) and a 2021 third-round selection as compensation for Houston hiring assistant head coach and passing game coordinator David Culley as head coach.[7]
 New Orleans received a third-round selection (101st overall) and a 2021 third-round selection as compensation for Atlanta hiring pro scouting director Terry Fontenot as general manager.[8]
 San Francisco received a third-round selection (102nd overall), a 2021 third-round selection and a 2023 third-round selection as compensation for the NY Jets hiring defensive coordinator Robert Saleh as head coach and Washington hiring vice president of player personnel Martin Mayhew as general manager.[9][10][11]
 Kansas City received a third-round selection (103rd overall) and a 2023 third-round selection as compensation for Chicago hiring executive director of player personnel Ryan Poles as general manager.[12]
 The LA Rams received a third-round selection (104th overall) and a 2021 third-round selection as compensation for Detroit hiring college scouting director Brad Holmes as general manager.[13]
 San Francisco received a third-round selection (105th overall) and another 2023 third-round selection when Miami hired offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel as head coach.[14]
Notesedit
 Players are identified as Pro Bowlers if they were selected for the Pro Bowl at any time in their career.

Forfeited selections

 New Orleans forfeited a sixth-round selection as a penalty for repeated violations of the league's COVID-19 guidelines.[15]

The 2022 NFL draft was the National Football League's 87th annual draft and was held from April 28–30, 2022, at the Caesars Forum on the Las Vegas Strip in Paradise next to Las Vegas. The first round was held on Thursday, April 28, and was followed by the second and third rounds on Friday, April 29. The draft concluded with rounds 4–7 on Saturday, April 30. It was the first draft to be held in the Las Vegas metropolitan area and the state of Nevada.

The first five selections were defensive players, the second-most taken at the start of a draft after the six in 1991. Along with the 1972 and 2000 drafts, it marked the third time defensive players were the first two picks after the first three picks in the previous year's draft were quarterbacks. Five Georgia defensive players were taken during the first round, the most from an individual school in a draft. In addition to the high number of defensive selections, nine offensive linemen were taken in the first round, the most since 2013. Conversely, only one quarterback was selected in the first round at 20th overall, the lowest for a draft's first quarterback since 1997, and no running backs were taken in the first round for the first time since 2014.

A record nine draft-day trades with first-round picks were made, which resulted in less than half of the first-round selections being made by the teams that initially owned them. Analysts attributed the high number of trades to eight teams entering the draft without a first-round selection and a general absence of highly touted prospects.[1]

Host cityedit

Las Vegas was originally scheduled to host the 2020 NFL draft, coinciding with the Oakland Raiders' relocation to the city. Due to the COVID-19 pandemic the draft was held as a virtual event. Las Vegas was given the 2022 Draft as a result.[2]

Draft activities were held around two main locations on the Las Vegas Strip; invited players walked a floating red carpet on the man-made lake in front of the Bellagio and its fountains. The plans were similar to those originally intended for the 2020 draft, although a plan for players to be transported onto the stage by boat was scrapped in favor of using walkways.[3][4]

Caesars Forum housed infrastructure for the event.[3][4] The Linq Promenade hosted the NFL Draft Experience, which featured fan activities.[3][4] Parts of Flamingo Road and Las Vegas Boulevard were closed to vehicle traffic to allow spectators to travel between the two sites.[5]

Resolution JC-2A selectionsedit

Resolution JC-2A, enacted by the NFL in November 2020, rewards teams for developing minority candidates for head coach and/or general manager positions.[16] The resolution rewards teams whose minority candidates are hired away for one of those positions by awarding draft selections, which are at the end of the third round, after standard compensatory selections; if multiple teams qualify, they are awarded by draft order in the first round. These picks are in addition to, and have no impact on, the standard 32 compensatory selections.[17] Seven picks were awarded for the 2022 draft pursuant to the resolution.

 Cleveland received a third-round selection (99th overall) and a 2023 third-round selection as compensation for Minnesota hiring vice president of football operations Kwesi Adofo-Mensah as general manager.[6]
 Baltimore received a third-round selection (100th overall) and a 2021 third-round selection as compensation for Houston hiring assistant head coach and passing game coordinator David Culley as head coach.[7]
 New Orleans received a third-round selection (101st overall) and a 2021 third-round selection as compensation for Atlanta hiring pro scouting director Terry Fontenot as general manager.[8]
 San Francisco received a third-round selection (102nd overall), a 2021 third-round selection and a 2023 third-round selection as compensation for the NY Jets hiring defensive coordinator Robert Saleh as head coach and Washington hiring vice president of player personnel Martin Mayhew as general manager.[9][10][11]
 Kansas City received a third-round selection (103rd overall) and a 2023 third-round selection as compensation for Chicago hiring executive director of player personnel Ryan Poles as general manager.[12]
 The LA Rams received a third-round selection (104th overall) and a 2021 third-round selection as compensation for Detroit hiring college scouting director Brad Holmes as general manager.[13]
 San Francisco received a third-round selection (105th overall) and another 2023 third-round selection when Miami hired offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel as head coach.[14]
Notesedit
 Players are identified as Pro Bowlers if they were selected for the Pro Bowl at any time in their career.

Forfeited selections

 New Orleans forfeited a sixth-round selection as a penalty for repeated violations of the league's COVID-19 guidelines.[15]

**Kenneth Pickett** (born June 6, 1998) is an American professional [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_football "American football")[quarterback](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quarterback "Quarterback") for the [Carolina Panthers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carolina_Panthers "Carolina Panthers") of the [National Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League") (NFL). He played [college football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_football "College football") for the [Pittsburgh Panthers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_Panthers_football "Pittsburgh Panthers football"), winning the [Johnny Unitas Golden Arm Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Unitas_Golden_Arm_Award "Johnny Unitas Golden Arm Award"), [ACC Player of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Coast_Conference_football_individual_awards "Atlantic Coast Conference football individual awards"), and [ACC Athlete of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACC_Athlete_of_the_Year "ACC Athlete of the Year") between 2021 and 2022. Pickett was selected by the [Pittsburgh Steelers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_Steelers "Pittsburgh Steelers") in the first round of the 2022 NFL draft, spending two seasons as the primary starter and helping the team clinch a playoff appearance in 2023. Due to inconsistent play, he was traded to the [Philadelphia Eagles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_Eagles "Philadelphia Eagles"), where he spent one season as a backup and was a member of the team that won [Super Bowl LIX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LIX "Super Bowl LIX"). He joined the [Las Vegas Raiders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas_Raiders "Las Vegas Raiders") as a backup the following year before signing with the Panthers in 2026.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenny_Pickett&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Pickett was born in the [Oakhurst](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oakhurst,_New_Jersey "Oakhurst, New Jersey") section of [Ocean Township, New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ocean_Township,_Monmouth_County,_New_Jersey "Ocean Township, Monmouth County, New Jersey").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-auto-1) He attended [Ocean Township High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ocean_Township_High_School "Ocean Township High School")[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-2) and graduated in 2017. Pickett led the Ocean Township Spartans to the New Jersey Central Group III semifinal game as a junior, leading his team to a 9–2 record.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-auto-1) 247Sports ranked Pickett as the No. 23 overall high school football player in New Jersey in his senior year.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-3) During his high school career, Pickett passed for 4,670 yards with 43 [touchdowns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Touchdowns "Touchdowns") and rushed for 873 yards and 17 touchdowns. He originally committed to play [college football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_football "College football") at [Temple University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temple_University "Temple University"), but changed his commitment to the [University of Pittsburgh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Pittsburgh "University of Pittsburgh").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-4)

## College career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenny_Pickett&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: College career")]

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/80/Kenny_Pickett_vs._Clemson_%28cropped_1%29.jpg/250px-Kenny_Pickett_vs._Clemson_%28cropped_1%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kenny_Pickett_vs._Clemson_(cropped_1).jpg)

Pickett in 2020

Pickett spent most of his true freshman season at Pittsburgh in 2017 as a backup to [Max Browne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Browne "Max Browne") and [Ben DiNucci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_DiNucci "Ben DiNucci"). He started his first career game in Pittsburgh's final game of the season against the second ranked [Miami Hurricanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Miami_Hurricanes_football_team "2017 Miami Hurricanes football team"). During the team's upset victory, Pickett completed 18-of-29 passes for 193 yards with a touchdown and also rushed for 60 yards and two touchdowns.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-5) He finished the season completing 39-of-66 passes for 509 yards, a touchdown, and an interception.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-7)

Pickett returned as Pittsburgh's starter in 2018.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-9) He started all 14 games, completing 180-of-310 passes for 1,969 yards, 12 touchdowns, and six interceptions.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-10) Pickett led Pittsburgh to their first ever [Atlantic Coast Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Coast_Conference "Atlantic Coast Conference") Coastal Division Championship in his first season as the full-time starter.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-auto-1) The Associated Press ranked the Panthers as high as the No. 24 team in the country at one point in the 2018 season.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-:1-11) The Panthers lost 14–13 to the [Stanford Cardinal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Stanford_Cardinal_football_team "2018 Stanford Cardinal football team") in the [Sun Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Sun_Bowl "2018 Sun Bowl").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-12)

Pickett remained the starter in 2019, making 12 starts and missing one game due to injury. He completed 289-of-469 passes for 3,098 yards, 13 touchdowns, and nine interceptions.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-13) This was Pickett's first season with [Mark Whipple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Whipple "Mark Whipple") acting as the offensive coordinator, who increased the amount of passes the offense threw each week. Pickett led the Panthers to a 7–5 record heading into the postseason.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-14) The Panthers were selected to the [2019 Quick Lane Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Quick_Lane_Bowl "2019 Quick Lane Bowl") in [Detroit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detroit "Detroit") and defeated the [Eastern Michigan Eagles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Eastern_Michigan_Eagles_football_team "2019 Eastern Michigan Eagles football team") 34–30. Pickett threw for 361 yards and three touchdowns, including a game winning touchdown to wide receiver Taysir Mack in the final minutes of the game.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-15)

Pickett and the Panthers played in a shortened season due to the COVID-19 pandemic, finishing with a 6–5 record. Pickett played in nine games and threw for 2,408 yards, 13 touchdowns, and nine interceptions in that stretch.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-SR-16) The Associated Press ranked the Panthers as high as the No. 21 team in the country at one point in the 2020 season.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-:1-11) Despite being eligible for a bowl game, the Panthers collectively opted out of participating in the postseason.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-17)

The NCAA granted all 2020 fall athletes an extra year of eligibility, and Pickett used this option to return as the Panthers' starting quarterback in 2021.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-18)

Pickett took advantage of his final year of eligibility and broke out as one of the nation's top players. Pickett recorded 4,319 yards and 42 touchdowns setting school records for single season yards and touchdowns as well as career yards and touchdowns.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-19) He was named a first-team [All-American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_College_Football_All-America_Team "2021 College Football All-America Team") and was a finalist for the [Heisman Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heisman_Trophy "Heisman Trophy"), finishing in third place.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-SR-16) Pittsburgh won the [ACC Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_ACC_Championship_Game "2021 ACC Championship Game") and finished 11–2 in games Pickett started, the school's best record since 1976.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-:1-11) He graduated with a bachelor's degree in marketing and enrolled at [Joseph M. Katz Graduate School of Business](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_M._Katz_Graduate_School_of_Business "Joseph M. Katz Graduate School of Business").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-auto-1) Pickett was also named the men's [ACC Athlete of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACC_Athlete_of_the_Year "ACC Athlete of the Year") across all sports, sharing honors with women's recipient Charlotte North of [Boston College lacrosse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_College_Eagles_women's_lacrosse "Boston College Eagles women's lacrosse").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-20)

### Pittsburgh Steelers

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenny_Pickett&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Pittsburgh Steelers")]

#### 2022

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenny_Pickett&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 2022")]

Pickett was selected by the [Pittsburgh Steelers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_Steelers "Pittsburgh Steelers") in the first round (20th overall) of the 2022 NFL draft, the highest the Steelers selected a quarterback since drafting [Ben Roethlisberger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Roethlisberger "Ben Roethlisberger") in 2004;[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-36) the selection was announced by Steelers' legend [Franco Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franco_Harris "Franco Harris") in one of his last public appearances with the team before his unexpected death on December 20, 2022.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-37) With the starting quarterback position wide open following Roethlisberger's retirement, Pickett was named the backup quarterback for the Steelers behind starter [Mitchell Trubisky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitchell_Trubisky "Mitchell Trubisky").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-38) Initially, Pickett was designated as the team’s third-string quarterback behind both Trubisky and veteran [Mason Rudolph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mason_Rudolph_(American_football) "Mason Rudolph (American football)"), but head coach [Mike Tomlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Tomlin "Mike Tomlin") would adjust the depth chart to put Pickett in the backup role citing a "clerical error" with the original depth chart.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-39)

Pickett made his NFL debut in the second half of a Week 4 loss against the [New York Jets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Jets "New York Jets") after Trubisky was benched.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-40) Pickett completed 10-of-13 passes for 120 yards and rushed for two touchdowns, but threw three interceptions in the 24–20 loss. On his first career pass attempt, Pickett threw a deep ball to wide receiver [Chase Claypool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chase_Claypool "Chase Claypool") that was intercepted by safety [Jordan Whitehead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan_Whitehead "Jordan Whitehead"). On his second drive, Pickett scored his first NFL touchdown on a one-yard rush.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-41)

On October 4, Pickett was named the starter by head coach Tomlin.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-42) In his first career start against the [Buffalo Bills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buffalo_Bills "Buffalo Bills"), Pickett completed 34-of-51 passes for 327 yards and an interception during the 38–3 road loss.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-43) The following week against the [Tampa Bay Buccaneers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tampa_Bay_Buccaneers "Tampa Bay Buccaneers"), Pickett threw his first touchdown pass to running back [Najee Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Najee_Harris "Najee Harris"), but he exited the narrow 20–18 victory during the third quarter with a [concussion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concussion "Concussion").[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-44)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-StunBrady-45)

During Week 14, in a narrow 16–14 loss to the [Baltimore Ravens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltimore_Ravens "Baltimore Ravens"), Pickett once again suffered a concussion.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-46) He was ruled out for Week 15 against the [Carolina Panthers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carolina_Panthers "Carolina Panthers"), but started in Week 16 against the [Las Vegas Raiders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas_Raiders "Las Vegas Raiders").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-47)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-48) Pickett threw a game-winning 14-yard touchdown to wide receiver [George Pickens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Pickens "George Pickens") with under a minute left and finished the 13–10 victory with 244 passing yards, the aforementioned touchdown, and an interception.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-49)

During Week 17 against the Ravens, Pickett threw the game-winning touchdown with under a minute left for the second consecutive game; a 10-yard pass to Harris. Pickett finished the 16–13 road victory with 168 passing yards and the touchdown, keeping the Steelers' playoff hopes alive.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-50) Pickett became the first rookie quarterback in NFL history to throw a game-winning touchdown in the final minute of the fourth quarter in two consecutive games.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-51)

Pickett finished his rookie season with 2,404 passing yards, seven touchdowns, and nine interceptions, to go along with 55 carries for 237 yards and three touchdowns in 13 games with 12 starts.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-52) On March 13, 2023, the game ball from the Steelers' victory over the [Las Vegas Raiders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Las_Vegas_Raiders_season "2023 Las Vegas Raiders season") was put on display in the [Professional Football Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_Football_Hall_of_Fame "Professional Football Hall of Fame").

#### 2023

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenny_Pickett&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2023")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d2/KennyPickett2023.jpg/250px-KennyPickett2023.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:KennyPickett2023.jpg)

Pickett in 2023

During Week 3 against the Raiders, Pickett threw for 235 yards and two touchdowns in the 23–18 road victory, marking his first professional game with multiple touchdown passes.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-53) In the next game against the [Houston Texans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Houston_Texans_season "2023 Houston Texans season"), Pickett completed 15-of-23 passes for 114 yards and an interception before leaving the eventual 30–6 road loss in the third quarter with a bone bruise.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-54) Three weeks later against the [Los Angeles Rams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Los_Angeles_Rams_season "2023 Los Angeles Rams season"), Pickett had 230 passing yards and scored his first rushing touchdown of the season on a quarterback sneak in the 24–17 road victory.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-55)

During a Week 8 loss of 20–10 to the [Jacksonville Jaguars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Jacksonville_Jaguars_season "2023 Jacksonville Jaguars season"), Pickett had 73 passing yards and suffered a rib injury late in the second quarter and did not return.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-56) However, he started in the next game against the [Tennessee Titans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Tennessee_Titans_season "2023 Tennessee Titans season") and threw for 160 yards and the game-winning touchdown during the 20–16 victory.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-57)

In Week 13 against the [Arizona Cardinals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona_Cardinals "Arizona Cardinals"), Pickett had 70 passing yards before leaving the 24–10 loss with a high ankle sprain.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-58) He underwent surgery to accelerate the healing process on his ankle.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-59)

In the regular-season finale against the Ravens, Pickett was listed as active for the first time since his injury, but was demoted to backup duties following the success of Mason Rudolph.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-60) Rudolph started in the Steelers' 31–17 Wild Card loss to the Buffalo Bills.

Pickett finished his second professional season with 2,070 passing yards and the lowest touchdown percentage of all eligible starting quarterbacks in the league, only throwing for six touchdowns (as well as four interceptions) out of 324 pass attempts across 12 games and as many starts.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-o797-61)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-62) Pickett's passer rating improved from 76.7 to 81.4.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-63)

### Philadelphia Eagles

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenny_Pickett&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Philadelphia Eagles")]

Following the Steelers' signing of [Russell Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russell_Wilson "Russell Wilson") in the 2024 offseason, Pickett requested a trade.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-64) On March 16, 2024, he was traded to the [Philadelphia Eagles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_Eagles "Philadelphia Eagles") along with a 2024 fourth-round pick (No. 120; [Jaylen Wright](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaylen_Wright "Jaylen Wright")) in exchange for a 2024 third-round pick (No. 98; [Payton Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Payton_Wilson "Payton Wilson")) and two 2025 seventh-round picks (No. 223 went to the [Seattle Seahawks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seattle_Seahawks "Seattle Seahawks") where they selected [Damien Martinez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Damien_Martinez "Damien Martinez")) (No. 229; [Donte Kent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donte_Kent "Donte Kent")).[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-65)

Pickett entered the season as the backup quarterback behind incumbent starter [Jalen Hurts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jalen_Hurts "Jalen Hurts"), despite a competition with [Tanner McKee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanner_McKee "Tanner McKee").[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-f354-66) Pickett made his Eagles debut during a Week 7 28–3 road victory over the [New York Giants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_New_York_Giants_season "2024 New York Giants season"). He attempted one pass, but it fell incomplete.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-67) Three weeks later, in a 34–6 road victory over the [Dallas Cowboys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Dallas_Cowboys_season "2024 Dallas Cowboys season"), Pickett would relieve Hurts, completing 1-of-2 passes for five yards.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-68)

During Week 16 against the [Washington Commanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Commanders "Washington Commanders"), Pickett replaced Hurts after he was ruled out with a [concussion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concussion "Concussion").[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-69) Pickett finished the 36–33 road loss with 143 passing yards, a touchdown and an interception. Despite suffering a rib injury, he did not miss any plays.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-70)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-71) Pickett was named the Eagles' starter for the Week 17 matchup against the Cowboys.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-r954-72) He completed 10-of-15 passes for 143 yards and a touchdown, while also rushing for a touchdown before leaving the eventual 41–7 victory in the third quarter with a rib injury.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-73)[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-g533-74)

At the end of the NFC Championship game against the [Washington Commanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Commanders "Washington Commanders"), Pickett was substituted in for Hurts to kneel out the 55–23 victory.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-r834-75) Pickett won his first Super Bowl when the Eagles defeated the [Kansas City Chiefs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Kansas_City_Chiefs_season "2024 Kansas City Chiefs season") in [Super Bowl LIX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LIX "Super Bowl LIX"). Pickett finished the game at quarterback for the Eagles, handing the ball off, attempting one pass, and then kneeling to close out the 40–22 victory.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-h456-76)

### Cleveland Browns

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenny_Pickett&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Cleveland Browns")]

On March 12, 2025, the Eagles traded Pickett to the [Cleveland Browns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland_Browns "Cleveland Browns") in exchange for [Dorian Thompson-Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorian_Thompson-Robinson "Dorian Thompson-Robinson") and a fifth-round pick in the [2025 NFL draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_NFL_draft "2025 NFL draft").[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-77) Pickett entered training camp in a four-way competition with [Joe Flacco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Flacco "Joe Flacco"), [Dillon Gabriel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dillon_Gabriel "Dillon Gabriel"), and [Shedeur Sanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shedeur_Sanders "Shedeur Sanders") for Cleveland's starting quarterback role.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-78) A hamstring injury limited his participation in camp, and Pickett was named Flacco's backup before the start of the [2025 NFL season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_NFL_season "2025 NFL season").[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-79)

### Las Vegas Raiders

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenny_Pickett&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Las Vegas Raiders")]

On August 25, 2025, Pickett was traded to the [Las Vegas Raiders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas_Raiders "Las Vegas Raiders") in exchange for a fifth-round pick (141st overall) in the [2026 NFL draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_NFL_draft "2026 NFL draft").[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-80) He spent the 2025 season as the backup to [Geno Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geno_Smith "Geno Smith"). After Smith hurt his shoulder in a Week 14 loss to the [Denver Broncos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Denver_Broncos_season "2025 Denver Broncos season"), Pickett entered the game and made all but three of his 11 passes for 96 yards and a touchdown.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-81) Pickett was named the starter for the following week against the [Philadelphia Eagles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Philadelphia_Eagles_season "2025 Philadelphia Eagles season"),[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-82) where he completed 15-of-25 passes for 64 yards, was intercepted once, and sacked four times as the Raiders lost 31–0.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-83) Smith returned to the starting position for Week 16.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-84)

### Carolina Panthers

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenny_Pickett&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Carolina Panthers")]

On March 11, 2026, Pickett signed a one-year, $4 million contract with the [Carolina Panthers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carolina_Panthers "Carolina Panthers").[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-85)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenny_Pickett&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Pickett married Amy Paternoster, a former women's soccer player at [Princeton University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Princeton_University "Princeton University"), on June 24, 2023.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-86) His sister, Alex,[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-m535-87) played collegiate soccer at [East Stroudsburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Stroudsburg_University_of_Pennsylvania "East Stroudsburg University of Pennsylvania"),[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-z681-88) and became the coach of [Seton Hill University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seton_Hill_University "Seton Hill University")'s women's soccer team in 2019.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-x985-89)

From 2022 to 2024, Pickett resided in [Cranberry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cranberry_Township,_Butler_County,_Pennsylvania "Cranberry Township, Butler County, Pennsylvania"), a suburb of [Pittsburgh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh "Pittsburgh"). He sold his home in Cranberry following his trade to the [Philadelphia Eagles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_Eagles "Philadelphia Eagles") in early 2024.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-a683-90)
