**Kenneth Pickett** (born June 6, 1998) is an American professional [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_football "American football")[quarterback](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quarterback "Quarterback") for the [Carolina Panthers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carolina_Panthers "Carolina Panthers") of the [National Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League") (NFL). He played [college football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_football "College football") for the [Pittsburgh Panthers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_Panthers_football "Pittsburgh Panthers football"), winning the [Johnny Unitas Golden Arm Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Unitas_Golden_Arm_Award "Johnny Unitas Golden Arm Award"), [ACC Player of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Coast_Conference_football_individual_awards "Atlantic Coast Conference football individual awards"), and [ACC Athlete of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACC_Athlete_of_the_Year "ACC Athlete of the Year") between 2021 and 2022. Pickett was selected by the [Pittsburgh Steelers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_Steelers "Pittsburgh Steelers") in the first round of the 2022 NFL draft, spending two seasons as the primary starter and helping the team clinch a playoff appearance in 2023. Due to inconsistent play, he was traded to the [Philadelphia Eagles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_Eagles "Philadelphia Eagles"), where he spent one season as a backup and was a member of the team that won [Super Bowl LIX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LIX "Super Bowl LIX"). He joined the [Las Vegas Raiders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas_Raiders "Las Vegas Raiders") as a backup the following year before signing with the Panthers in 2026.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenny_Pickett&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Pickett was born in the [Oakhurst](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oakhurst,_New_Jersey "Oakhurst, New Jersey") section of [Ocean Township, New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ocean_Township,_Monmouth_County,_New_Jersey "Ocean Township, Monmouth County, New Jersey").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-auto-1) He attended [Ocean Township High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ocean_Township_High_School "Ocean Township High School")[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-2) and graduated in 2017. Pickett led the Ocean Township Spartans to the New Jersey Central Group III semifinal game as a junior, leading his team to a 9–2 record.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-auto-1) 247Sports ranked Pickett as the No. 23 overall high school football player in New Jersey in his senior year.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-3) During his high school career, Pickett passed for 4,670 yards with 43 [touchdowns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Touchdowns "Touchdowns") and rushed for 873 yards and 17 touchdowns. He originally committed to play [college football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_football "College football") at [Temple University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temple_University "Temple University"), but changed his commitment to the [University of Pittsburgh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Pittsburgh "University of Pittsburgh").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-4)

## College career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenny_Pickett&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: College career")]

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/80/Kenny_Pickett_vs._Clemson_%28cropped_1%29.jpg/250px-Kenny_Pickett_vs._Clemson_%28cropped_1%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kenny_Pickett_vs._Clemson_(cropped_1).jpg)

Pickett in 2020

Pickett spent most of his true freshman season at Pittsburgh in 2017 as a backup to [Max Browne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Browne "Max Browne") and [Ben DiNucci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_DiNucci "Ben DiNucci"). He started his first career game in Pittsburgh's final game of the season against the second ranked [Miami Hurricanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Miami_Hurricanes_football_team "2017 Miami Hurricanes football team"). During the team's upset victory, Pickett completed 18-of-29 passes for 193 yards with a touchdown and also rushed for 60 yards and two touchdowns.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-5) He finished the season completing 39-of-66 passes for 509 yards, a touchdown, and an interception.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-7)

Pickett returned as Pittsburgh's starter in 2018.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-9) He started all 14 games, completing 180-of-310 passes for 1,969 yards, 12 touchdowns, and six interceptions.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-10) Pickett led Pittsburgh to their first ever [Atlantic Coast Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Coast_Conference "Atlantic Coast Conference") Coastal Division Championship in his first season as the full-time starter.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-auto-1) The Associated Press ranked the Panthers as high as the No. 24 team in the country at one point in the 2018 season.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-:1-11) The Panthers lost 14–13 to the [Stanford Cardinal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Stanford_Cardinal_football_team "2018 Stanford Cardinal football team") in the [Sun Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Sun_Bowl "2018 Sun Bowl").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-12)

Pickett remained the starter in 2019, making 12 starts and missing one game due to injury. He completed 289-of-469 passes for 3,098 yards, 13 touchdowns, and nine interceptions.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-13) This was Pickett's first season with [Mark Whipple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Whipple "Mark Whipple") acting as the offensive coordinator, who increased the amount of passes the offense threw each week. Pickett led the Panthers to a 7–5 record heading into the postseason.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-14) The Panthers were selected to the [2019 Quick Lane Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Quick_Lane_Bowl "2019 Quick Lane Bowl") in [Detroit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detroit "Detroit") and defeated the [Eastern Michigan Eagles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Eastern_Michigan_Eagles_football_team "2019 Eastern Michigan Eagles football team") 34–30. Pickett threw for 361 yards and three touchdowns, including a game winning touchdown to wide receiver Taysir Mack in the final minutes of the game.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-15)

Pickett and the Panthers played in a shortened season due to the COVID-19 pandemic, finishing with a 6–5 record. Pickett played in nine games and threw for 2,408 yards, 13 touchdowns, and nine interceptions in that stretch.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-SR-16) The Associated Press ranked the Panthers as high as the No. 21 team in the country at one point in the 2020 season.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-:1-11) Despite being eligible for a bowl game, the Panthers collectively opted out of participating in the postseason.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-17)

The NCAA granted all 2020 fall athletes an extra year of eligibility, and Pickett used this option to return as the Panthers' starting quarterback in 2021.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-18)

Pickett took advantage of his final year of eligibility and broke out as one of the nation's top players. Pickett recorded 4,319 yards and 42 touchdowns setting school records for single season yards and touchdowns as well as career yards and touchdowns.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-19) He was named a first-team [All-American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_College_Football_All-America_Team "2021 College Football All-America Team") and was a finalist for the [Heisman Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heisman_Trophy "Heisman Trophy"), finishing in third place.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-SR-16) Pittsburgh won the [ACC Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_ACC_Championship_Game "2021 ACC Championship Game") and finished 11–2 in games Pickett started, the school's best record since 1976.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-:1-11) He graduated with a bachelor's degree in marketing and enrolled at [Joseph M. Katz Graduate School of Business](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_M._Katz_Graduate_School_of_Business "Joseph M. Katz Graduate School of Business").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-auto-1) Pickett was also named the men's [ACC Athlete of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACC_Athlete_of_the_Year "ACC Athlete of the Year") across all sports, sharing honors with women's recipient Charlotte North of [Boston College lacrosse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_College_Eagles_women's_lacrosse "Boston College Eagles women's lacrosse").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-20)

### Pittsburgh Steelers

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenny_Pickett&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Pittsburgh Steelers")]

#### 2022

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenny_Pickett&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 2022")]

Pickett was selected by the [Pittsburgh Steelers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_Steelers "Pittsburgh Steelers") in the first round (20th overall) of the 2022 NFL draft, the highest the Steelers selected a quarterback since drafting [Ben Roethlisberger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Roethlisberger "Ben Roethlisberger") in 2004;[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-36) the selection was announced by Steelers' legend [Franco Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franco_Harris "Franco Harris") in one of his last public appearances with the team before his unexpected death on December 20, 2022.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-37) With the starting quarterback position wide open following Roethlisberger's retirement, Pickett was named the backup quarterback for the Steelers behind starter [Mitchell Trubisky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitchell_Trubisky "Mitchell Trubisky").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-38) Initially, Pickett was designated as the team’s third-string quarterback behind both Trubisky and veteran [Mason Rudolph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mason_Rudolph_(American_football) "Mason Rudolph (American football)"), but head coach [Mike Tomlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Tomlin "Mike Tomlin") would adjust the depth chart to put Pickett in the backup role citing a "clerical error" with the original depth chart.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-39)

Pickett made his NFL debut in the second half of a Week 4 loss against the [New York Jets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Jets "New York Jets") after Trubisky was benched.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-40) Pickett completed 10-of-13 passes for 120 yards and rushed for two touchdowns, but threw three interceptions in the 24–20 loss. On his first career pass attempt, Pickett threw a deep ball to wide receiver [Chase Claypool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chase_Claypool "Chase Claypool") that was intercepted by safety [Jordan Whitehead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan_Whitehead "Jordan Whitehead"). On his second drive, Pickett scored his first NFL touchdown on a one-yard rush.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-41)

On October 4, Pickett was named the starter by head coach Tomlin.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-42) In his first career start against the [Buffalo Bills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buffalo_Bills "Buffalo Bills"), Pickett completed 34-of-51 passes for 327 yards and an interception during the 38–3 road loss.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-43) The following week against the [Tampa Bay Buccaneers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tampa_Bay_Buccaneers "Tampa Bay Buccaneers"), Pickett threw his first touchdown pass to running back [Najee Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Najee_Harris "Najee Harris"), but he exited the narrow 20–18 victory during the third quarter with a [concussion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concussion "Concussion").[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-44)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-StunBrady-45)

During Week 14, in a narrow 16–14 loss to the [Baltimore Ravens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltimore_Ravens "Baltimore Ravens"), Pickett once again suffered a concussion.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-46) He was ruled out for Week 15 against the [Carolina Panthers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carolina_Panthers "Carolina Panthers"), but started in Week 16 against the [Las Vegas Raiders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas_Raiders "Las Vegas Raiders").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-47)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-48) Pickett threw a game-winning 14-yard touchdown to wide receiver [George Pickens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Pickens "George Pickens") with under a minute left and finished the 13–10 victory with 244 passing yards, the aforementioned touchdown, and an interception.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-49)

During Week 17 against the Ravens, Pickett threw the game-winning touchdown with under a minute left for the second consecutive game; a 10-yard pass to Harris. Pickett finished the 16–13 road victory with 168 passing yards and the touchdown, keeping the Steelers' playoff hopes alive.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-50) Pickett became the first rookie quarterback in NFL history to throw a game-winning touchdown in the final minute of the fourth quarter in two consecutive games.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-51)

Pickett finished his rookie season with 2,404 passing yards, seven touchdowns, and nine interceptions, to go along with 55 carries for 237 yards and three touchdowns in 13 games with 12 starts.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-52) On March 13, 2023, the game ball from the Steelers' victory over the [Las Vegas Raiders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Las_Vegas_Raiders_season "2023 Las Vegas Raiders season") was put on display in the [Professional Football Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_Football_Hall_of_Fame "Professional Football Hall of Fame").

#### 2023

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenny_Pickett&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2023")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d2/KennyPickett2023.jpg/250px-KennyPickett2023.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:KennyPickett2023.jpg)

Pickett in 2023

During Week 3 against the Raiders, Pickett threw for 235 yards and two touchdowns in the 23–18 road victory, marking his first professional game with multiple touchdown passes.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-53) In the next game against the [Houston Texans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Houston_Texans_season "2023 Houston Texans season"), Pickett completed 15-of-23 passes for 114 yards and an interception before leaving the eventual 30–6 road loss in the third quarter with a bone bruise.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-54) Three weeks later against the [Los Angeles Rams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Los_Angeles_Rams_season "2023 Los Angeles Rams season"), Pickett had 230 passing yards and scored his first rushing touchdown of the season on a quarterback sneak in the 24–17 road victory.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-55)

During a Week 8 loss of 20–10 to the [Jacksonville Jaguars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Jacksonville_Jaguars_season "2023 Jacksonville Jaguars season"), Pickett had 73 passing yards and suffered a rib injury late in the second quarter and did not return.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-56) However, he started in the next game against the [Tennessee Titans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Tennessee_Titans_season "2023 Tennessee Titans season") and threw for 160 yards and the game-winning touchdown during the 20–16 victory.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-57)

In Week 13 against the [Arizona Cardinals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona_Cardinals "Arizona Cardinals"), Pickett had 70 passing yards before leaving the 24–10 loss with a high ankle sprain.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-58) He underwent surgery to accelerate the healing process on his ankle.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-59)

In the regular-season finale against the Ravens, Pickett was listed as active for the first time since his injury, but was demoted to backup duties following the success of Mason Rudolph.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-60) Rudolph started in the Steelers' 31–17 Wild Card loss to the Buffalo Bills.

Pickett finished his second professional season with 2,070 passing yards and the lowest touchdown percentage of all eligible starting quarterbacks in the league, only throwing for six touchdowns (as well as four interceptions) out of 324 pass attempts across 12 games and as many starts.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-o797-61)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-62) Pickett's passer rating improved from 76.7 to 81.4.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-63)

### Philadelphia Eagles

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenny_Pickett&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Philadelphia Eagles")]

Following the Steelers' signing of [Russell Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russell_Wilson "Russell Wilson") in the 2024 offseason, Pickett requested a trade.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-64) On March 16, 2024, he was traded to the [Philadelphia Eagles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_Eagles "Philadelphia Eagles") along with a 2024 fourth-round pick (No. 120; [Jaylen Wright](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaylen_Wright "Jaylen Wright")) in exchange for a 2024 third-round pick (No. 98; [Payton Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Payton_Wilson "Payton Wilson")) and two 2025 seventh-round picks (No. 223 went to the [Seattle Seahawks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seattle_Seahawks "Seattle Seahawks") where they selected [Damien Martinez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Damien_Martinez "Damien Martinez")) (No. 229; [Donte Kent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donte_Kent "Donte Kent")).[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-65)

Pickett entered the season as the backup quarterback behind incumbent starter [Jalen Hurts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jalen_Hurts "Jalen Hurts"), despite a competition with [Tanner McKee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanner_McKee "Tanner McKee").[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-f354-66) Pickett made his Eagles debut during a Week 7 28–3 road victory over the [New York Giants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_New_York_Giants_season "2024 New York Giants season"). He attempted one pass, but it fell incomplete.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-67) Three weeks later, in a 34–6 road victory over the [Dallas Cowboys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Dallas_Cowboys_season "2024 Dallas Cowboys season"), Pickett would relieve Hurts, completing 1-of-2 passes for five yards.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-68)

During Week 16 against the [Washington Commanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Commanders "Washington Commanders"), Pickett replaced Hurts after he was ruled out with a [concussion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concussion "Concussion").[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-69) Pickett finished the 36–33 road loss with 143 passing yards, a touchdown and an interception. Despite suffering a rib injury, he did not miss any plays.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-70)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-71) Pickett was named the Eagles' starter for the Week 17 matchup against the Cowboys.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-r954-72) He completed 10-of-15 passes for 143 yards and a touchdown, while also rushing for a touchdown before leaving the eventual 41–7 victory in the third quarter with a rib injury.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-73)[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-g533-74)

At the end of the NFC Championship game against the [Washington Commanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Commanders "Washington Commanders"), Pickett was substituted in for Hurts to kneel out the 55–23 victory.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-r834-75) Pickett won his first Super Bowl when the Eagles defeated the [Kansas City Chiefs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Kansas_City_Chiefs_season "2024 Kansas City Chiefs season") in [Super Bowl LIX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LIX "Super Bowl LIX"). Pickett finished the game at quarterback for the Eagles, handing the ball off, attempting one pass, and then kneeling to close out the 40–22 victory.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-h456-76)

### Cleveland Browns

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenny_Pickett&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Cleveland Browns")]

On March 12, 2025, the Eagles traded Pickett to the [Cleveland Browns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland_Browns "Cleveland Browns") in exchange for [Dorian Thompson-Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorian_Thompson-Robinson "Dorian Thompson-Robinson") and a fifth-round pick in the [2025 NFL draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_NFL_draft "2025 NFL draft").[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-77) Pickett entered training camp in a four-way competition with [Joe Flacco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Flacco "Joe Flacco"), [Dillon Gabriel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dillon_Gabriel "Dillon Gabriel"), and [Shedeur Sanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shedeur_Sanders "Shedeur Sanders") for Cleveland's starting quarterback role.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-78) A hamstring injury limited his participation in camp, and Pickett was named Flacco's backup before the start of the [2025 NFL season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_NFL_season "2025 NFL season").[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-79)

### Las Vegas Raiders

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenny_Pickett&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Las Vegas Raiders")]

On August 25, 2025, Pickett was traded to the [Las Vegas Raiders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas_Raiders "Las Vegas Raiders") in exchange for a fifth-round pick (141st overall) in the [2026 NFL draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_NFL_draft "2026 NFL draft").[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-80) He spent the 2025 season as the backup to [Geno Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geno_Smith "Geno Smith"). After Smith hurt his shoulder in a Week 14 loss to the [Denver Broncos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Denver_Broncos_season "2025 Denver Broncos season"), Pickett entered the game and made all but three of his 11 passes for 96 yards and a touchdown.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-81) Pickett was named the starter for the following week against the [Philadelphia Eagles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Philadelphia_Eagles_season "2025 Philadelphia Eagles season"),[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-82) where he completed 15-of-25 passes for 64 yards, was intercepted once, and sacked four times as the Raiders lost 31–0.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-83) Smith returned to the starting position for Week 16.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-84)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kenny_Pickett&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Pickett married Amy Paternoster, a former women's soccer player at [Princeton University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Princeton_University "Princeton University"), on June 24, 2023.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-86) His sister, Alex,[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-m535-87) played collegiate soccer at [East Stroudsburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Stroudsburg_University_of_Pennsylvania "East Stroudsburg University of Pennsylvania"),[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-z681-88) and became the coach of [Seton Hill University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seton_Hill_University "Seton Hill University")'s women's soccer team in 2019.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-x985-89)

From 2022 to 2024, Pickett resided in [Cranberry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cranberry_Township,_Butler_County,_Pennsylvania "Cranberry Township, Butler County, Pennsylvania"), a suburb of [Pittsburgh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh "Pittsburgh"). He sold his home in Cranberry following his trade to the [Philadelphia Eagles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_Eagles "Philadelphia Eagles") in early 2024.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Pickett#cite_note-a683-90)

**Justin Patrick Herbert** (born March 10, 1998) is an American professional [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_football "American football")[quarterback](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quarterback "Quarterback") for the [Los Angeles Chargers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Chargers "Los Angeles Chargers") of the [National Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League") (NFL). He played [college football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_football "College football") for the [Oregon Ducks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oregon_Ducks_football "Oregon Ducks football"), where he won the [2019 Pac-12 Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Pac-12_Football_Championship_Game "2019 Pac-12 Football Championship Game"), and was selected by the Chargers as the sixth overall pick in the 2020 NFL draft.

Herbert became the Chargers' starting quarterback in the second game of his rookie season. He remained the starter for the rest of the season and set several rookie statistical records, including the most touchdown passes and 300-yard games. He was named the [AP NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Associated_Press_NFL_Rookie_of_the_Year_Award "Associated Press NFL Rookie of the Year Award") for his performance. In 2021, he became the first quarterback in Chargers history to throw for over 5,000 yards and was named to his first [Pro Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pro_Bowl "Pro Bowl"). He signed a five-year, $262.5 million contract extension ahead of the 2023 season.

School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheldon_High_School_(Oregon) "Sheldon High School (Oregon)"), where he played football, basketball, and baseball.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-3) During the third football game of his junior season, he suffered a broken leg, complicating his recruitment touchdowns.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-Sheldon-5) He was named first-team All-State[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-6) and the Southwest ## College career

### 2016 season

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/51/Justin_Herbert_2.png/250px-Justin_Herbert_2.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Justin_Herbert_2.png)

Herbert with [Oregon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oregon_Ducks_football "Oregon Ducks football")

Entering his true freshman season listed as QB2 on the depth chart behind [Dakota Prukop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dakota_Prukop "Dakota Prukop"),[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-10) Herbert became the first true freshman at Oregon to start at quarterback since [Chris Miller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Miller_(quarterback) "Chris Miller (quarterback)") in 1983 when the Ducks took on their arch-rivals, the [Washington Huskies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Washington_Huskies_football_team "2016 Washington Huskies football team"), on October 8, 2016.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-11) Despite Herbert setting or equaling Oregon's single-game records for total offensive yards (512), passing yards (489), and touchdown passes (6),[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-:0-12) the Ducks finished with their worst season in 25 years, going 4–8 and failing to make a bowl game for the first time in over a decade.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-13)

After the fifth game of the season, Herbert became the starting quarterback. He showcased his talents by throwing for 1,936 yards including 19 touchdowns with just four interceptions in eight starts.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-:0-12)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-14) He led a come-from-behind upset when playing the ranked No. 11 [Utah Utes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Utah_Utes_football_team "2016 Utah Utes football team"). The team scored four touchdowns in the final 15:27 of the game to overcome a 14–3 deficit. On the final drive, Herbert completed 6-of-9 passes for 63 yards, including a 17-yard game-winning touchdown pass with two seconds left.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-15)

### 2017 season

The Ducks entered the 2017 season with new head coach [Willie Taggart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Taggart "Willie Taggart").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-16) Leading the Ducks to a 4–1 start, Herbert's transition from the [Chip Kelly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chip_Kelly "Chip Kelly")/[Mark Helfrich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Helfrich_(American_football) "Mark Helfrich (American football)")-era's "Blur Offense" to Taggart's "Gulf Coast Offense" was successful, before he fractured his collarbone against the [California Golden Bears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_California_Golden_Bears_football_team "2017 California Golden Bears football team") on September 30, 2017.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-17)

Without Herbert in the lineup, the Ducks dropped four of their next five games, and the offense went from averaging 49.2 points per game to just 15.0 points per game.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-18) Herbert returned to help the Ducks win their last two regular season games to become bowl eligible.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-19) The Ducks were selected to play the [Boise State Broncos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Boise_State_Broncos_football_team "2017 Boise State Broncos football team") in the [Las Vegas Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Las_Vegas_Bowl "2017 Las Vegas Bowl") but their performance fell flat and the Ducks lost 38–28 after Taggart left the team to become the head coach at [Florida State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_State_Seminoles_football "Florida State Seminoles football") a week before their bowl game.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-21)

In eight starts, Herbert had a 6–2 record and threw for 1,983 yards on 139-of-206 passing attempts (67.5%), including 15 touchdowns against only five interceptions. He also rushed the ball 44 times for 183 yards and five touchdowns.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-22) Herbert was named first-team [CoSIDA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CoSIDA "CoSIDA") Academic All-American with a 4.08 grade-point average in biology.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-goducks.com-23)

### 2018 season

Herbert entered his third collegiate season as an early [Heisman Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heisman_Trophy "Heisman Trophy") candidate despite being coached by a third different head coach. He also learned a third different offensive scheme with new head coach [Mario Cristobal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Cristobal "Mario Cristobal"), transitioning from the [spread offense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spread_offense "Spread offense") to the [pistol offense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pistol_offense "Pistol offense").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-espn.com-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-25) Herbert led the Ducks to a 9–4 record and a victory in the [Redbox Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Redbox_Bowl "2018 Redbox Bowl"). He finished the year with 3,151 passing yards, 29 passing touchdowns, and two rushing touchdowns.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-26) His 31 total touchdowns were good for second in the [Pac-12 Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pac-12_Conference "Pac-12 Conference") behind [Gardner Minshew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gardner_Minshew "Gardner Minshew") of the [Washington State Cougars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_State_Cougars_football "Washington State Cougars football").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-27) He was named to the Pac-12 All-Academic first-team.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-2018_all-academic-28)

### 2019 season

Herbert (right) in a game against the [Arizona State Sun Devils](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Arizona_State_Sun_Devils_football_team "2019 Arizona State Sun Devils football team") in 2019

Despite projecting as a high draft pick,[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-29) Herbert announced that he would return to Oregon for his senior season.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-30) He led the Ducks to a 12–2 record, including a win in the [Rose Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Rose_Bowl "2020 Rose Bowl") where he ran for three touchdowns and was named Offensive MVP.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-31)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-32) In his best statistical collegiate season, Herbert totaled 3,471 passing yards, 32 passing touchdowns, and four rushing touchdowns.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-33) In addition to his on-field success, Herbert was named the 30th recipient of the [William V. Campbell Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_V._Campbell_Trophy "William V. Campbell Trophy"), which recognizes excellence in academics, athletics, and leadership, and is also referred to as the "Academic Heisman". He graduated from Oregon with a bachelor's degree in [general science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_science "General science").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-35)

### 2020

See also: [2020 Los Angeles Chargers season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Los_Angeles_Chargers_season "2020 Los Angeles Chargers season")

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e3/Los_Angeles_Chargers_%2851156573705%29.jpg/250px-Los_Angeles_Chargers_%2851156573705%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Los_Angeles_Chargers_(51156573705).jpg)

Herbert's locker at [SoFi Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SoFi_Stadium "SoFi Stadium")

Herbert was selected sixth overall by the [Los Angeles Chargers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Chargers "Los Angeles Chargers") in the first round of the 2020 NFL draft.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-39) He was the third quarterback taken, behind Joe Burrow and [Tua Tagovailoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tua_Tagovailoa "Tua Tagovailoa").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-40) On July 25, 2020, Herbert signed his four-year rookie contract, worth a fully guaranteed $26.6 million.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-41) Herbert's jersey was listed as the 12th best selling jersey to start the season.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-42) Herbert was named the backup quarterback behind starter [Tyrod Taylor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyrod_Taylor "Tyrod Taylor") ahead of Week 1.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-43)

On September 20, 2020, Herbert made his first NFL start in Week 2 against the [Kansas City Chiefs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City_Chiefs "Kansas City Chiefs"), replacing Taylor, who was ruled inactive after the team's doctor accidentally punctured his lung.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-44) He finished with 311 passing yards, one touchdown, one interception, and one rushing score as the Chargers lost 23–20 in overtime.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-45) He became only the third player in NFL history to pass for at least 300 yards and rush for a touchdown in his first career game.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-46) During Week 4 against the [Tampa Bay Buccaneers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tampa_Bay_Buccaneers "Tampa Bay Buccaneers"), Herbert completed 20 passes out of 25 attempts for 290 yards, three touchdowns, and an interception as the Chargers lost 38–31.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-47) On October 8, 2020, Herbert was named the starting quarterback for the Chargers over Taylor going forward.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-48)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-49)

In Week 5 against the [New Orleans Saints](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans_Saints "New Orleans Saints") on _Monday Night Football_, Herbert threw for 264 yards and four touchdowns during the 30–27 overtime loss.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-50) He became the first rookie in NFL history to throw for four touchdown passes on _Monday Night Football_.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-51) Herbert was named Offensive Rookie of the Month after throwing 10 touchdowns to one interception in three starts with 901 passing yards and a 122.2 passer rating.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-52) He also became the first rookie quarterback in NFL history with multiple touchdowns in seven consecutive games.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-53) Herbert was named the Offensive Rookie of the Month for his performance in November.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-54)

On December 27, 2020, Herbert threw his 28th passing touchdown of the season against the [Denver Broncos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver_Broncos "Denver Broncos"), breaking the NFL record for most passing touchdowns by a rookie (previously held by [Baker Mayfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baker_Mayfield "Baker Mayfield")) during the 19–16 win.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-55) During the game, he also reached 4,000 yards passing for the season, becoming only the fourth rookie quarterback to achieve the feat.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-56) He was named Rookie of the Year and Offensive Rookie of the Year by the [Pro Football Writers of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pro_Football_Writers_of_America "Pro Football Writers of America").[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-57) Herbert finished the 2020 season on a four-game winning streak with 4,336 yards passing, 31 touchdowns, and 10 interceptions.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-58) He was named to the NFL All-Rookie Team.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-59) He was ranked 56th by his fellow players on the [NFL Top 100 Players of 2021](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_Top_100_Players_of_2021 "NFL Top 100 Players of 2021").[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-60)

### 2021

See also: [2021 Los Angeles Chargers season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Los_Angeles_Chargers_season "2021 Los Angeles Chargers season")

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/88/Justin_Herbert_%2851459803577%29.jpg/250px-Justin_Herbert_%2851459803577%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Justin_Herbert_(51459803577).jpg)

Herbert in a game against the [Washington Football Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Washington_Football_Team_season "2021 Washington Football Team season"), 2021

Herbert helped lead the Chargers to a 4–1 start, including a Week 3 30–24 victory over the [Kansas City Chiefs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City_Chiefs "Kansas City Chiefs").[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-61) In Week 5, against the [Cleveland Browns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland_Browns "Cleveland Browns"), Herbert had his best statistical game of the season. He had 398 passing yards, four passing touchdowns, and a rushing touchdown in a 47–42 shootout victory.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-62) In Week 9, Herbert had three total touchdowns while completing 32-of-38 passes for 356 yards, two touchdowns, a rushing touchdown, and no interceptions in a 27–24 win over the [Philadelphia Eagles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_Eagles "Philadelphia Eagles"), earning [American Football Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Football_Conference "American Football Conference") (AFC) Offensive Player of the Week honors.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-63) Against the [Pittsburgh Steelers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_Steelers "Pittsburgh Steelers") on Week 11, Herbert had 382 passing yards, three touchdowns, and an interception in a 41–37 win.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-64)

In a Week 13 matchup against the [Cincinnati Bengals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cincinnati_Bengals "Cincinnati Bengals"), Herbert had 317 passing yards, three passing touchdowns, and an interception in a 41–22 victory, earning him his second AFC Offensive Player of the Week berth of the season.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-65) He followed that performance with 275 passing yards, three passing touchdowns, and no interceptions in Week 14 against the [New York Giants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Giants "New York Giants"), lifting the Chargers to a 37–21 victory, and an 8–5 record. He earned his second consecutive, and third overall, AFC Offensive Player of the Week honor for his performance.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-66)

In Week 15, playing against the Chiefs, Herbert surpassed [Andrew Luck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Luck "Andrew Luck")'s record for the most passing yards in an NFL quarterback's first two seasons.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-67) Additionally, he surpassed [Dan Marino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Marino "Dan Marino")'s record for the most total touchdowns in an NFL quarterback's first two seasons.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-68) In a Week 18 win or tie or go home situation against the [Las Vegas Raiders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas_Raiders "Las Vegas Raiders"), Herbert threw for 383 yards, three touchdowns, and an interception in the [35–32 overtime loss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Los_Angeles_Chargers%E2%80%93Las_Vegas_Raiders_game "2021 Los Angeles Chargers–Las Vegas Raiders game"), eliminating the Chargers from the playoffs.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-69)

In the 2021 season, Herbert set franchise records with 5,014 passing yards, 38 passing touchdowns, and 15 interceptions.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-sspassing-70) In addition, he had 63 carries for 302 rushing yards and three rushing touchdowns, leading the Chargers to a 9–8 record and his first career [Pro Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pro_Bowl "Pro Bowl").[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-71)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-72) Herbert became the first quarterback in franchise history to throw for at least 5,000 yards in a single season.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-73) He was ranked 40th by his fellow players on the [NFL Top 100 Players of 2022](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_Top_100_Players_of_2022 "NFL Top 100 Players of 2022").[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-74)

### 2022

See also: [2022 Los Angeles Chargers season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Los_Angeles_Chargers_season "2022 Los Angeles Chargers season")

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/df/Washington_Football_Team_vs._Baltimore_Ravens%2C_August_27%2C_2021_D50_6379_%2851459802632%29_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Washington_Football_Team_vs._Baltimore_Ravens%2C_August_27%2C_2021_D50_6379_%2851459802632%29_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Washington_Football_Team_vs._Baltimore_Ravens,_August_27,_2021_D50_6379_(51459802632)_(cropped).jpg)

Herbert taking a snap in the [shotgun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shotgun_formation "Shotgun formation")

In Week 1 against the [Las Vegas Raiders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas_Raiders "Las Vegas Raiders"), Herbert threw for 279 yards and three touchdowns in the 24–19 win.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-75) In Week 2 against the [Kansas City Chiefs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City_Chiefs "Kansas City Chiefs"), Herbert threw for 334 yards and three touchdowns for the second consecutive game. In the fourth quarter, Herbert suffered a fracture to his rib cartilage.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-76) Despite a late touchdown, the Chargers would go on to lose 27–24.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-77) In Week 6 against the [Denver Broncos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver_Broncos "Denver Broncos"), Herbert completed 37 of 57 passes for 238 yards, no touchdowns, and an interception in the 19–16 victory. His 57 passes were the most in a winning effort without a passing touchdown in NFL history.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-78) Overall, Herbert passed for 4,739 yards, 25 touchdowns, and ten interceptions in 17 games in the 2022 season.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-79) He set single-season franchise records for pass attempts and completions.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-sspassing-70) The Chargers finished with a 10–7 record and earned a playoff berth.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-80)

In his first playoff game, Herbert passed for 273 yards and a touchdown as the Chargers fell to the [Jacksonville Jaguars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacksonville_Jaguars "Jacksonville Jaguars") 31–30 in the [Wild Card Round](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_NFL_playoffs#AFC:_Jacksonville_Jaguars_31,_Los_Angeles_Chargers_30 "2022–23 NFL playoffs").[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-81) The Chargers surrendered a 27–0 lead for the third-largest blown lead in NFL playoff history.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-82)

After the season, he was ranked 32nd by his fellow players on the [NFL Top 100 Players of 2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_Top_100_Players_of_2023 "NFL Top 100 Players of 2023").[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-83)

### 2023

See also: [2023 Los Angeles Chargers season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Los_Angeles_Chargers_season "2023 Los Angeles Chargers season")

On April 28, 2023, the Chargers picked up the fifth-year option on Herbert's contract.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-84) On July 25, he signed a five-year extension worth $262.5 million, which extends through the 2029 season. At the time of the signing, the deal made Herbert the highest-paid player in NFL history (surpassing the previous record set by [Lamar Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lamar_Jackson "Lamar Jackson") just months earlier) and the highest-paid NFL quarterback based on average annual value at $52.5 million per season.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-85)[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-86) However, this record deal would be surpassed by Joe Burrow's extension just two months later.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-87)

After starting the season 0–2, Herbert had a fourth-quarter comeback against the [Minnesota Vikings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota_Vikings "Minnesota Vikings") in Week 3, resulting in a 28–24 win. This game also marked his first 400-yard passing performance in the NFL. In Week 14 against the [Denver Broncos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver_Broncos "Denver Broncos"), Herbert suffered a broken index finger on his throwing hand in the second quarter and was ruled out for the remainder of the game.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-88) On December 12, the Chargers announced Herbert would undergo surgery and was placed on [injured reserve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Injured_reserve "Injured reserve"), ending his season.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-89) He was ranked 75 by his fellow players on the [NFL Top 100 Players of 2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_Top_100_Players_of_2024 "NFL Top 100 Players of 2024").[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-90)

### 2024

See also: [2024 Los Angeles Chargers season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Los_Angeles_Chargers_season "2024 Los Angeles Chargers season")

Herbert entered his fifth NFL season with his third different head coach, as [Brandon Staley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandon_Staley "Brandon Staley") was replaced by [Jim Harbaugh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Harbaugh "Jim Harbaugh").[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-91) Herbert began the season with a 90-plus passer rating in his first ten games, the longest streak of starts with a 90-plus passer rating by any quarterback to begin a season since 2018.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-92) In Week 10 against the [Tennessee Titans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee_Titans "Tennessee Titans"), Herbert passed [David Carr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Carr_(American_football) "David Carr (American football)") for the most completions by a quarterback in their first five seasons.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-93) From Weeks 2 to 14, Herbert recorded 357 consecutive pass attempts without an interception, the fifth-longest such streak in NFL history.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-94) In a 40–7 victory against the [New England Patriots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_England_Patriots "New England Patriots") in Week 17, Herbert passed for 281 yards and three touchdowns to become the third player in NFL history with at least 3,000 passing yards and 20 touchdown passes in each of his first five seasons. The win also clinched a playoff berth for the Chargers, marking their second appearance in three seasons.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-95) He finished the regular season with 346 yards, two touchdowns, and no turnovers in a 34–20 win over the Raiders.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-96)

Herbert had an efficient year in his first season under Jim Harbaugh, finishing with 3,870 passing yards, 23 touchdowns, and just three interceptions, along with career highs in rushing yards.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-97) Herbert's 23:3 TD–INT ratio (7.67) ranks eighth all-time in NFL history among quarterbacks with at least 15 touchdown passes in a season. His numbers on [play-action](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Play-action_pass "Play-action pass") passes were among the best in the league, completing 74.7 percent for 1,617 yards with eight touchdowns and just two interceptions on such throws.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-98) Despite a productive regular season, Herbert had the worst game of his career in the [Wild Card Round](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024%E2%80%9325_NFL_playoffs#AFC:_Houston_Texans_32,_Los_Angeles_Chargers_12 "2024–25 NFL playoffs") against the [Houston Texans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_Texans "Houston Texans"), posting a career-low 43.8% completion percentage, one touchdown, and a career-high four interceptions for a career-low passer rating of 40.9 as the Chargers lost 32–12.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-99) He was ranked 56th by his fellow players on the [NFL Top 100 Players of 2025](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_Top_100_Players_of_2025 "NFL Top 100 Players of 2025").[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-100)

See also: [2025 Los Angeles Chargers season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Los_Angeles_Chargers_season "2025 Los Angeles Chargers season")

Herbert and the Chargers opened the 2025 season playing in [São Paulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A3o_Paulo "São Paulo"), Brazil, against the [Kansas City Chiefs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Kansas_City_Chiefs_season "2025 Kansas City Chiefs season"). They won 27–21 with Herbert completing 25 out of 34 passes for 318 passing yards and 3 passing touchdowns.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-101) In Week 8 against the [Minnesota Vikings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Minnesota_Vikings_season "2025 Minnesota Vikings season"), Herbert passed [Peyton Manning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peyton_Manning "Peyton Manning") for the most completions by a quarterback in their first six seasons.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-102) On December 1, he underwent surgery to repair a fracture in his left hand, which he suffered in Week 14 against the [Philadelphia Eagles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Philadelphia_Eagles_season "2025 Philadelphia Eagles season").[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-103) On December 23, Herbert was named to his second career Pro Bowl.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-104) Playing behind an offensive line that lost starters [Joe Alt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Alt "Joe Alt") and [Rashawn Slater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rashawn_Slater "Rashawn Slater") to season-ending injuries, Herbert led the team to 11 wins while being pressured on a league-high 288 dropbacks.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-105) He ran for a career-high 498 yards. The Chargers lost their playoff opener 16–3 to the Patriots. "I didn't play well enough and didn't make any plays," Herbert said. He completed 19 of 31 passes for 159 yards with no touchdowns, was sacked six times, and lost a fumble, while leading the Chargers in rushing with 55 yards.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-106)[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-107)

## Personal life

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/eb/Madison_Beer_%26_Justin_Herbert_-_2025_Commanders_at_Chargers_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Madison_Beer_%26_Justin_Herbert_-_2025_Commanders_at_Chargers_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Madison_Beer_&_Justin_Herbert_-_2025_Commanders_at_Chargers_(cropped).jpg)

Herbert with fiancée and singer-songwriter [Madison Beer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madison_Beer "Madison Beer"), 2025

Herbert's maternal grandfather, Rich Schwab, played receiver at the [University of Oregon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Oregon "University of Oregon") in the 1960s.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-espn.com-24) His paternal grandfather, Roger Herbert, was a biology teacher at Sheldon High School and fueled Herbert’s interest in science.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-133) His father, Mark Herbert, played football and ran track at the [University of Montana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Montana "University of Montana").[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-134) Herbert was a [San Diego Chargers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego_Chargers "San Diego Chargers") fan growing up.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-135) Herbert's younger brother, [Patrick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Herbert_(American_football) "Patrick Herbert (American football)"), currently plays [tight end](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tight_end "Tight end") (also on the Chargers).[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-136) His older brother, Mitchell, played [wide receiver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wide_receiver "Wide receiver") at [Montana State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montana_State_University "Montana State University").[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-137) Herbert has been in a relationship with singer-songwriter [Madison Beer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madison_Beer "Madison Beer") since 2025.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-138) They announced their engagement on July 28, 2026.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-139)

### Chess

Herbert, after being beaten by Chargers teammate [Rashawn Slater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rashawn_Slater "Rashawn Slater") in [chess](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chess "Chess") during a road trip in 2024 to play the [Carolina Panthers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carolina_Panthers "Carolina Panthers"), decided to improve his play of the game over the next year, studying chess from various sources. He appeared with Swedish chess player, [Woman FIDE Master](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woman_FIDE_Master "Woman FIDE Master") and internet chess celebrity [Anna Cramling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anna_Cramling "Anna Cramling") in a video in 2025 to talk about his journey to improve his chess game.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-ChessSI-140)[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-CramlingVideo-141)

**Justin Patrick Herbert** (born March 10, 1998) is an American professional [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_football "American football")[quarterback](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quarterback "Quarterback") for the [Los Angeles Chargers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Chargers "Los Angeles Chargers") of the [National Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League") (NFL). He played [college football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_football "College football") for the [Oregon Ducks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oregon_Ducks_football "Oregon Ducks football"), where he won the [2019 Pac-12 Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Pac-12_Football_Championship_Game "2019 Pac-12 Football Championship Game"), and was selected by the Chargers as the sixth overall pick in the 2020 NFL draft.

Herbert became the Chargers' starting quarterback in the second game of his rookie season. He remained the starter for the rest of the season and set several rookie statistical records, including the most touchdown passes and 300-yard games. He was named the [AP NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Associated_Press_NFL_Rookie_of_the_Year_Award "Associated Press NFL Rookie of the Year Award") for his performance. In 2021, he became the first quarterback in Chargers history to throw for over 5,000 yards and was named to his first [Pro Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pro_Bowl "Pro Bowl"). He signed a five-year, $262.5 million contract extension ahead of the 2023 season.

Oregon"),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-2) on March 10, 1998, and attended [Sheldon High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheldon_High_School_(Oregon) "Sheldon High School (Oregon)"), where he played football, basketball, and baseball.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-3) During the third football game of his junior season, he suffered a broken leg, complicating his recruitment ## College career

### 2016 season

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/51/Justin_Herbert_2.png/250px-Justin_Herbert_2.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Justin_Herbert_2.png)

Herbert with [Oregon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oregon_Ducks_football "Oregon Ducks football")

Entering his true freshman season listed as QB2 on the depth chart behind [Dakota Prukop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dakota_Prukop "Dakota Prukop"),[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-10) Herbert became the first true freshman at Oregon to start at quarterback since [Chris Miller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Miller_(quarterback) "Chris Miller (quarterback)") in 1983 when the Ducks took on their arch-rivals, the [Washington Huskies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Washington_Huskies_football_team "2016 Washington Huskies football team"), on October 8, 2016.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-11) Despite Herbert setting or equaling Oregon's single-game records for total offensive yards (512), passing yards (489), and touchdown passes (6),[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-:0-12) the Ducks finished with their worst season in 25 years, going 4–8 and failing to make a bowl game for the first time in over a decade.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-13)

After the fifth game of the season, Herbert became the starting quarterback. He showcased his talents by throwing for 1,936 yards including 19 touchdowns with just four interceptions in eight starts.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-:0-12)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-14) He led a come-from-behind upset when playing the ranked No. 11 [Utah Utes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Utah_Utes_football_team "2016 Utah Utes football team"). The team scored four touchdowns in the final 15:27 of the game to overcome a 14–3 deficit. On the final drive, Herbert completed 6-of-9 passes for 63 yards, including a 17-yard game-winning touchdown pass with two seconds left.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-15)

### 2017 season

The Ducks entered the 2017 season with new head coach [Willie Taggart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Taggart "Willie Taggart").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-16) Leading the Ducks to a 4–1 start, Herbert's transition from the [Chip Kelly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chip_Kelly "Chip Kelly")/[Mark Helfrich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Helfrich_(American_football) "Mark Helfrich (American football)")-era's "Blur Offense" to Taggart's "Gulf Coast Offense" was successful, before he fractured his collarbone against the [California Golden Bears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_California_Golden_Bears_football_team "2017 California Golden Bears football team") on September 30, 2017.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-17)

Without Herbert in the lineup, the Ducks dropped four of their next five games, and the offense went from averaging 49.2 points per game to just 15.0 points per game.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-18) Herbert returned to help the Ducks win their last two regular season games to become bowl eligible.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-19) The Ducks were selected to play the [Boise State Broncos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Boise_State_Broncos_football_team "2017 Boise State Broncos football team") in the [Las Vegas Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Las_Vegas_Bowl "2017 Las Vegas Bowl") but their performance fell flat and the Ducks lost 38–28 after Taggart left the team to become the head coach at [Florida State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_State_Seminoles_football "Florida State Seminoles football") a week before their bowl game.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-21)

In eight starts, Herbert had a 6–2 record and threw for 1,983 yards on 139-of-206 passing attempts (67.5%), including 15 touchdowns against only five interceptions. He also rushed the ball 44 times for 183 yards and five touchdowns.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-22) Herbert was named first-team [CoSIDA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CoSIDA "CoSIDA") Academic All-American with a 4.08 grade-point average in biology.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-goducks.com-23)

### 2018 season

Herbert entered his third collegiate season as an early [Heisman Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heisman_Trophy "Heisman Trophy") candidate despite being coached by a third different head coach. He also learned a third different offensive scheme with new head coach [Mario Cristobal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Cristobal "Mario Cristobal"), transitioning from the [spread offense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spread_offense "Spread offense") to the [pistol offense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pistol_offense "Pistol offense").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-espn.com-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-25) Herbert led the Ducks to a 9–4 record and a victory in the [Redbox Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Redbox_Bowl "2018 Redbox Bowl"). He finished the year with 3,151 passing yards, 29 passing touchdowns, and two rushing touchdowns.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-26) His 31 total touchdowns were good for second in the [Pac-12 Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pac-12_Conference "Pac-12 Conference") behind [Gardner Minshew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gardner_Minshew "Gardner Minshew") of the [Washington State Cougars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_State_Cougars_football "Washington State Cougars football").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-27) He was named to the Pac-12 All-Academic first-team.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-2018_all-academic-28)

### 2019 season

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c7/Justin_Herbert.jpg/250px-Justin_Herbert.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Justin_Herbert.jpg)

Herbert (right) in a game against the [Arizona State Sun Devils](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Arizona_State_Sun_Devils_football_team "2019 Arizona State Sun Devils football team") in 2019

Despite projecting as a high draft pick,[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-29) Herbert announced that he would return to Oregon for his senior season.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-30) He led the Ducks to a 12–2 record, including a win in the [Rose Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Rose_Bowl "2020 Rose Bowl") where he ran for three touchdowns and was named Offensive MVP.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-31)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-32) In his best statistical collegiate season, Herbert totaled 3,471 passing yards, 32 passing touchdowns, and four rushing touchdowns.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-33) In addition to his on-field success, Herbert was named the 30th recipient of the [William V. Campbell Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_V._Campbell_Trophy "William V. Campbell Trophy"), which recognizes excellence in academics, athletics, and leadership, and is also referred to as the "Academic Heisman". He graduated from Oregon with a bachelor's degree in [general science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_science "General science").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-35)

### 2020

See also: [2020 Los Angeles Chargers season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Los_Angeles_Chargers_season "2020 Los Angeles Chargers season")

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e3/Los_Angeles_Chargers_%2851156573705%29.jpg/250px-Los_Angeles_Chargers_%2851156573705%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Los_Angeles_Chargers_(51156573705).jpg)

Herbert's locker at [SoFi Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SoFi_Stadium "SoFi Stadium")

Herbert was selected sixth overall by the [Los Angeles Chargers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Chargers "Los Angeles Chargers") in the first round of the 2020 NFL draft.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-39) He was the third quarterback taken, behind Joe Burrow and [Tua Tagovailoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tua_Tagovailoa "Tua Tagovailoa").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-40) On July 25, 2020, Herbert signed his four-year rookie contract, worth a fully guaranteed $26.6 million.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-41) Herbert's jersey was listed as the 12th best selling jersey to start the season.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-42) Herbert was named the backup quarterback behind starter [Tyrod Taylor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyrod_Taylor "Tyrod Taylor") ahead of Week 1.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-43)

On September 20, 2020, Herbert made his first NFL start in Week 2 against the [Kansas City Chiefs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City_Chiefs "Kansas City Chiefs"), replacing Taylor, who was ruled inactive after the team's doctor accidentally punctured his lung.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-44) He finished with 311 passing yards, one touchdown, one interception, and one rushing score as the Chargers lost 23–20 in overtime.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-45) He became only the third player in NFL history to pass for at least 300 yards and rush for a touchdown in his first career game.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-46) During Week 4 against the [Tampa Bay Buccaneers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tampa_Bay_Buccaneers "Tampa Bay Buccaneers"), Herbert completed 20 passes out of 25 attempts for 290 yards, three touchdowns, and an interception as the Chargers lost 38–31.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-47) On October 8, 2020, Herbert was named the starting quarterback for the Chargers over Taylor going forward.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-48)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-49)

In Week 5 against the [New Orleans Saints](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans_Saints "New Orleans Saints") on _Monday Night Football_, Herbert threw for 264 yards and four touchdowns during the 30–27 overtime loss.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-50) He became the first rookie in NFL history to throw for four touchdown passes on _Monday Night Football_.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-51) Herbert was named Offensive Rookie of the Month after throwing 10 touchdowns to one interception in three starts with 901 passing yards and a 122.2 passer rating.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-52) He also became the first rookie quarterback in NFL history with multiple touchdowns in seven consecutive games.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-53) Herbert was named the Offensive Rookie of the Month for his performance in November.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-54)

On December 27, 2020, Herbert threw his 28th passing touchdown of the season against the [Denver Broncos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver_Broncos "Denver Broncos"), breaking the NFL record for most passing touchdowns by a rookie (previously held by [Baker Mayfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baker_Mayfield "Baker Mayfield")) during the 19–16 win.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-55) During the game, he also reached 4,000 yards passing for the season, becoming only the fourth rookie quarterback to achieve the feat.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-56) He was named Rookie of the Year and Offensive Rookie of the Year by the [Pro Football Writers of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pro_Football_Writers_of_America "Pro Football Writers of America").[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-57) Herbert finished the 2020 season on a four-game winning streak with 4,336 yards passing, 31 touchdowns, and 10 interceptions.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-58) He was named to the NFL All-Rookie Team.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-59) He was ranked 56th by his fellow players on the [NFL Top 100 Players of 2021](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_Top_100_Players_of_2021 "NFL Top 100 Players of 2021").[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-60)

### 2021
