[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/88/Justin_Herbert_%2851459803577%29.jpg/250px-Justin_Herbert_%2851459803577%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Justin_Herbert_(51459803577).jpg)

Herbert in a game against the [Washington Football Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Washington_Football_Team_season "2021 Washington Football Team season"), 2021

Herbert helped lead the Chargers to a 4–1 start, including a Week 3 30–24 victory over the [Kansas City Chiefs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City_Chiefs "Kansas City Chiefs").[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-61) In Week 5, against the [Cleveland Browns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland_Browns "Cleveland Browns"), Herbert had his best statistical game of the season. He had 398 passing yards, four passing touchdowns, and a rushing touchdown in a 47–42 shootout victory.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-62) In Week 9, Herbert had three total touchdowns while completing 32-of-38 passes for 356 yards, two touchdowns, a rushing touchdown, and no interceptions in a 27–24 win over the [Philadelphia Eagles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_Eagles "Philadelphia Eagles"), earning [American Football Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Football_Conference "American Football Conference") (AFC) Offensive Player of the Week honors.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-63) Against the [Pittsburgh Steelers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh_Steelers "Pittsburgh Steelers") on Week 11, Herbert had 382 passing yards, three touchdowns, and an interception in a 41–37 win.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-64)

In a Week 13 matchup against the [Cincinnati Bengals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cincinnati_Bengals "Cincinnati Bengals"), Herbert had 317 passing yards, three passing touchdowns, and an interception in a 41–22 victory, earning him his second AFC Offensive Player of the Week berth of the season.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-65) He followed that performance with 275 passing yards, three passing touchdowns, and no interceptions in Week 14 against the [New York Giants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Giants "New York Giants"), lifting the Chargers to a 37–21 victory, and an 8–5 record. He earned his second consecutive, and third overall, AFC Offensive Player of the Week honor for his performance.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-66)

In Week 15, playing against the Chiefs, Herbert surpassed [Andrew Luck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Luck "Andrew Luck")'s record for the most passing yards in an NFL quarterback's first two seasons.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-67) Additionally, he surpassed [Dan Marino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Marino "Dan Marino")'s record for the most total touchdowns in an NFL quarterback's first two seasons.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-68) In a Week 18 win or tie or go home situation against the [Las Vegas Raiders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas_Raiders "Las Vegas Raiders"), Herbert threw for 383 yards, three touchdowns, and an interception in the [35–32 overtime loss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Los_Angeles_Chargers%E2%80%93Las_Vegas_Raiders_game "2021 Los Angeles Chargers–Las Vegas Raiders game"), eliminating the Chargers from the playoffs.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-69)

In the 2021 season, Herbert set franchise records with 5,014 passing yards, 38 passing touchdowns, and 15 interceptions.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-sspassing-70) In addition, he had 63 carries for 302 rushing yards and three rushing touchdowns, leading the Chargers to a 9–8 record and his first career [Pro Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pro_Bowl "Pro Bowl").[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-71)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-72) Herbert became the first quarterback in franchise history to throw for at least 5,000 yards in a single season.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-73) He was ranked 40th by his fellow players on the [NFL Top 100 Players of 2022](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_Top_100_Players_of_2022 "NFL Top 100 Players of 2022").[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-74)

In Week 1 against the [Las Vegas Raiders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas_Raiders "Las Vegas Raiders"), Herbert threw for 279 yards and three touchdowns in the 24–19 win.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-75) In Week 2 against the [Kansas City Chiefs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City_Chiefs "Kansas City Chiefs"), Herbert threw for 334 yards and three touchdowns for the second consecutive game. In the fourth quarter, Herbert suffered a fracture to his rib cartilage.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-76) Despite a late touchdown, the Chargers would go on to lose 27–24.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-77) In Week 6 against the [Denver Broncos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver_Broncos "Denver Broncos"), Herbert completed 37 of 57 passes for 238 yards, no touchdowns, and an interception in the 19–16 victory. His 57 passes were the most in a winning effort without a passing touchdown in NFL history.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-78) Overall, Herbert passed for 4,739 yards, 25 touchdowns, and ten interceptions in 17 games in the 2022 season.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-79) He set single-season franchise records for pass attempts and completions.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-sspassing-70) The Chargers finished with a 10–7 record and earned a playoff berth.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-80)

In his first playoff game, Herbert passed for 273 yards and a touchdown as the Chargers fell to the [Jacksonville Jaguars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacksonville_Jaguars "Jacksonville Jaguars") 31–30 in the [Wild Card Round](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_NFL_playoffs#AFC:_Jacksonville_Jaguars_31,_Los_Angeles_Chargers_30 "2022–23 NFL playoffs").[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-81) The Chargers surrendered a 27–0 lead for the third-largest blown lead in NFL playoff history.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-82)

After the season, he was ranked 32nd by his fellow players on the [NFL Top 100 Players of 2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_Top_100_Players_of_2023 "NFL Top 100 Players of 2023").[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-83)

### 2023

See also: [2023 Los Angeles Chargers season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Los_Angeles_Chargers_season "2023 Los Angeles Chargers season")

On April 28, 2023, the Chargers picked up the fifth-year option on Herbert's contract.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-84) On July 25, he signed a five-year extension worth $262.5 million, which extends through the 2029 season. At the time of the signing, the deal made Herbert the highest-paid player in NFL history (surpassing the previous record set by [Lamar Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lamar_Jackson "Lamar Jackson") just months earlier) and the highest-paid NFL quarterback based on average annual value at $52.5 million per season.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-85)[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-86) However, this record deal would be surpassed by Joe Burrow's extension just two months later.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-87)

After starting the season 0–2, Herbert had a fourth-quarter comeback against the [Minnesota Vikings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota_Vikings "Minnesota Vikings") in Week 3, resulting in a 28–24 win. This game also marked his first 400-yard passing performance in the NFL. In Week 14 against the [Denver Broncos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver_Broncos "Denver Broncos"), Herbert suffered a broken index finger on his throwing hand in the second quarter and was ruled out for the remainder of the game.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-88) On December 12, the Chargers announced Herbert would undergo surgery and was placed on [injured reserve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Injured_reserve "Injured reserve"), ending his season.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-89) He was ranked 75 by his fellow players on the [NFL Top 100 Players of 2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_Top_100_Players_of_2024 "NFL Top 100 Players of 2024").[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-90)

### 2024

See also: [2024 Los Angeles Chargers season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Los_Angeles_Chargers_season "2024 Los Angeles Chargers season")

Herbert entered his fifth NFL season with his third different head coach, as [Brandon Staley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandon_Staley "Brandon Staley") was replaced by [Jim Harbaugh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Harbaugh "Jim Harbaugh").[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-91) Herbert began the season with a 90-plus passer rating in his first ten games, the longest streak of starts with a 90-plus passer rating by any quarterback to begin a season since 2018.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-92) In Week 10 against the [Tennessee Titans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee_Titans "Tennessee Titans"), Herbert passed [David Carr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Carr_(American_football) "David Carr (American football)") for the most completions by a quarterback in their first five seasons.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-93) From Weeks 2 to 14, Herbert recorded 357 consecutive pass attempts without an interception, the fifth-longest such streak in NFL history.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-94) In a 40–7 victory against the [New England Patriots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_England_Patriots "New England Patriots") in Week 17, Herbert passed for 281 yards and three touchdowns to become the third player in NFL history with at least 3,000 passing yards and 20 touchdown passes in each of his first five seasons. The win also clinched a playoff berth for the Chargers, marking their second appearance in three seasons.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-95) He finished the regular season with 346 yards, two touchdowns, and no turnovers in a 34–20 win over the Raiders.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-96)

Herbert had an efficient year in his first season under Jim Harbaugh, finishing with 3,870 passing yards, 23 touchdowns, and just three interceptions, along with career highs in rushing yards.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-97) Herbert's 23:3 TD–INT ratio (7.67) ranks eighth all-time in NFL history among quarterbacks with at least 15 touchdown passes in a season. His numbers on [play-action](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Play-action_pass "Play-action pass") passes were among the best in the league, completing 74.7 percent for 1,617 yards with eight touchdowns and just two interceptions on such throws.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-98) Despite a productive regular season, Herbert had the worst game of his career in the [Wild Card Round](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024%E2%80%9325_NFL_playoffs#AFC:_Houston_Texans_32,_Los_Angeles_Chargers_12 "2024–25 NFL playoffs") against the [Houston Texans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_Texans "Houston Texans"), posting a career-low 43.8% completion percentage, one touchdown, and a career-high four interceptions for a career-low passer rating of 40.9 as the Chargers lost 32–12.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-99) He was ranked 56th by his fellow players on the [NFL Top 100 Players of 2025](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_Top_100_Players_of_2025 "NFL Top 100 Players of 2025").[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-100)

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c7/Justin_Herbert_with_Chargers_2025.jpg/250px-Justin_Herbert_with_Chargers_2025.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Justin_Herbert_with_Chargers_2025.jpg)

Herbert in 2025 passing the ball

Herbert and the Chargers opened the 2025 season playing in [São Paulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A3o_Paulo "São Paulo"), Brazil, against the [Kansas City Chiefs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Kansas_City_Chiefs_season "2025 Kansas City Chiefs season"). They won 27–21 with Herbert completing 25 out of 34 passes for 318 passing yards and 3 passing touchdowns.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-101) In Week 8 against the [Minnesota Vikings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Minnesota_Vikings_season "2025 Minnesota Vikings season"), Herbert passed [Peyton Manning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peyton_Manning "Peyton Manning") for the most completions by a quarterback in their first six seasons.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-102) On December 1, he underwent surgery to repair a fracture in his left hand, which he suffered in Week 14 against the [Philadelphia Eagles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Philadelphia_Eagles_season "2025 Philadelphia Eagles season").[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-103) On December 23, Herbert was named to his second career Pro Bowl.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-104) Playing behind an offensive line that lost starters [Joe Alt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Alt "Joe Alt") and [Rashawn Slater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rashawn_Slater "Rashawn Slater") to season-ending injuries, Herbert led the team to 11 wins while being pressured on a league-high 288 dropbacks.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-105) He ran for a career-high 498 yards. The Chargers lost their playoff opener 16–3 to the Patriots. "I didn't play well enough and didn't make any plays," Herbert said. He completed 19 of 31 passes for 159 yards with no touchdowns, was sacked six times, and lost a fumble, while leading the Chargers in rushing with 55 yards.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-106)[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-107)

## Personal life

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/eb/Madison_Beer_%26_Justin_Herbert_-_2025_Commanders_at_Chargers_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Madison_Beer_%26_Justin_Herbert_-_2025_Commanders_at_Chargers_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Madison_Beer_&_Justin_Herbert_-_2025_Commanders_at_Chargers_(cropped).jpg)

Herbert with fiancée and singer-songwriter [Madison Beer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madison_Beer "Madison Beer"), 2025

Herbert's maternal grandfather, Rich Schwab, played receiver at the [University of Oregon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Oregon "University of Oregon") in the 1960s.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-espn.com-24) His paternal grandfather, Roger Herbert, was a biology teacher at Sheldon High School and fueled Herbert’s interest in science.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-133) His father, Mark Herbert, played football and ran track at the [University of Montana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Montana "University of Montana").[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-134) Herbert was a [San Diego Chargers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego_Chargers "San Diego Chargers") fan growing up.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-135) Herbert's younger brother, [Patrick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Herbert_(American_football) "Patrick Herbert (American football)"), currently plays [tight end](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tight_end "Tight end") (also on the Chargers).[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-136) His older brother, Mitchell, played [wide receiver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wide_receiver "Wide receiver") at [Montana State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montana_State_University "Montana State University").[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-137) Herbert has been in a relationship with singer-songwriter [Madison Beer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madison_Beer "Madison Beer") since 2025.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-138) They announced their engagement on July 28, 2026.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-139)

### Chess

Herbert, after being beaten by Chargers teammate [Rashawn Slater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rashawn_Slater "Rashawn Slater") in [chess](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chess "Chess") during a road trip in 2024 to play the [Carolina Panthers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carolina_Panthers "Carolina Panthers"), decided to improve his play of the game over the next year, studying chess from various sources. He appeared with Swedish chess player, [Woman FIDE Master](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woman_FIDE_Master "Woman FIDE Master") and internet chess celebrity [Anna Cramling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anna_Cramling "Anna Cramling") in a video in 2025 to talk about his journey to improve his chess game.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-ChessSI-140)[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Herbert#cite_note-CramlingVideo-141)
